auto-6e05d6ab268b.headline: EU and UK urge Iran to halt Hormuz attacks and hybrid operations in Europe
auto-6e05d6ab268b.summary:
The European Union and Britain issued a joint statement after a Brussels summit condemning Iranian attacks on neighbouring states and on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. They demanded Tehran end its destabilising activity and what they called hybrid attacks on European soil, and reaffirmed that Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon. Leaders also signed a pledge rejecting any tolls or fees for passage through the strait and agreed closer cooperation against cyber and hybrid threats.

The statement follows Iran-linked incidents in Europe, including a French probe into a cyber attack on supermarket refrigeration systems and convictions in Britain for spying on Iran International journalists. A US official separately told the Jerusalem Post that Iran has increasingly used anti-ship cruise missiles against vessels, while oil traffic through the strait remained high.

Coordinated stance against Iran and expanded cooperation on hybrid and cyber threats

impact_points: Iran faces growing European pressure over Hormuz shipping attacks and alleged hybrid operations on European soil.

auto-93aac4acf220.headline: Drone strike sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
auto-93aac4acf220.summary:
A Russian cargo vessel, the Sparta II, was hit by drones in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday and caught fire. The ship later drifted into Finnish territorial waters, prompting a rescue operation for its crew. Finnish authorities said the vessel has links to Russia's armed forces but could not confirm whether military materiel was aboard. Finland's defence forces later said Ukraine likely carried out the strike, and Helsinki alerted NATO and imposed temporary air and sea restrictions in the area.

The ship was reportedly bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, and Kaliningrad's governor said supplies there were not at risk. A Russian helicopter also briefly entered Finnish airspace, possibly during rescue or tracking efforts.

impact_points: Finland faces spillover from the war, with its prime minister saying the conflict is reaching its immediate vicinity.

auto-e25fa229f972.headline: Iran vows countermeasures against US naval blockade as tankers gather at Kharg
auto-e25fa229f972.summary:
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi described the US economic blockade of Iran as a hostile act and an act of war, vowing to take any necessary steps to break it. He also said nuclear negotiations have not begun and that enriched material will not be exported under any circumstances. Satellite imagery and ship-tracking data reportedly show more than 14 tankers positioned at Kharg Island, which handles most of Iran's crude exports, possibly preparing a convoy toward the Gulf of Oman. Iranian-linked voices have warned that any attack on the tankers could bring strikes on Gulf oil facilities, while US officials have said they would target vessels involved in such transfers.

The moves come as Washington signals no urgency on Iran until next year, and oil prices have fallen for weeks as Gulf supplies recover. Some reports say the US is still hitting Iranian positions near the Strait of Hormuz, and Israel is reportedly urging a swift strike on Iran, a claim that could not be independently verified.

impact_points: Iran faces severe financial pressure as loadings at Kharg Island remain halted under the blockade.

auto-dbc99093b3c2.headline: Antalya climate talks stall over fossil fuels and adaptation finance
auto-dbc99093b3c2.summary: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ran past the scheduled end date as they struggled to agree on fossil fuels and finance for poorer countries adapting to climate change. A draft text dropped earlier references to phasing out fossil fuels and a proposed $120 billion adaptation finance target, reportedly after opposition from Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers. The EU climate commissioner said the outcome would either be a good deal or no deal, while Turkey's COP31 president urged countries to act responsibly. The United States is absent for a second year.

impact_points: The EU and developing nations such as Gambia and Malawi face a weaker outcome if divisions persist.

auto-86a1d7bc17be.headline: Russian strikes injure nine across Sumy Oblast, police report
auto-86a1d7bc17be.summary:
Ukrainian police in Sumy Oblast say nine people were hurt in Russian attacks over the past day, with Russian forces reportedly hitting 22 settlements in the region. Injuries were reported in the Krolevets and Seredyna-Buda hromadas and in Hlukhiv, mostly from drone strikes. The attacks came as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian forces had hit a railway station in Sumy Oblast on the morning of 21 November.

The reporting describes the strikes as part of a wider pattern, with separate Russian attacks reported the same period in Kryvyi Rih and other oblasts. Russia's government has not commented in the coverage provided.

auto-a9e2d95dee7a.headline: UN climate summit in Antalya collapses without consensus after EU rejects draft
auto-a9e2d95dee7a.summary:
UN climate talks hosted by Turkey in Antalya ended without an agreed deal on Sunday, after the European Union and several other countries rejected the final draft. COP31 presidents Turkey and Australia had drafted the text, which acknowledged that global warming is on course to pass 1.5 degrees Celsius but omitted explicit mention of fossil fuels. Turkish COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing session that no consensus existed and the decisions were not adopted.

EU officials, through Ireland's environment minister Darragh O'Brien, said the bloc would not endorse a text that fails to mention fossil fuels, the main driver of climate change. Panama and Antigua and Barbuda also voiced objections, while Saudi Arabia and other oil producers were reported to have pushed to keep fossil fuels out of the text.

auto-199392b2640a.headline: Drone strikes damage homes and UN premises in Khartoum
auto-199392b2640a.summary:
Drones struck residential areas of Khartoum early on Sunday, damaging homes and a United Nations building, according to witnesses and the UN. Explosions were heard around the airport and other parts of the city between about 2 and 4:30 a.m. local time. One witness said a house was completely destroyed and people were digging through rubble for trapped relatives. A separate strike reportedly hit a mosque caller's home in Jebel Aulia, south of the capital. The UN humanitarian office condemned the danger to its staff, calling it unacceptable. A Sudanese army source claimed the drones were launched from Ethiopia, an accusation Addis Ababa denies. No casualty figures were immediately released.

The conflict between the army and the Rapid Support Forces, which began in April 2023, has killed over 200,000 people according to aid workers estimates. The UN says drone strikes killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

impact_points: Ethiopia faces accusations from Sudan's army that its territory was used to launch the drone attacks.

auto-fb1aa79ac0d6.headline: Blast aboard Russian vessel in Benghazi port blamed on suspected drone strike
auto-fb1aa79ac0d6.summary:
An explosion struck a Russian ship docked at the naval base port in Benghazi, eastern Libya, at dawn on Sunday. Libya's eastern-based government said a preliminary probe pointed to a suspected drone attack, and satellite images showed the vessel on fire and later partly submerged. The ship had stopped to refuel and resupply on its way back to Russia under a maritime agreement. Reports differ on casualties: the eastern authorities said no one was killed, while medical sources cited injuries of unknown number. Moscow had not commented and no group has claimed the attack.

The eastern government condemned the strike as a breach of Libya's sovereignty and said it is coordinating with Russia to identify those responsible. Separately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli warned against hosting foreign forces or letting them use civilian facilities.

Suspected attacker per earlier Russian accusations, not confirmed in this incident

impact_points: Russia faces a damaged vessel and an unresolved question over who attacked it in Libya.

auto-36849c16f2a2.headline: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill several Palestinians despite October ceasefire
auto-36849c16f2a2.summary:
Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip killed several Palestinians and wounded others on Sunday, according to Palestinian and aid-related reports. A drone strike near Deir al-Balah in central Gaza killed one man, while Israeli army fire in Khan Younis reportedly wounded a child. Earlier, a drone strike on a van delivering food aid in Gaza City killed three people, though the aid group named in witness accounts said the vehicle was not linked to it.

Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025. Winter flooding is worsening the humanitarian situation, and aid groups report restrictions on delivering shelter materials into the enclave.

impact_points: Palestinian civilians in Gaza face continued lethal fire despite the October 2025 ceasefire, with aid distribution also targeted.

auto-8555c80fcb92.headline: Russian drone strike on Kyiv region apartment block leaves dozens dead or missing
auto-8555c80fcb92.summary: A Russian drone attack early on a Sunday morning hit a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, a town in the Kyiv region of Ukraine, destroying part of the structure and starting a fire. Regional officials said at least 11 people were killed and six injured, with others still trapped under the rubble. Rescue work was repeatedly halted by new air raid alerts and drone warnings, though a young boy was pulled out alive after nearly 14 hours. Russia launched a wider overnight barrage of hundreds of drones and over 100 missiles across Ukraine.

auto-66232f8479a7.headline: Report warns Gaza war has left widespread toxic contamination for decades
auto-66232f8479a7.summary:
A report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory says Israel's military campaign in Gaza has contaminated air, soil and water across the entire strip. The authors cite heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings and raw sewage as threats to public health, with children and pregnant women most at risk.

The UN Environment Programme estimates the fighting has produced more than 61 million tonnes of debris, which the report describes as a large store of hazardous material. The authors say clean-up will be difficult because unexploded ordnance limits access, and they call on Israel to allow an on-the-ground environmental assessment. Israel has rejected the findings from UN inquiry bodies that accused it of genocide.

impact_points: Palestinians in Gaza face long-term exposure to toxins through air, food, water and contaminated debris.

auto-94a2d65f7a13.headline: German media report NATO intelligence sees Russian nuclear satellite launch planned
auto-94a2d65f7a13.summary:
German broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung reported that NATO members' intelligence services believe Russia plans to put a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit this year. The satellite, called Sputnik-S, is said to have been assembled several years ago and kept in the Moscow region, according to Western intelligence shared among allies, including Germany's BND.

Russia denied similar claims from US officials in 2024 that it was building a space-based nuclear weapon able to destroy satellite networks such as SpaceX's Starlink, which Ukrainian forces use. Russia's embassy in Germany, the BND and NATO did not immediately comment, and the reporting could not be independently verified.

auto-8715c345a820.headline: Israeli spokeswoman's school visit in occupied south Lebanon draws Beirut's condemnation
auto-8715c345a820.summary: An Israeli military spokeswoman posted a video of herself at a school in Debel, a Christian village in the Israeli-occupied border zone of southern Lebanon, on Lebanon's Independence Day. The footage showed her in front of a classroom of children. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and Education Minister Rima Karami condemned the visit, with Salam saying an occupying power has no right to use Lebanese children for propaganda. Debel's municipality said the visit happened about a month earlier without coordination with the school. The Israeli military said it is reviewing whether the officer had the required approvals to publish the content.

auto-fe57fa332ac7.headline: Israeli strike in Gaza kills UNRWA-linked worker near water well
auto-fe57fa332ac7.summary:
An Israeli airstrike in the Gaza Strip killed a man working for UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, on Monday, the agency and local health officials said. Medics named him as Adel Al-Helo. He was working near a water well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the north of the enclave, and three others were wounded. UNRWA said the strike hit a street target near the well, which was staffed by agency workers and a guard, while they were carrying out routine water operations.

The strike comes amid continued Israeli attacks in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire, which halted major fighting without ending military operations. Israeli forces now control or restrict access to about two-thirds of the territory.

auto-82a933daf53c.headline: German reports say Russia may orbit a nuclear-armed satellite; Moscow denies
auto-82a933daf53c.summary:
German outlets reported, citing Western intelligence assessments, that Russia could launch a satellite carrying a nuclear weapon into orbit within weeks or months. The satellite, called Sputnik-S, is said to be fully assembled and stored near Moscow, with warnings suggesting launch within 60 days. Berlin says it is taking the reports very seriously, but the claims could not be independently verified.

The Kremlin said it had not seen the reports and dismissed them as hardly worth taking seriously, while Russia's embassy in Berlin called them unfounded propaganda and said its space activities serve only peaceful purposes. Any such deployment would breach the 1967 Outer Space Treaty and the 1963 Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.

auto-91d664c90197.headline: EU unveils 22nd Russia sanctions package targeting banks, veterans and sport
auto-91d664c90197.summary:
The European Commission has proposed the bloc's 22nd sanctions package against Russia, announced by President Ursula von der Leyen on Monday. It would cut around 60 more Russian banks from the SWIFT payment system, target crypto and payment networks, and add more than 70 vessels from Russia's shadow fleet to the blacklist. It would also bar European firms from repairing damaged Russian energy facilities such as refineries, and bar Russian teams and athletes from competing in the EU.

A visa ban on former Russian combatants is also proposed, which von der Leyen linked to a recent rise in covert Russian operations in Europe. EU member states will now negotiate the package, with diplomats aiming for agreement by year's end. Von der Leyen said Moscow should be given reason to pursue peace.

auto-01c43a1d6c41.headline: Houthis report 17 killed in Saudi strike on Hodeidah telecoms site
auto-01c43a1d6c41.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement says Saudi-led coalition air strikes hit a telecommunications facility in Hodeidah governorate on the Red Sea coast on Monday. The Houthis' telecoms ministry says 17 workers were killed, 11 wounded, and administrative buildings, staff housing and a mosque destroyed, disrupting phone and internet service. These casualty and damage figures come from the Houthi side and could not be independently confirmed. The strike comes amid renewed fighting that resumed in July alongside the wider US-Israeli war on Iran.

The same week, the Houthis also claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery, which the coalition said it intercepted a missile aimed at, while a Houthi military spokesman put the total number of Saudi-led air and missile attacks on Yemen at 5,581 since the escalation began.

auto-b0d26115b6f6.headline: Israeli opposition leader sees no urgent case for striking Iran
auto-b0d26115b6f6.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot, the Israeli opposition leader tasked with forming the next government, said on Monday he sees no direct and immediate threat from Iran that would require military action before a government is in place. He described Iran as the gravest threat facing Israel, but said intervention was not needed at this stage.

His comments contrasted with caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who warned against downplaying grave threats and has pressed to resume the war with Iran. The remarks came as Eisenkot's and Netanyahu's parties prepared for a third round of coalition talks, which have so far produced no breakthrough.

auto-44dcd2eab020.headline: Finland summons Russian envoy over helicopter incursion and drone-hit ship
auto-44dcd2eab020.summary:
Finland has summoned Russia's ambassador after a Russian helicopter was suspected of entering its airspace, reaching about 4 kilometres inland near Loviisa. The move follows a Ukrainian drone strike on the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, which caused a fire and forced crew evacuation. Finland's foreign ministry also condemned Russia's escalating strikes on civilian targets in Ukraine and called Moscow's actions in Europe unacceptable.

Finland's defence minister linked the suspected violation to rescue or monitoring work around the damaged ship, which was later towed to Russia. Moldova and Poland reported separate Russian airspace incidents in the same period.

auto-265278a1b36c.headline: US weighs small demining training mission with Syrian military
auto-265278a1b36c.summary:
The United States is considering a multinational programme to train Syrian soldiers in demining and explosive ordnance disposal, according to five people familiar with the plan. It would be Washington's first training mission with Syria's military since former rebel fighters took power in Damascus in 2024, and could bring a small number of US troops back as early as next year.

The plan still faces obstacles. US law bars aid to security units with credible evidence of gross rights abuses, and some Syrian defence officials are reluctant to give American personnel access. Reuters could not verify reported funding of about $200 million from remaining Operation Inherent Resolve money. Participation could extend to around 15 allies, including Britain, France, Germany, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

auto-62e954c55d60.headline: Russia launches over 150 drones at Ukraine; most downed, others hit sites
auto-62e954c55d60.summary:
Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 153 attack drones, including 60 jet-powered Shaheds, plus decoys, overnight into 23 November. Early figures put 134 drones destroyed or jammed by air defences, with hits recorded at 11 sites and debris falling at seven. Separately, Ukrainian drones struck Russian oil infrastructure overnight, including a refinery in Perm Krai, a pumping station in Tatarstan and a fuel plant in Rostov. Russian authorities reported one death in Perm Krai.

The Kyiv Independent reports that Ukraine has shifted recent long-range strikes toward airfields and missile-supply plants, after a pause in refinery attacks under US pressure. The pressure followed a claimed energy ceasefire in October.

auto-425488c461e1.summary:
Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, is scheduled to meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington on Monday. The talks are expected to focus on Doha's mediation between Washington and Tehran, aimed at restoring a ceasefire in the US-Israeli war on Iran and reopening nuclear negotiations.

Iran has said it remains in contact with Qatar and other mediators, and a Qatari delegation visited Tehran recently. Iranian officials played down the trip as routine, while Tehran warned it would counter a US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz by all available means.

auto-88275413b446.headline: US sanctions dozens tied to Iran's shadow banking network
auto-88275413b446.summary:
The US Treasury Department on Monday imposed new sanctions on dozens of people and entities it says support Iran's shadow banking system. The targets include Iranian citizens and roughly two dozen exchange houses and front companies based in the United Arab Emirates, Turkey and Hong Kong. Treasury said these networks, overseen by Iran's central bank, keep Iran's foreign trade moving despite sanctions.

A separate Treasury analysis estimated nearly $15 billion in potentially linked financial activity from January 2025 to August 2026, and found a decline over the period that it said may point to partial disruption. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described the network as the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime.

Estonia had linked the decision to an alleged attempted arson attack on a defence company, which Moscow denies. Three more people died in a supermarket attack in Vyshneve and a strike on a home in Bila Tserkva, and a power substation in Dnipropetrovsk was also hit as temperatures fell.

Ukraine said its forces sank the Russian corvette Merkury and a cargo ship off Libya, and drones struck oil facilities in Tatarstan and Rostov in Russia. Separately, an exiled analysis of leaked Rosstat records estimates at least 490,000 Russian troops have been killed in the invasion.

auto-cdf361f6bd25.headline: Merz says denying Ukraine a NATO path in 2008 was an error
auto-cdf361f6bd25.summary:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said at a Berlin press conference with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that the alliance was wrong not to back a 2008 US proposal to give Ukraine a Membership Action Plan. He argued the war might have been prevented had Ukraine joined then. Merz also backed French President Emmanuel Macron's call to reopen the question of Ukraine's NATO membership, describing security guarantees similar to NATO's Article 5 as very close to membership.

Rutte was more cautious, saying successful peace talks must come first and that there is no unanimous agreement among the 32 allies on Ukraine's accession. auto-74917a18055d.headline: Israeli coalition talks stall as Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties fail to agree

auto-0727975ba655.headline: Court allows army to detonate degraded explosive material at Iowa plant
auto-0727975ba655.summary:
A federal appeals court has allowed the US Army to proceed with detonating roughly 9,500 pounds of degraded lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The material sits in 68 barrels, and officials warned the explosion could scatter toxic lead dust up to 100 miles northeast, reaching towns including Wapello and New Boston, Illinois. The move followed a presidential post in which Donald Trump paused the plan and made it subject to the approval of incoming Iowa governor Rob Sand.

The army had moved the date several times after public concern about health and environmental effects. Environmental groups challenged the emergency approach, arguing the EPA skipped required permitting steps, and the court placed a temporary stay while it reviewed the request. Officials had not said who carried out the attack. Another police station in the Cesar region was hit by drones the same day, injuring an officer. The attacks follow a government offensive against rebel groups and drug gangs, which armed groups have answered with drone, rocket and bomb attacks on military and police targets.

auto-2c21a12c8963.summary:

The Justice Department says the army will act by November 24 under an emergency exemption, arguing that falling temperatures could trigger an uncontrolled explosion. The explosives, stored in 68 barrels for over two decades, have partly dried out and formed crystals, raising the risk of accidental detonation. auto-d95141adf58c.summary:

Air traffic controllers at Skeyes, the country's air traffic control company, said they could not safely guarantee regular services between 07:00 and 21:00 local time, so flights at Brussels, Charleroi and other airports were largely cancelled, affecting more than 50,000 passengers at Brussels alone. auto-ad424e18210d.headline: NATO sends early-warning aircraft to Poland after Russian missiles hit

NATO has approved sending an Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft to Poland after three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles landed in southeast Poland last Friday. Poland's deputy defence minister said the aircraft would give Warsaw sharper situational awareness, and NATO confirmed the forward deployment.

auto-283fd3cdbfc3.summary:
Ukraine says it is short of Patriot interceptors, which are US-made and needed to counter ballistic missiles. A Pentagon spokesperson said US policy has not changed, while Zelensky called the delays hard to understand as Russia launched around 165 missiles and about 2,700 drones in a single week.

auto-fa4aec5cea1a.headline: Iranian lawmaker warns future war would reshape oil markets and regional balance
auto-fa4aec5cea1a.summary:
Abbas Golrou, who heads the foreign relations committee of Iran's parliament, warned in an interview with Mehr News that any future war with Iran would not resemble earlier conflicts. auto-58f1324b0ca5.headline: US envoy doubts Trump's pledge to end Israel military aid this year
auto-58f1324b0ca5.summary:
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has questioned whether Washington will halt its $3.8 billion in yearly military aid to Israel by the end of 2026, as President Trump promised on Election Day in November. Trump said he had struck a deal with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu months earlier to end the funding, but gave no details on how it would stop. Huckabee said the existing agreement runs until 2028 and that Congress had already allocated the funds, so he was unsure it could end without congressional approval. He also said US and Israeli officials had been negotiating a new agreement for months.

The comments come as US support for Israel has eroded, especially among Democrats, who now control both houses of Congress. auto-e5b4aefb609f.headline: Landmine casualties worldwide reach five-year high, led by Myanmar and Syria
auto-e5b4aefb609f.summary:
Landmine and unexploded ordnance casualties reached a five-year high in 2025, according to an annual report from the International Campaign to Ban Landmines. The group recorded 6,929 casualties, with civilians making up about 84 percent and children around half of those. Myanmar recorded 1,891 casualties, the highest of any country for a third straight year, as mines are used by both the military and armed opposition groups.

Syria saw casualties rise by more than 50 percent to 1,602 as displaced people returned after the fall of the Assad government. The report also noted new mine use by North Korea and Iran, and said the United States reportedly deployed mines in Iran, which Washington has not addressed. Several countries near Russia, including Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland, withdrew from the 1997 Mine Ban Treaty.

auto-55bfd286154c.summary:
Suspected sea drones struck a Russian Navy corvette moored at Benghazi port in eastern Libya at dawn, causing an explosion, fire and sinking, with reported casualties among Libyan and Russian nationals. The eastern Libyan government said the ship had docked to refuel under a Russia cooperation agreement, and it has asked for a joint investigation with Moscow and a UN probe. Separately, a Ukrainian drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, which Finland's border guard said caused a fire; Finland has since reported a suspected Russian helicopter airspace violation.

auto-d570b1b46b75.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered federal authorities to take over all border crossings in the Kurdistan region and to manage oilfields in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahuddin and Nineveh provinces. auto-4e6078400f20.summary: Japan will make its full 2027 contribution to the International Criminal Court by the end of 2026, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on November 24, 2026. auto-f1cd4d477414.summary:

auto-ce02ab6a3244.summary:

Risks remain: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, and US-Iran talks have not moved forward. The US is also reportedly investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers.

Elsewhere, Libya reopened its Sharara pipeline after an armed group had shut a valve, and Deutsche Bank estimated global inventories rose by 52 million barrels in October. auto-d2a4a42b9b37.headline: Norway and Ukraine plan wider rollout of joint anti-drone air defence
auto-d2a4a42b9b37.summary:
Norway and Ukraine have agreed to broaden their work on an anti-drone air defence system called DESNA, the Norwegian defence ministry said. The system is built by Norway's Kongsberg together with a Ukrainian partner, pairing Ukrainian-made missiles and launchers with Kongsberg control systems Norway donated. It is already in service, and the ministry said it will be deployed in more parts of Ukraine, without giving details. The move comes as Russian forces have carried out near-constant air attacks on Kyiv and other cities since September.

In the same period, a strike on a central district of Kyiv injured five people on Monday, and an attack on a town in the surrounding region killed 11 on Sunday.

actors.why: Gains a wider deployment of anti-drone defences amid ongoing Russian air attacks
Deepens defence cooperation and Kongsberg's role supplying Ukraine
Faces a strengthened Ukrainian air defence against its ongoing aerial strikes

impact_points: Ukraine gains expanded access to an air defence system against drone attacks on its cities.
Norway and Kongsberg extend their defence industrial partnership and role in supporting Ukraine's protection.

auto-e893b322b5ee.headline: South Korea names new foreign, unification and spy chiefs as US ties stay under strain
auto-e893b322b5ee.summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Monday nominated Lim Woong-soon as foreign minister, Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister and Kang Kum-sil as head of the National Intelligence Service. The nominees still need parliamentary hearings, though no confirmation vote is required. The changes follow friction with Washington over intelligence sharing after a March disclosure about a North Korean uranium enrichment site. The U.S. State Department said it values close alliance cooperation and referred questions on the cabinet to Seoul.

Seoul says its core policy lines toward the United States and North Korea will stay the same. Reports say the NIS was left out of a June trilateral meeting on North Korean cyber threats, though it maintains intelligence sharing with Washington remains active.

actors.why: New leaders must repair alliance ties and manage North Korea policy amid tensions
Seeks to preserve alliance cooperation, though intelligence sharing was partly restricted
Inter-Korean ties remain deadlocked, with tensions simmering along the border

impact_points: South Korea must rebuild intelligence trust with Washington after partial restrictions on sensitive North Korean intelligence.
The United States faces continued uncertainty over intelligence cooperation with its key Northeast Asian ally until new officials are confirmed.

auto-db4218dbb8a9.headline: Settler attacks torch vehicles and daub graffiti in West Bank villages
auto-db4218dbb8a9.summary:
Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank overnight, setting vehicles on fire and spraying racist slogans on homes, including in Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik. Residents said the assailants arrived from a nearby settler outpost while families were asleep, and one said his household narrowly avoided being caught in a blaze.

Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemned the violence as "Jewish terrorism" and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for encouraging it. Reports on casualties were not detailed in the coverage reviewed.

actors.why: Villages attacked, vehicles burned, homes daubed, residents left fearful
Settler violence condemned domestically, with pressure on far-right ministers

impact_points: Palestinian residents in Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik face destroyed vehicles, fear and property damage.
Israel faces domestic condemnation over settler violence and scrutiny of far-right ministers' role.

auto-0cb3562802ff.headline: Leaked Rosstat data points to at least 490,000 Russian military deaths in Ukraine
auto-0cb3562802ff.summary:
A hack of Russia's federal statistics agency Rosstat, carried out by the Belarusian group Cyber Partisans and the hacking group Silent Crow, has reportedly exposed records indicating at least 490,000 Russian military deaths in Ukraine since February 2022. Independent outlets including Meduza and Mediazona estimate that adding missing servicemen could push the total above 700,000. The Kremlin does not publish such figures, and the leaked data could not be independently verified.

Ukraine's General Staff, whose numbers are unverified, reports a total of about 1.64 million Russian losses including wounded, while a Economist study put Russian deaths between 374,000 and 770,000. The Kremlin has not commented on the leak, and Russian authorities have restricted access to official databases.

actors.why: Leak exposes heavy military deaths and suppressed official casualty figures
Ukrainian sources report heavy Russian losses, strengthening its position
Belarusian activists carried out the hack, linking Minsk-based opposition to the leak

impact_points: Russia faces major military and social strain, with deaths concentrated in its Far East and Siberia.
Ukraine gains an external assessment of Russian casualties, though the figures remain unverified and contested.

auto-9a3f01fc92c2.headline: Drone strikes on Khartoum and Omdurman damage homes and UN premises
auto-9a3f01fc92c2.summary:
Drone strikes early on Sunday hit residential areas of Khartoum and Omdurman in Sudan, killing at least four civilians and damaging a United Nations building while staff were inside, though no UN staff were hurt. Sudan's army blamed Ethiopia, alleging the drones were launched from Bahir Dar airport; Addis Ababa has denied allowing such attacks. The Rapid Support Forces are blamed for other strikes, and diplomats and the UN have condemned the attacks.

The UN humanitarian office and several ambassadors, including Germany's envoy and the EU delegation, called for civilians and aid workers to be protected. Drone warfare has caused more than 1,100 deaths in the first half of 2026, and the UN says food prices and funding shortfalls are worsening conditions.

actors.why: Civilians killed and homes and UN premises hit by drone strikes
Accused by Sudan's army of launching drones; Addis Ababa denies it
Delegation joined condemnation and urged protection of humanitarian workers
Germany's ambassador voiced solidarity with civilians and UN staff

impact_points: Sudan's civilians face continued drone deaths, displacement and worsening food insecurity amid rising prices.
Ethiopia faces accusations from the Sudanese army that it allowed drones to launch from its territory, which it denies.

auto-e1f2e7c1b9bf.headline: Polish investigators confirm three Russian cruise missiles entered its airspace
auto-e1f2e7c1b9bf.summary: Polish prosecutors say debris from three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles was recovered at sites in eastern Poland, one more than first reported. The missiles entered Polish airspace on 20 November during a large overnight Russian strike on Ukraine. Investigators in Lublin say early findings point to manufacture at a plant in Dubna, Moscow Oblast. Probes at two sites are complete, while the Mołodycz inquiry is due to finish on 23 November. NATO's North Atlantic Council is set to meet in Brussels to discuss the incursion.

actors.why: Missiles fell on Polish soil, violating airspace and raising security concerns
Its missiles entered NATO airspace, drawing condemnation and diplomatic pressure
Russia's mass strike on Ukraine caused the incursion; Kyiv gains support for its cause
European leaders condemn the incident and face pressure over shared security

impact_points: Poland faces a direct airspace violation and new security concerns after the missiles fell on its territory.
Russia faces growing international condemnation and pressure as NATO and European leaders respond to the incursion.

auto-fedba1989b17.headline: UK warns defence suppliers to Ukraine of rising Russian sabotage risk
auto-fedba1989b17.summary:
Britain's security services have warned firms that supply Ukraine's military that Russia is stepping up sabotage against them, including arson carried out through proxies. After a closed-door briefing with defence industry leaders, the National Protective Security Authority and the Ministry of Defence issued a joint alert with protective guidance. Companies are urged to limit publicly available information about their sites, weapons and staff, vary predictable routines, and report suspicious activity.

The alert follows a wave of sabotage attempts and security incidents across Europe in recent months. Separate briefings were scheduled for defence and critical infrastructure chief executives. Officials said the threat comes from Russian state-directed activity, and a British man was previously charged over an alleged plot tied to Russian military intelligence.

actors.why: Defence firms must bolster security against Russian-backed sabotage threats
Accused of using proxies for sabotage to undermine support for Ukraine
Western supply chains supporting its armed forces face disruption risks
Sabotage attempts against defence facilities across Europe are rising

impact_points: UK defence firms supplying Ukraine face heightened risk of arson and sabotage, and must improve their security.
Russia is accused of using proxies to undermine Western support for Ukraine, a threat that extends across European defence sites.

auto-4db72f66d116.headline: Britain sanctions Houthi group and four officials over abuses and attacks
auto-4db72f66d116.summary:
The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions on Yemen's Houthi movement and four senior figures in its administration. London accuses the group of attacks on shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb strait and strikes on Saudi civilian infrastructure, and says four officials were involved in torture, sexual violence and other abuse of detainees. The sanctioned individuals face asset freezes and travel bans. The measures follow a renewed flare-up in Yemen's conflict after a 2022 ceasefire broke down.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the sanctions were aimed at holding the group to account. The UK also said the Houthi campaign has driven up costs for British families, and reiterated support for Saudi Arabia and Yemen's recognised government.

actors.why: Imposes sanctions to pressure Houthis, citing shipping and cost-of-living concerns
Four senior officials sanctioned and renewed conflict deepens national crisis
Targeted by Houthi strikes; gains explicit UK solidarity and support
Houthis described as Iran-backed, so Tehran faces indirect pressure

impact_points: Houthi leadership and officials face asset freezes and travel bans, adding diplomatic and financial pressure on the group.
Saudi Arabia, targeted by Houthi rocket and drone strikes, gains explicit British backing against the attacks.

auto-3c3be9093c2d.headline: UN climate talks in Turkey end without deal over fossil fuels and finance
auto-3c3be9093c2d.summary: The UN COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, closed without an agreement after the longest such conference on record. Negotiations ran past their Friday deadline into Sunday, but the final draft did not mention fossil fuels directly and offered no concrete new financing for poorer nations facing climate impacts. The European Union and Pacific island states rejected the text, while Saudi Arabia and Russia pushed back against stronger language on coal, oil and gas. It is the first failure of this kind since the 2009 Copenhagen talks.

Co-hosted and led negotiations, with its president blaming geopolitical tensions for the collapse
Rejected the draft as lacking ambition, leaving its climate push unrealised
Opposed fossil fuel language, keeping oil producers' position intact
Warned against rapid fossil fuel phase-out, preserving its energy-sector stance
Called the failure disappointing but reaffirmed its climate commitment

impact_points: The European Union and Pacific island nations are left without the strengthened climate commitments they sought.
Poorer countries seeking climate adaptation money gain no clear new financing figures, leaving them exposed to rising temperatures.

auto-1017b56ef179.headline: US Army clears path to detonate toxic lead azide stockpile in Iowa
auto-1017b56ef179.summary: The US Army says it will go ahead on Wednesday with a controlled detonation of about 4,500kg of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The move follows an appeals court decision that lifted its earlier stay on the Environmental Protection Agency permit, after President Trump had ordered a pause. Environmental groups and Iowa's incoming governor have raised concerns about a possible toxic lead dust plume and called for more transparency, while federal officials argue an uncontrolled blast is the greater risk.

actors.why: Army proceeds with detonation after court clearance, facing legal and public criticism

impact_points: Residents and farmers near Middletown face possible lead dust exposure, with officials advising evacuation and livestock relocation.
The Iowa government and environmental groups are pressing for disclosure as the federal administration pushes the detonation forward.

auto-51496a45dd70.headline: Iran says mine disabled cargo ship using unauthorised Hormuz route
auto-51496a45dd70.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy said a cargo vessel hit a naval mine and was disabled on Tuesday in the southern Strait of Hormuz. Tehran said the ship had switched off its tracking systems and was trying to pass through an unauthorised route north of Khasab Port, which it described as a fabricated lane, with support from US military aircraft. The blast caused a major fire that halted the vessel. The Guard warned commercial operators to use approved routes and follow official instructions.

The incident comes amid a sharp rise in reported attacks on shipping around the Strait since the Iran war began in February. Maritime data cited by the Jerusalem Post counted over 30 incidents in October and at least 22 in November so far, though monitors say the true figure is likely higher because many ships are not reporting attacks. Iran's account of the mine strike could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Guard asserts control of the strait, but faces US blockade and economic strain
Reportedly aided the vessel's passage, amid a blockade of Iranian exports
Coastal neighbour near the Strait, exposed to shipping disruption and attacks
Major buyer of Iranian oil, whose supply is being cut off by the blockade

impact_points: Shipping operators in the Strait face mounting danger as attacks and mines rise sharply.
Iran's oil exports are already under US blockade, and Tehran faces further economic strain.

auto-65659e5a8cd2.headline: Turkish air force helicopter crashes in northwest Turkey, all five aboard killed
auto-65659e5a8cd2.summary: A Turkish air force helicopter crashed in the northwest of the country on Tuesday while on a training flight from Eskisehir province. The Turkish Defense Ministry said all five service members on board died. Search and rescue teams reached the crash site and located the wreckage of the AS-532 aircraft. The incident is the second military helicopter loss in Turkey in less than two weeks, following a crash in Malatya province on November 12 that killed four service members. The ministry said it was still investigating the cause of that earlier accident.

actors.why: Five service members killed and a second helicopter loss in two weeks

impact_points: Turkey's armed forces suffer a second helicopter loss in under two weeks, with nine personnel dead.
Turkish military aviation faces scrutiny over its safety record as investigations into both crashes continue.

auto-a4e389b26862.headline: Putin warns of retaliation over Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries
auto-a4e389b26862.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Ukraine is continuing to strike Russian oil refineries even after a direct request from US President Donald Trump to stop. Speaking at a Kremlin meeting with officials and oil executives, he said Moscow's response was unavoidable and asked for stronger protection of energy sites. Industry sources estimate Ukrainian drone attacks have cut refinery crude processing by about 45% since late October, and some Russian regions have restricted fuel sales. Kyiv has said it will halt strikes on Russian energy only if Moscow does the same.

Putin also said Europe's attempts to curb Russian energy exports had backfired, pointing to new markets and Arctic shipping routes. The European Union plans to end purchases of Russian seaborne LNG from January 1.

actors.why: Ukraine faces threatened Russian retaliation while continuing refinery strikes despite US request.
Refinery output cut about 45% and fuel sales restricted in several regions.
Trump's request to halt strikes was publicly ignored, weakening his mediation influence.
Ending Russian seaborne LNG purchases from January 1, though Russian supplies still rose this year.

impact_points: Ukraine faces possible Russian retaliation as Moscow vows action over refinery strikes.
Russia faces fuel shortages and sales limits as refinery output drops sharply after drone attacks.

auto-da60b3452264.headline: Iran vows to break US naval blockade of its oil exports
auto-da60b3452264.summary:
Iran has pledged to break the naval blockade the United States reimposed on its oil exports in July. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on X that Iran and its armed forces are determined to end the blockade and respond with full force to any new aggression. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said at a weekly briefing that Iran would use all its tools to confront the measure, which Tehran calls military aggression.

Iran says it controls passage through the Strait of Hormuz and will reopen it only if Washington halts hostilities, lifts the blockade and waives sanctions. Visible Iranian crude exports have fallen to near zero, and a report of a tanker loading Iranian crude by ship-to-ship transfer was called speculation by Baghaei.

Blockade pressure faces Iranian threats to respond and Hormuz reopening conditions

impact_points: Iran faces near-zero visible crude exports and pressure from the renewed American naval blockade.
The United States faces an Iranian pledge to resist its blockade and conditions tied to reopening Hormuz.

auto-0fb311cc9bac.headline: Israeli minister alleges Iran is pursuing chemical weapons, vows to block them
auto-0fb311cc9bac.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that Iran is developing chemical weapons and that Israel will not allow Tehran to acquire that capability. Speaking to Israeli reporters, he said Iran began this work after the joint Israeli-American military operation launched on February 28, which ended in an April ceasefire. Katz also floated the possibility of a pre-emptive strike if Israel judged an Iranian attack imminent. Iran's foreign minister dismissed a separate US report about an Iranian dirty bomb plot as propaganda. Katz's claims could not be independently verified in these reports.

Accused of chemical weapons development and faces possible Israeli strike
Joint operation partner; pressure to decide on any strike on Iran

impact_points: Iran faces Israeli threats of pre-emptive military action over alleged chemical weapons development.
Israel's political leaders are divided on whether urgent military action against Iran is needed now.

auto-2fcb230f3106.headline: Houthi strike on Riyadh financial tower wounds 11, second attack in a week
auto-2fcb230f3106.summary:
A strike hit a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Tuesday, wounding 11 people, according to Saudi civil defence. Witnesses told AFP the building was the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund. The Saudi-led coalition called the attack a terrorist act and blamed Yemen's Houthi group, which has not publicly claimed it. Those hurt included Saudi, Indian, Nepali and Egyptian nationals.

The attack is the second on the district in under a week, following a November 8 strike on an Aramco office building. Riyadh's airport has seen most international flights cancelled, and major events were postponed. Yemen's civil war has reignited since July.

Four Egyptian nationals wounded in the Riyadh attack

auto-ef700eef3628.headline: Houthi strike wounds 11 at Riyadh's PIF tower, second hit in days
auto-ef700eef3628.summary:
Yemen's Houthi forces struck the PIF tower in Riyadh's financial district on Tuesday, wounding at least 11 people, according to Saudi Civil Defence. It was the second attack on the skyscraper, which houses the sovereign wealth fund's headquarters, in less than a week. Saudi authorities called it a terrorist attack. Separately, Saudi air strikes in Yemen's Lahij governorate reportedly killed as many as 25 people, though those reports could not be independently verified.

The attacks are part of a renewed Yemeni conflict that flared in July, linked to the wider US-Iran war. The Houthis have pressed attacks on Saudi airports, oil sites and office buildings, and have made territorial gains in Yemen.

Yemen's government in Aden faces a Houthi advance, with a humanitarian crisis worsening for civilians.

auto-0aa5a775a2b3.headline: US Army pushes to detonate degraded lead azide stockpile in Iowa amid court fight
auto-0aa5a775a2b3.summary:
The US Army planned to blow up about 4.4 tonnes of degraded lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, after a federal appeals court paused its emergency permit. Officials said crystallised barrels posed a growing risk of an uncontrolled explosion as temperatures fall, and invoked emergency powers to proceed. Environmental groups and their lawyers argue the move sidesteps the court and that lead dust could spread widely, while President Trump later ordered a pause pending a court ruling.

Lead azide is an explosive used in military ammunition, and the planned blast was expected to release lead particles into the air. Critics said alternatives were not fully weighed and residents received little notice.

actors.why: Army and government face legal challenge and public criticism over the detonation plan

impact_points: Residents near Middletown, Iowa face possible lead exposure from the planned detonation, which critics say was poorly communicated.
The US Army and federal government face legal and public scrutiny over bypassing a court order and the EPA emergency permit.

auto-5a433846d68e.headline: Russian aircraft briefly enter South Korean air defence zone, prompting island alert
auto-5a433846d68e.summary:
Several Russian military aircraft briefly entered South Korea's air defence identification zone over the East Sea early on November 24, according to Seoul's military. They approached Ulleung Island before leaving the zone without entering national airspace. South Korean fighter jets were scrambled in response, and the military believes the planes would likely have crossed into its airspace without that reaction.

Residents of the island received an evacuation and air raid alert, which was lifted about three to five minutes later. The provincial advisory wrongly described the aircraft as suspected North Korean. Seoul said it planned to summon Russia's military attaché to lodge a formal complaint, the latest in a string of such incidents.

Nearby Sea of Japan airspace activity raises regional security concerns

Russia faces a formal complaint from Seoul amid growing military cooperation with North Korea.

auto-89e73372d705.headline: Iran and US tensions escalate around Hormuz as strike options and talks stall
auto-89e73372d705.summary: Tensions between Iran and the United States rose further as Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they shot down another US drone east of the Strait of Hormuz, and two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines there. Iran also said it struck US-linked radar sites at bases in Bahrain, while Bahraini authorities reported civilian injuries and a fire at an industrial site. Diplomacy remains stalled, with Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan trying to restart talks. Reports say the Trump administration may delay new strikes, while Israel presses for a joint campaign and is reportedly weighing unilateral action. Mediating talks and warning of economic damage from prolonged conflict
Working with regional mediators to revive US-Iran negotiations

Global energy markets and shipping face risk from mines and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

auto-c76d98c5a755.headline: Car bomb wrecks Colombian state building as armed violence spreads
auto-c76d98c5a755.summary: A car bomb exploded outside the government headquarters in Villavicencio, the capital of Meta province southeast of Bogotá, on Monday night. Footage shows collapsed façades, burnt-out vehicles and shattered glass, and nearby shops and homes were also damaged. Reports put the number of injured at around 23 to 25. Colombia's president, Abelardo de la Espriella, blamed Antonio Medina, a commander of the FARC dissident group EMC, and vowed retaliation. Police said the car held an estimated 80 to 100 kg of pentolite. Separately, a candlelit march in Cúcuta honoured families hurt in a recent attack, where the ELN is suspected but not formally blamed.

Violence along the Venezuelan border tied to trafficking networks fuels regional instability

Civilians in Villavicencio and Cúcuta bear the cost, with injuries, damaged homes and fear spreading through communities.

auto-44660770b7cb.headline: Eisenkot's Yashar signs first coalition pact as Israel government talks continue
auto-44660770b7cb.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said it agreed a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's Israel Our Home party, the first such alliance since Israel's October 27 election. Neither bloc won a clear majority, and Yashar and its partners hold 48 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

Talks with Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud on a possible unity government have continued without a breakthrough. Left-wing Democrats suspended their own talks with Eisenkot, and Israeli officials have also disagreed publicly over whether Iran poses an immediate threat.

Israel's Arab-majority parties, holding 19 seats, could become pivotal partners in any government Eisenkot forms.

auto-7a262dff1a9c.headline: Gunmen seize hostages in Cartagena, a major Colombian tourist city
auto-7a262dff1a9c.summary: Armed men have taken hostages in Cartagena, a coastal city in Colombia that draws large numbers of foreign tourists. The reporting available describes the seizure as taking place in the city, which is one of the country's best-known tourist destinations. Details on the number of hostages, the identity of the attackers and the demands made were not confirmed in the coverage reviewed. Colombian authorities were expected to respond, and the incident raises concern for visitors and residents in the area.

actors.why: Hostage-taking in a major tourist city threatens security and the tourism economy

impact_points: Colombia faces a security crisis in a key tourist city, threatening its reputation with visitors.

auto-adc6751b4eab.headline: Dozens dead in land dispute violence in Nigeria's Niger State
auto-adc6751b4eab.summary:
Dozens of people were reportedly killed in a fresh round of attacks linked to land disputes in Niger State, in north-central Nigeria. Residents described the weekend violence as among the deadliest recent incidents in the area. The exact death toll could not be independently confirmed, and the attackers' identities were not clearly established in the reporting.

Such clashes between farming and herding communities over land and water have recurred in the region for years, often causing heavy loss of life and displacement. Local authorities and security forces have been urged to act to protect civilians.

actors.why: Dozens killed and communities displaced, straining security forces and government

impact_points: Nigeria faces renewed insecurity in its north-central states, adding pressure on security forces and the government.

auto-0e5ad5804c07.headline: Belgian national strike grounds flights and disrupts transport over budget cuts
auto-0e5ad5804c07.summary:
A national strike against the government's planned austerity measures has brought air traffic in Belgium to a near standstill. Air traffic controllers at Skeyes said they could not safely run regular services between 7am and 9pm local time, so nearly all flights at Brussels, Charleroi and other airports were cancelled, affecting tens of thousands of passengers. Underground services in Brussels were halted, and schools and public services were also disrupted.

The action coincides with a tense political standoff. Prime Minister Bart De Wever is seeking a budget of about 10 billion euros in savings, but his five-party coalition remains split, with the Vooruit party opposing cuts to pensions and health. King Philippe declined the prime minister's resignation earlier this month, giving him more time to reach a deal.

French travellers stranded by cancelled Brussels flights to Paris

auto-b316417a4706.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit two Russian refineries in Samara Oblast
auto-b316417a4706.summary: Overnight on November 25, 2026, Ukrainian forces reportedly struck two Russian oil refineries in Samara Oblast, setting both sites ablaze, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels. The Syzran and Kuibyshev refineries, about 100 kilometers apart, were the targets, with video from residents showing a large fire at Kuibyshev. The reports could not be independently verified. Separate overnight strikes that week also reportedly hit oil facilities in Tatarstan, Rostov and Perm Krai, as Ukraine continues deep strikes on Russian energy and military sites.

auto-b8d7f738a6dc.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine needs €115 billion in outside funding for 2027
auto-b8d7f738a6dc.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine will require about €115 billion in external financing in 2027 to keep its economy and war effort running against Russia. He told regional officials that roughly €90 billion has already been committed, mainly by the European Union, which is now Ukraine's largest financial backer. Officials are still looking for the remaining €25 billion.

Separately, Kyiv and Oslo said they would expand a jointly developed anti-drone air defense system called DESNA, already in use in Ukraine. Ukraine's defense minister said Norway plans at least $7 billion in aid for 2027, with a priority on air defense and interceptor missiles, as Ukraine faces shortages of interceptors ahead of winter.

actors.why: Needs large external funding and air defense to withstand Russian attacks
Committing at least $7 billion in aid and expanding joint air defense production
Continued missile and drone campaign against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure
Main financial backer of Ukraine, approving further borrowing for Kyiv

Russia's continued missile and drone attacks keep pressure on Ukraine's air defenses and energy infrastructure.

auto-ee752877c410.headline: Solomon Islands signs Australia security treaty, ending China pact
auto-ee752877c410.summary:
Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signed a new security treaty in Canberra on Wednesday. It makes Australia the Pacific nation's main security partner and bars foreign military bases or major security infrastructure on Solomon Islands territory. The move follows Honiara's decision to end its 2022 security pact with China when it expires in April, a decision China has not publicly contested beyond saying its cooperation is not aimed at third parties.

In return, Solomon Islands gains new policing funding and easier visa arrangements for its citizens working in Australia, while Australia pledged investment in education, infrastructure and community development. Wale said secrecy provisions limited his comments on the Chinese pact.
