Loses warship, helicopter and resupply hub; Kremlin calls Ukraine's attacks dangerous
Claims a successful strike on a Russian warship, though Kyiv faces diplomatic criticism

impact_points: Libya faces pressure over its sovereignty, with its eastern and western governments calling for investigations into the attack.
Russia loses a newer warship and a logistics link in Libya, and its military footprint in the region comes under strain.

auto-498aa44ae35b.headline: Trump pauses Army plan to detonate lead azide stockpile in Iowa
auto-498aa44ae35b.summary: President Donald Trump has ordered the US Army to hold off on detonating about 4,500 kilograms of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown. The planned blast, set for November 20, drew public alarm over the possibility of toxic lead dust spreading over nearby homes, crops and livestock. A federal appeals court had temporarily frozen the Army's environmental permit, and later lifted that stay, but it remained unclear whether the operation would go ahead. Trump said Iowa's incoming governor, Rob Sand, should also approve, while the EPA warned that colder weather raises the risk of an uncontrolled explosion.

actors.why: Federal agencies face court disputes, public backlash and uncertainty over the stockpile's disposal.

impact_points: Residents of Middletown and surrounding Iowa communities face possible toxic lead dust exposure and evacuation risk.
The Army and federal agencies face legal and political pressure over how to safely dispose of the unstable material.

auto-896a0042f32f.headline: US Army to destroy degraded explosive stockpile at Iowa plant despite lead dust concerns
auto-896a0042f32f.summary:
The US Army plans to detonate about five tons of degraded lead azide, a volatile explosive compound, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning. Officials say the material is deteriorating and could explode unpredictably, so a controlled blast is the safer option. A federal appeals court cleared the operation on Monday, finding that the Environmental Protection Agency had built adequate dust safeguards into its emergency permit.

Residents within about five miles may be asked to leave, and those up to 20 miles away were told to stay indoors. Neighbouring Missouri, Illinois and Wisconsin officials have raised concerns, and the Missouri governor said the states have no say over the timing. Experts warn the plume could travel toward Missouri depending on wind.

actors.why: Army removes a dangerous stockpile, though the operation draws public and political scrutiny
Plume could drift toward Missouri and state officials lack control over the operation
Possible plume reach to towns in Illinois and state officials have no say on timing

impact_points: Middletown and nearby Iowa communities face possible toxic lead dust exposure and evacuation during the controlled blast.
Missouri, Illinois and Wisconsin face possible dust drift and monitoring costs, with their officials saying they lack authority over the operation.

auto-eee1ffa77e09.headline: Baghdad moves to take control of Kurdish oilfields and border crossings
auto-eee1ffa77e09.summary:
Iraq's prime minister, Ali al-Zaidi, has ordered federal authorities to manage oilfields in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahuddin and Nineveh provinces, including the Khormala field under Kurdish security control. He also directed the border authority to take over all crossings in the Kurdistan region, which borders Türkiye, Iran and Syria, and required crude and petroleum exports to be approved only through the federal oil ministry. The moves follow an investigation into a years-long smuggling network that reportedly moved oil from the Kurdistan region to Iran and then on to Afghanistan.

Kurdistan's regional prime minister, Masrour Barzani, called the decisions unacceptable and said they contradicted recent talks with Baghdad. Analysts say the order also targets pro-Iran armed groups, and Kataib Hezbollah rejected the investigation's findings.

actors.why: Federal government gains control over oil and border crossings, though dispute risks constitutional fight

impact_points: Iraq's Kurdistan region loses control over oil exports, oilfields and border crossings to Baghdad.
Iran and Türkiye face disruption to cross-border oil trade routes long used by smugglers and traders.

auto-1f8169e68c29.headline: Ukraine confirms drone strike on Russian ship in Gulf of Finland
auto-1f8169e68c29.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed his forces struck the Russian cargo ship Sparta II with a drone on November 21 in the Gulf of Finland. He told Bloomberg the vessel was a legitimate target because it carried weapons, and that it was hit in Russian waters before drifting into Finnish waters. The ship, which is under US and Ukrainian sanctions, caught fire and its 16 crew were evacuated; one crew member was injured. Russia's Kremlin has warned of painful consequences and rising Baltic tensions, while Finland said the strike raised safety concerns for civilian shipping.

actors.why: Sanctioned cargo ship hit; Kaliningrad supply route exposed, prompting costly new ferries
Ukraine claims a lawful strike on a weapons-carrying vessel, disrupting Russian supply lines
Fire and drifting ship in its waters; shipping risk and airspace concerns
Estonian vessels helped fight the fire, and the Gulf of Finland is a shared shipping route
Lithuania's transit restrictions to Kaliningrad shape the route the ship was using

impact_points: Finland faces risks to civilian shipping and environmental safety in a busy, narrow Baltic corridor.
Russia's Kaliningrad exclave depends on sea supplies, so it is pressing to secure its supply routes.

auto-e301db1a961b.headline: Overnight Russian strikes hit energy and industrial sites in Zhytomyr and Poltava
auto-e301db1a961b.summary: Russian forces struck energy infrastructure and industrial businesses in Zhytomyr and Poltava oblasts overnight into 25 November, according to regional military administration heads. In Zhytomyr, one person was injured and taken to hospital after an attack on an energy facility and a civilian business. In Poltava, a drone hit an industrial site, causing a fire with no casualties. The attacks come amid emergency power cuts in parts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, announced by Ukrenergo.

actors.why: Energy and industrial sites hit, one injured, emergency power cuts imposed
Strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure continue, though no direct cost to Russia reported

impact_points: Ukraine faces further damage to energy and industrial capacity in Zhytomyr and Poltava, with an injured civilian.
Ukrainian households in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast face emergency power cuts as the grid strains under continued attacks.

auto-138753032068.headline: Washington drops business incentives for Russia, returns to land-for-peace talks
auto-138753032068.summary:
The Trump administration has reportedly set aside plans to offer Russia business deals, such as US investment in oil projects, titanium production and gas pipeline supplies, as a reason to end the war in Ukraine. According to the Financial Times, citing five officials, the shift followed little Russian interest in energy and aviation ventures. Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner reportedly told European officials that the focus is now on territory and security.

Moscow has reportedly kept demanding that Ukraine cede territory, including Donbas, which Kyiv rejects. Reuters could not immediately verify the report, and the White House did not respond to its request for comment.

actors.why: Business incentives dropped; Moscow keeps hardline demands, avoiding pressure to concede.
US pivots to territorial concessions Kyiv rejects, increasing pressure on Ukraine.
Abandons its business-deal approach after Russian disinterest, reverting to traditional negotiation.
European officials were briefed on the change; Nord Stream and gas supply ideas are sidelined.

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued Russian demands for territorial concessions it considers unacceptable, with the US now favouring a land-for-peace approach.
Russia loses a potential route to Western business and investment, though it may still expect sanctions relief after any settlement.

auto-6f7ef493c791.headline: Two Libyan officers die after drone strike on Russian warship in Benghazi
auto-6f7ef493c791.summary: Two officers of the eastern-based Libyan National Army died from wounds sustained in a drone attack on a Russian corvette at Benghazi port, local authorities said. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Kyiv carried out the strike using naval drones, while Libyan officials said the vessel was heavily damaged rather than sunk. A cargo ship linked to Russian military supply routes was also hit. The eastern government has asked the UN for an investigation, and Tripoli's government demanded an explanation from Ukraine.

actors.why: Two officers killed and Libya risks becoming a battleground for foreign conflicts
Corvette damaged and a supply vessel hit, undermining its Libyan military ties
Claimed the strike but faces diplomatic demands for explanation and investigation
Russian military supply route to Syria disrupted by the attack on the vessel

impact_points: Libya's eastern authorities face fallout after two officers died and have vowed retaliation against Kyiv.
Russia loses a warship and a supply vessel tied to its military links with Libya and Syria.

auto-389c693bbd30.headline: Russian strikes kill two in Odesa Oblast, injure three including a child
auto-389c693bbd30.summary:
Russian attacks on Odesa Oblast on 24 November killed a 41-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy, according to the regional military administration, which said three others were hurt, one of them a 12-year-old child. Damage was reported to civilian infrastructure, a house, an industrial building and vehicles, and a fire broke out.

The Odesa strikes came amid wider Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities, including a late-November strike on a residential building in Zaporizhzhia that officials said killed at least two and injured dozens, with some of the injured reported in critical condition.

actors.why: Civilians killed and injured in Odesa Oblast, with homes and infrastructure damaged
Strikes on Ukrainian cities continue, drawing attention to its attacks on civilians

impact_points: Ukraine's Odesa Oblast faces fresh civilian deaths and injuries, including a child, from Russian strikes.
Russia's continued attacks on Ukrainian cities keep civilian infrastructure and homes under pressure ahead of winter.

auto-ee894aa99f56.headline: Estonia's foreign minister visits Kyiv as Russia threatens retaliation over refinery strikes
auto-ee894aa99f56.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna arrived in Kyiv on a visit, posting footage of the Ukrainian capital on social media on Wednesday 25 November. The same period saw sharp escalation between Moscow and Kyiv. Russian President Vladimir Putin said Ukraine keeps striking Russian oil refineries despite a request from US President Donald Trump to stop, and warned that retaliation is inevitable. Estonia's closure of its land border with Russia drew Moscow's accusations of hostile acts.

actors.why: Foreign minister visits Kyiv while Estonia closes its border with Russia
Continued refinery strikes draw Russian retaliation threats while Ukraine shows diplomatic support
Refinery throughput down about 45 percent, fuel restrictions, and Putin threatens retaliation

impact_points: Estonia is strengthening its ties with Ukraine through a high-level visit to Kyiv during heightened tensions.
Russia faces refinery losses and fuel rationing, and has signalled it will retaliate against Ukraine and its supporters.

auto-4f42edbb8809.headline: Eisenkot's bid to form Israeli government hit as left-wing Democrats pause talks
auto-4f42edbb8809.summary:
Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot faces a setback in his effort to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, after the left-wing Democrats suspended coalition talks with his Yashar party. The move came as Yashar reached its first coalition agreement with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing Israel Our Home party. The Democrats objected to Eisenkot's talks with Likud and ultra-Orthodox parties about a possible unity government.

An inconclusive October 27 election left neither leader with a clear path. Eisenkot's bloc won 48 seats and Netanyahu's allies 53, both short of the 120-seat majority needed. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

actors.why: Political deadlock over government formation continues, with Netanyahu remaining caretaker prime minister.

impact_points: Eisenkot's Yashar party faces a weaker path to power after losing its left-wing Democrats partners from talks.
Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister and would likely be next to try forming a government if Eisenkot fails.

auto-875b45aea9c9.headline: UK sanctions Myanmar generals after court finds genocide against Rohingya
auto-875b45aea9c9.summary: The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions on five senior Myanmar military officers after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. The officers face asset freezes and travel bans, and London plans legislation to restrict aviation fuel supplies to the country. The court found that about 10,000 Rohingya were killed and more than 700,000 forced into Bangladesh. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the UK would press the issue at the UN Security Council, while Myanmar's military-backed government has rejected the ruling.

actors.why: Officers sanctioned and ruling rejected, facing international isolation and pressure
Leads a coordinated response, sanctions and Security Council push
Hosts over a million Rohingya refugees, supported by international attention

impact_points: Myanmar's military leaders face UK asset freezes, travel bans and a ban on serving as UK company directors.
The Rohingya and Bangladesh, which hosts refugees, gain international recognition but face an uncertain path to justice and return.

auto-6d44e8cca0d8.headline: China and Cambodia launch their largest joint military drill yet
auto-6d44e8cca0d8.summary:
China and Cambodia are holding their Golden Dragon joint military exercise, which reporting describes as the largest of the series so far. Chinese forces are taking part on Cambodian territory, with training focused on shared security and military cooperation between the two countries. The drill continues a long-running partnership between Beijing and Phnom Penh. Details of specific scenarios and troop numbers were not fully confirmed in the reporting.

The exercise reinforces close defence ties between the two governments and signals growing Chinese military presence in Southeast Asia. Neither side's reported statements were independently verified against the scale claims.

actors.why: Hosts the drill and deepens security ties with Beijing
Expands military cooperation and regional influence in Southeast Asia

impact_points: Cambodia deepens its defence partnership with China, strengthening its security ties with Beijing.
China expands its military footprint and influence in Southeast Asia through the joint drill.

auto-3ddaeb93e31c.headline: Baghdad orders federal control of oilfields in Kurdish-secured areas
auto-3ddaeb93e31c.summary: Iraq's Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered the federal oil ministry to take over management of oilfields in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahuddin and Nineveh provinces, areas under Kurdish security control. The order also gives federal border authorities control of crossings in the Kurdistan Region and requires Kurdish exports of crude and petroleum products to receive federal oil ministry approval. Zaidi's office framed the move as protecting national sovereignty and Iraq's resources from smuggling, following an investigation into the state-owned North Oil Company. Kurdish leaders, including Masrour Barzani, rejected the directives as unacceptable.

actors.why: Central government asserts control over oil, borders and smuggling networks
Iran's oil smuggling route and Iran-aligned militia face Baghdad's crackdown
Kurdish oil pipeline exports to Turkey could be disrupted by federal control

impact_points: Iraq's Kurdistan Region faces a serious loss of control over oil output, exports and border crossings.
Iran-aligned groups such as Kataib Hezbollah are also targeted, as Baghdad accuses them of running smuggling networks.

auto-e20b92a91a98.headline: Rights group urges war crimes inquiry into deadly shelling in Ethiopia's Tigray
auto-e20b92a91a98.summary:
Amnesty International has called for an investigation into possible war crimes after 14 civilians, three of them children, were killed in artillery shelling of Alamata in Tigray between September 26 and 28. The rights group says the Ethiopian army and a pro-government Tigrayan militia carried out the attacks, which it describes as indiscriminate. It also accused the Tigray People's Liberation Front of placing military bases in residential areas, including schools. The TPLF rejected the accusations, while the federal army and government did not respond to requests for comment.

Amnesty based its findings on interviews with 28 people, including survivors and witnesses, and urged the UN Human Rights Council to act. The call comes after the TPLF's failed September offensive and fears of a return to the 2020-22 war, in which an estimated 600,000 people died. No one has yet been prosecuted for alleged war crimes from that conflict.

actors.why: Federal army accused of indiscriminate shelling; faces war crimes investigation calls
Not directly reported as involved; no clear effect from these reports

impact_points: Ethiopia's federal government and army face scrutiny over alleged war crimes in Tigray, with possible international accountability pressure.
Tigray's civilians remain exposed to shelling, and the TPLF faces accusations over placing bases near homes and schools.

auto-b5a22ae7c692.headline: US Army to detonate Iowa lead azide stockpile as residents shelter
auto-b5a22ae7c692.summary: The US Army plans a controlled detonation of its entire lead azide stockpile, about 4,400 kg, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, a town of roughly 400 people. The blast has been postponed several times amid public concern over possible toxic lead dust spreading across a wide area. Officials say the material degraded and became unstable, and that no viable alternative existed. Residents have been advised to shelter indoors, some nearby areas face evacuation, and FEMA is supporting relocation. A court challenge by environmental groups and a pause ordered by President Trump have also shaped the timing, with the plan now set for Wednesday.

actors.why: Domestic safety operation with federal response and legal disputes, not an international event

impact_points: Middletown residents and nearby communities in Iowa and Missouri face possible toxic lead dust exposure and evacuation.
The US Army and federal agencies must manage the detonation's health, legal and public trust fallout.

auto-cbfe74753f85.headline: Western-made parts and Lithuanian SIM cards found in downed Russian attack drones
auto-cbfe74753f85.summary:
Ukrainian intelligence reports, seen by the Kyiv Independent, say a Russian Geran-4 drone shot down over Kyiv Oblast in August 2026 contained components made by U.S. and European manufacturers only months earlier. Twelve parts carried date codes, seven of them from 2026, which suggests Russia is still obtaining restricted Western technology through third-country sanctions-evasion networks. The manufacturers named, including STMicroelectronics and Vishay, either did not explain how the parts reached Russia or said they block such shipments.

A separate Ukrainian intelligence file lists eight prepaid SIM cards from Lithuanian operators found in Russian drones that struck Ukraine in 2025. Lithuanian operator Tele2 said its cards were activated in 2024, before mandatory registration, and that such cards can be resold to third parties.

actors.why: Russian drones using Western parts and SIM cards struck Ukrainian civilian infrastructure
Russia still obtains restricted Western tech via sanctions-evasion networks
Lithuanian prepaid SIM cards found in Russian drones, reputational and regulatory pressure
U.S.-made components found in Russian drones, export control failures under scrutiny
European components in Russian drones expose gaps in EU export restrictions
Swiss-headquartered STMicroelectronics part found in a Russian drone

impact_points: Ukraine faces Russian drones that use Western components and foreign SIM cards to navigate and evade detection.
Western manufacturers and Lithuanian telecom operators face scrutiny over how their products reached Russian weapons supply chains.

auto-0eddb6bce2ec.headline: Israeli minister alleges Iranian chemical weapons work; ally urges no immediate strike
auto-0eddb6bce2ec.summary: Israel's defence minister, Israel Katz, said Iran is developing chemical weapons and that Israel will not allow it to acquire them, while noting Iran has not yet reached the capability to attack Israel with them. He also floated a possible pre-emptive strike. Iran dismissed the allegations as propaganda. Avigdor Liberman, who has joined a coalition deal with opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot, said there was no intelligence or operational justification for an independent Israeli attack in the immediate term. The remarks come after a recent Israeli election that produced no clear majority.

actors.why: Officials divided over timing of possible strikes on Iran amid political deadlock
Faces accusations of chemical weapons development and threat of Israeli action

impact_points: Israel faces a debate over whether to launch strikes on Iran, with its leadership divided over timing.
Iran is accused of chemical weapons development it denies, raising pressure on Tehran and tensions with Israel.

auto-7e84665255d1.headline: Court clears US Army plan to blow up degraded lead azide in Iowa
auto-7e84665255d1.summary:
A federal appeals court has allowed the US Army to proceed with a controlled detonation of about 68 drums of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa. Officials say the material is at risk of spontaneous explosion. The blast could release a plume of toxic lead dust reaching up to 100 miles northeast, and residents have been urged to leave as a precaution.

The detonation was postponed several times after public concern over health and environmental effects. President Trump said the decision depended on incoming Democratic governor-elect Rob Sands agreeing, and urged him to take responsibility if the operation did not proceed. Sand has asked for more federal transparency, while Republican senator Chuck Grassley backed a controlled removal.

actors.why: Federal army operation proceeds after court ruling, despite public and political criticism over transparency
Local town and state face toxic lead dust risk from the controlled blast
State agencies must add air and water monitoring without a say in the operation
Possible dust plume could reach cities such as New Boston, with no say in the decision
Senator Baldwin protests the army's handling of the lead azide

impact_points: Middletown and nearby Iowa communities face possible lead dust exposure, so residents are urged to stay indoors.
Neighbouring Missouri, Illinois and Wisconsin face concern over monitoring, public health and agriculture, with limited say in the operation.

auto-06bd329264c9.headline: RSF drone attacks in Blue Nile state leave 19 civilians dead
auto-06bd329264c9.summary: Drone strikes attributed to Sudan's Rapid Support Forces killed at least 19 civilians and wounded about 20 others in Damazin and Roseires in Blue Nile state on Tuesday night, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. The dead in Damazin included six women and members of three families, while the group said drones also targeted power and dam facilities in Roseires, raising the risk of electricity disruption across the state. Residents who witnessed the strikes confirmed to Reuters that drone attacks took place, and a Sudanese military source gave a similar account. The attacks come amid a sharp rise in drone warfare between the RSF and the army, which has been fighting since April 2023.

actors.why: Civilians killed and power facilities targeted by RSF drone attacks

impact_points: Sudanese civilians in Blue Nile state face deadly strikes and possible loss of electricity supplies.
Sudan's army and the RSF are both locked in escalating drone warfare, deepening the nation's civil war.

auto-f84d2ca148a8.headline: Trump says US can fund Iran war into late January
auto-f84d2ca148a8.summary:
US President Donald Trump told the New York Post that his administration has enough funding to keep fighting Iran until the end of January, and that he could end the conflict whenever he chooses. He warned that Democrats taking control of Congress could restrict his military options, and said regime change was not his main aim, focusing instead on preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon. Reports said officials were weighing further strikes, including assassinations of senior Iranian leaders.

In Tehran, Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran would hold no talks or actions until its seven conditions were met, and vowed a decisive response to any hostile move. He was responding to remarks by Trump and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who announced fresh sanctions on Iranian entities.

actors.why: Faces ongoing war, sanctions and threats of leadership assassinations
Pursuing war with funding limits and possible congressional constraints
US embassy warns of Houthi and Iranian threats, forcing security precautions
Iranian attacks on US sites in Bahrain raise regional security risks
Iranian attacks on US sites in Kuwait raise regional security risks
Houthi attack warnings tied to the wider regional escalation

impact_points: Iran faces continued US strikes, sanctions and naval blockade, with its leadership and military capabilities under pressure.
The United States faces prolonged war costs and tighter congressional limits, while regional US sites and citizens face heightened security risks.

auto-66c705c4981d.headline: US jury convicts Huawei on fraud and trade secret theft charges
auto-66c705c4981d.summary:
A federal jury in New York convicted Chinese telecoms equipment maker Huawei on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including bank and wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. Huawei was acquitted of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice. The charges stem from alleged dealings in Iran that deceived banks, and from theft of technology from US firms such as Cisco and T-Mobile.

The company's lawyers said they will appeal, and sentencing is set for September 14, 2027. Beijing condemned the verdict as an effort to contain Chinese firms, while Huawei's business has reportedly been little affected by the case.

actors.why: Huawei convicted; Beijing condemns verdict as US containment of Chinese firms
Jury verdict backs Justice Department claims on sanctions and national security
Recalls 2018 Meng Wanzhou detention that sparked a diplomatic crisis
Huawei's alleged dealings in Iran were central to the sanctions-violation charges

impact_points: China and Huawei face reputational and financial costs, including expected penalties and a prolonged appeal process.
US financial institutions and American technology firms are linked to the case, as the verdict affirms claims of banking deception and trade secret theft.

auto-4b46e6086929.headline: Poland seeks NATO backing to shoot down Russian missiles over Ukraine
auto-4b46e6086929.summary:
Three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles struck southeast Poland on 20 November, prompting debate within NATO. Poland has asked allies to consider intercepting Russian missiles over Ukrainian territory when they head toward NATO airspace, but sources said talks were preliminary, no decision was reached, and unanimity does not currently exist.

NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe has authorised the forward deployment of an AWACS early-warning aircraft to Poland, with further assets under review. Poland also reported a brief Russian drone incursion from Ukraine that night, which it chose not to shoot down, and Russia was blamed for the missile strikes.

actors.why: Missiles and a drone violated its airspace, though it gains AWACS support
Russian missiles and drones target its territory, and it would host any interception
Its missiles struck Poland, drawing a NATO response and escalation scrutiny
Its eastern NATO flank faces spillover risk and debate over response options

impact_points: Poland faces repeated airspace violations and gains an AWACS aircraft for better surveillance and response.
Ukraine and NATO allies could face direct confrontation with Russia if interception over Ukraine were approved.

auto-dbf83816bc17.headline: Iraqi court backs federal troop deployment to borders, including Kurdish-run crossings
auto-dbf83816bc17.summary:
Iraq's Federal Supreme Court has ruled that federal forces can be deployed along all international borders, including those in the Kurdistan region, state television reported. The decision follows Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's order to take over border crossings run by Kurdish authorities after an oil smuggling probe at the state-run North Oil Company. The court also said the federal oil ministry can oversee and audit oil and gas fields, though Baghdad must coordinate with regional and provincial governments.

Kurdish authorities rejected what they called military language and threats, while saying they are working with Baghdad to fight corruption and oil smuggling. The ruling is seen as a win for Zaidi, whose moves also came a week after a standoff with the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah.

actors.why: Central government gains legal authority to assert control over borders and oil
Oil smuggling routes to Iran are targeted by the new border measures

impact_points: Iraq's Kurdistan region faces tighter central control over its border crossings and oil fields.
Iran-linked smuggling routes are targeted, affecting Iran and oil flows through Kurdish and Iraqi territory.

auto-fe9d21a77215.headline: Eisenkot and Netanyahu split over need for immediate Iran strike
auto-fe9d21a77215.summary:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming the next government, said on Monday he saw no immediate threat from Iran requiring military action before a government is formed. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu countered that the Iranian threat is grave and that downplaying it is political. The two men's parties were set to hold a third round of coalition talks, which had yet to produce a breakthrough. Reports say Netanyahu has pressed the Trump administration to authorise a short, forceful strike on Iran.

Eisenkot has until 6 December, extendable by 14 days, to form a government after the October election left neither bloc with a majority. He argues a caretaker government lacks authority to launch a major offensive without imminent danger.

actors.why: Political split over a possible strike and unresolved coalition talks
Faces renewed threat of an Israeli strike over its nuclear stockpile
Reportedly being pressed by Netanyahu to authorise a strike on Iran

impact_points: Iran faces renewed threat of Israeli military action, though Eisenkot says no immediate strike is needed.
The United States, whose administration Netanyahu reportedly lobbied, could be drawn into any strike on Iran.

auto-858399b78e1f.headline: Eastern Libyan commander Haftar holds talks in Ankara ahead of Erdoğan visit
auto-858399b78e1f.summary:
Khalifa Haftar, who commands forces in eastern Libya, travelled to Ankara this week and held talks with senior Turkish officials, including Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Defence Minister Yaşar Güler and intelligence chief İbrahim Kalın. He also met President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, according to a photograph released by the presidency, though no details of the closed-door discussions were published. The visit came days after Ukrainian naval drones sank a Russian warship at Benghazi, an incident that has raised concerns about wider instability in Libya.

The talks come before Erdoğan's planned trip to Tripoli on 8-9 December for a Turkey-Africa summit, which would be his first visit to Libya in 15 years. Turkey has backed the Tripoli government in the past but has recently widened its contacts with eastern authorities as it seeks to bridge Libya's political divide.

actors.why: Divided country may gain mediation momentum, but the Benghazi incident raises instability.
Strengthens influence with both Libyan camps ahead of Erdoğan's planned visit.
Russian warship sunk at Benghazi and its eastern Libya foothold faces uncertainty.
Ukrainian naval strike drew requests for explanation from Tripoli and calls for investigation.

impact_points: Libya's divided factions gain a possible route toward unity if Turkey's mediation advances.
Russia's position in eastern Libya faces uncertainty after the Benghazi naval strike and deepening Turkish engagement.

auto-1daa9424745a.headline: Greeks take to streets in nationwide strike over pay and services
auto-1daa9424745a.summary:
Thousands of people joined a nationwide strike across Greece to protest low wages and the state of public services. Workers walked off the job and rallied in major cities, and transport and other services were disrupted during the action. The protest focuses on domestic pressures rather than any international dispute, with demonstrators pressing the government for higher pay and better funding for public institutions.

The strike highlights ongoing labour discontent in Greece over the cost of living and the condition of publicly provided services. No international party is directly involved in the reporting.

actors.why: Nationwide strike disrupts transport and services while pressing government on pay

impact_points: Greece's government faces pressure to respond to labour demands on wages and public service funding.
Greek commuters and public service users face disruption to transport and other services during the strike.

auto-36f72e5e2ab7.headline: Washington moves to reimpose tariffs on sixteen economies over surplus production
auto-36f72e5e2ab7.summary: The United States is preparing a new round of tariffs on 16 economies, including China and the European Union, after its trade office found that their industrial subsidies harm American manufacturers. The Office of the US Trade Representative ran a Section 301 investigation, and the results are expected to be announced this week, according to reporting by El País citing The Wall Street Journal. The move follows a Supreme Court ruling that struck down earlier broad tariffs imposed under emergency powers. The administration has not disclosed the final rates, but reports say they will be set per economy, with trade-deal partners such as Japan and the EU likely held to about 15% or less, while China could face a higher rate.

actors.why: Likely higher tariffs, singled out over widespread production subsidies
Named in the probe, but trade-deal terms should cap its rate
Restores tariff leverage after the Supreme Court setback, though legal challenges remain
Trade agreement should keep its tariff near 15% or less

impact_points: China faces a likely higher tariff, as Washington argues its production subsidies are widespread and damaging.
The EU and Japan are expected to receive capped rates under existing trade agreements, limiting the damage to them.

auto-16b98667e3fa.headline: Kremlin refuses to address leaked estimates of Russian war dead in Ukraine
auto-16b98667e3fa.summary:
The Kremlin declined on Wednesday to comment on reports that hundreds of thousands of Russian soldiers have died in the war in Ukraine, now nearly five years old. The figures come from data hacked from Russia's federal statistics agency, Rosstat, which was analysed by several Russian and international outlets. Estimates range from roughly 470,000 to 700,000 dead, while Moscow has published no official military toll since 2022. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only the defence ministry can release casualty figures and urged people to disregard other data.

The reporting also notes that Ukrainian losses are estimated far lower, with President Zelensky citing about 55,000 soldiers killed, a figure thought to be an underestimate. Independent analysts could not independently confirm the totals.

actors.why: Official silence and leaked data expose heavy military losses and reputational strain
Its own reported losses are far lower, though estimates are also thought to be undercounts

impact_points: Russia faces mounting questions over its war losses, with its official silence now widely criticised by outside observers.
Russian families and military recruitment are affected, as the leaked figures point to heavy losses among young men from poorer regions.

auto-176b199df9ee.headline: NATO vows space defence as reports suggest Russian nuclear-armed satellite plan
auto-176b199df9ee.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance will guard against threats in space after German media reported that Russia may launch a satellite carrying a nuclear warhead within weeks. The reports, citing unnamed German military and intelligence sources, describe the satellite as capable of disrupting or destroying other satellites. Speaking in Berlin with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Rutte said NATO's deterrence assessments would be updated where needed. Moscow rejected the allegations as unfounded, and the Kremlin said it had not seen the reports and dismissed them as propaganda.

actors.why: Accused of preparing a nuclear-armed satellite; denies it and faces rising scrutiny
Chancellor Merz says the reports are shocking and Berlin is taking them seriously
Alliance partner whose space defence posture supports NATO's response
European Space Agency chief calls nuclear weapons in space a nightmare scenario

impact_points: Russia faces accusations of planning a nuclear weapon in orbit, which it firmly denies.
NATO members, including Germany, must weigh space defence and deterrence against a possible threat to satellites.

auto-0a92ef28e156.headline: Saudi Arabia projects $1 trillion investment potential as non-oil income grows
auto-0a92ef28e156.summary:
Saudi Arabia says it expects around $1 trillion in investment opportunities over the next eight to ten years, and that non-oil revenues have tripled since Vision 2030 began. At a budget forum in Riyadh, officials said non-oil income now covers roughly 36 to 37 percent of spending, up from about 17 percent before the programme. The figures came days after the Cabinet approved a 2027 budget of 1.392 trillion riyals, with a projected deficit of 190.6 billion riyals.

Officials also highlighted rerouting of trade through Red Sea ports after regional shipping disruptions, and a rise in oil output to 10.6 million barrels a day. Finance Minister Mohammed Aljadaan and Economy Minister Faisal Alibrahim presented the data; investment figures were not independently verified.

actors.why: Diversifying revenues and attracting investment, but facing a budget deficit and regional shipping disruption
Red Sea shipping rerouting may affect Egyptian Suez and regional trade flows

impact_points: Saudi Arabia's public finances gain resilience as oil revenue dependence declines, though a deficit remains.
Foreign and private investors are offered large opportunities, while Red Sea trade routes show growing importance.

auto-324253adb6c1.headline: US court allows Army to detonate degraded explosive chemicals in Iowa
auto-324253adb6c1.summary:
A federal appeals court has cleared the way for the US Army to detonate about 9,500 pounds of degraded lead azide, a bomb-making chemical, stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown. The detonation had been postponed several times after public concern over toxic lead dust, which the Army warns could travel up to 100 miles. President Trump said the move was subject to the incoming Democratic governor, Rob Sand, agreeing, and called for more transparency; officials advise residents to stay indoors during the blast.

Neighbouring Missouri, Illinois and Wisconsin have also voiced concern. Missouri's governor said it is a federal operation and the neighbouring states have no say, while a Wisconsin senator protested the handling of the material.

actors.why: Army proceeds with the detonation after court clearance despite local concerns
Residents face possible toxic lead exposure and evacuation or shelter advice
State agencies must monitor air and water without a say in the operation
Possible lead dust drift toward cities such as New Boston across the border
Senator protests the army's handling of the explosive material

impact_points: Middletown residents and Iowa are exposed to possible lead dust and must follow shelter guidance.
Neighbouring Missouri, Illinois and Wisconsin face possible spillover and have no formal say over the operation.

auto-2b9dd1e43c07.headline: Tehran rejects Israeli chemical weapons accusation as attempt to pull US into war
auto-2b9dd1e43c07.summary: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi accused Israel of trying to deceive the United States into another war, after Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz alleged Tehran is developing chemical weapons. Katz said Iran has not yet reached the capability to attack Israel with them, and he vowed to stop the programme. Iran dismissed the claims as propaganda. Israeli opposition figure Avigdor Liberman said there was no immediate justification for an independent Israeli strike, accusing Netanyahu and Katz of pursuing political gain. Separately, Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi raised Iran's chemical weapons victims and recent attacks on its facilities at the OPCW meeting in The Hague.

actors.why: Accused of chemical weapons work, but rejects claims and warns of being dragged into conflict
Officials openly weigh strike options amid domestic political criticism over timing
Pressed by Iran and Israel to consider joining a possible military action

impact_points: Israel faces domestic criticism over claims of a possible strike, with opponents questioning its timing and motives.
Iran and the US are drawn toward a possible confrontation, with Tehran warning Washington against being used by Israel.

auto-b5d5010f0e30.headline: Pentagon rebukes Ottawa over military spending and F-35 review; Canada rejects US oversight
auto-b5d5010f0e30.summary:
The US Department of Defense issued a blunt fact sheet criticising Canada's military spending and its review of a planned purchase of American-made F-35 fighter jets. The document says Canada has avoided hard choices needed to meet NATO commitments, cites low readiness rates across its air, naval and army forces, and claims Ottawa lacks a credible, fully costed path to 5% of GDP by 2035. Canada's defence minister, David McGuinty, said his country is sovereign and does not report to Washington, while stressing that cooperation through NORAD and NATO has not changed. The government is also weighing Swedish Gripen jets as an alternative.

The criticism comes as Prime Minister Mark Carney pushes a new defence bank in Europe, which so far has ten backers but no other G7 members. Ottawa says its spending has risen to meet NATO's 2% target, with further increases planned.

actors.why: Publicly criticised by the Pentagon and under pressure to fix readiness and spending gaps
Pushes allies on defence spending and seeks to shape Canada's fighter jet choice
Canada is courting European partners for its new defence bank, with few G7 takers so far

impact_points: Canada faces pressure over its readiness and spending, with its F-35 purchase decision now politically sensitive.
US-Canada defence ties face strain, though officials say NORAD cooperation and intelligence sharing continue unchanged.

auto-e4dbb7c35cc6.headline: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi refinery and Riyadh financial hub
auto-e4dbb7c35cc6.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement said on Wednesday it had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the kingdom's largest, on the Gulf coast, and claimed a further assault on Riyadh's financial district. Satellite imagery showed thick smoke rising over the Ras Tanura site, and a source familiar with the matter confirmed an attack there. Saudi authorities and Aramco had not immediately commented. A day earlier, 11 people were wounded in a strike on a tower housing the sovereign wealth fund's headquarters, the second hit on the building in under a week.

actors.why: Refinery fires and repeated strikes on Riyadh damage infrastructure, events and foreign flights
Houthis press offensives and gain ground, though Saudi-backed forces are on the back foot
Houthi attacks linked to the wider US-Iran war, bolstering Tehran's regional leverage
Wider US-Iran war drives the Houthi campaign, adding pressure on Gulf partners

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces repeated strikes on oil infrastructure and its capital, disrupting energy operations and major events.
Aramco and Saudi export routes are under strain, with the Houthi campaign spilling over from the wider US-Iran conflict.

auto-14b4a71919ff.headline: Ukrainian laser downs Russian jet drone in first combat use
auto-14b4a71919ff.summary:
Ukraine says a Blysk laser air defence system, built by the company Carmine Sky, shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran drone for the first time in combat. The laser was protecting a critical infrastructure site, according to Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to President Zelenskyy. He cautioned that serial production of such lasers is still far off, as the systems remain in trials. Separately, a German-Ukrainian venture reported that its SPYS interceptor drone destroyed a Russian Geran-5 variant during testing in Ukraine.

Jet-powered Geran drones are faster than earlier propeller models, making them harder to stop, and Ukraine's private air defence program is expanding with dozens of firms taking part. The reports did not independently verify the claims.

actors.why: Gains a new laser defence against fast Russian drones, still in trials
A jet-powered Geran drone type was downed by a new countermeasure
German firm's interceptor drone tested successfully in Ukraine

impact_points: Ukraine gains a cheaper potential counter to fast Russian jet drones, though the laser is still experimental.
Russia loses one of its newer drone types to a demonstrated countermeasure, while its attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure continue.

auto-2a2a052a194c.headline: Jordanian court sentences attacker to death for fatal Amman stabbing
auto-2a2a052a194c.summary: Jordan's State Security Court has sentenced a man to death for a stabbing in Amman that killed a security officer, according to the armed forces. The officer was stabbed near the Sri Lankan embassy on November 5, less than two weeks after gunmen attacked a church in Karak governorate. The court convicted the man of terrorist acts resulting in death and possessing a weapon for terrorist purposes. The verdict can be appealed and will get an automatic review by the Court of Cassation. Earlier this month, three men were sentenced to death over the church attack in Hamoud.

actors.why: Two rare militant attacks force a tough security and judicial response domestically.
Jordan is a US ally; attacks on its stability are a concern for Washington.

impact_points: Jordan faces rare militant violence in its capital and south, testing a traditionally stable US ally's security forces.
Jordanian security officers and the Christian community are directly affected by the attacks and the harsh judicial response.

auto-e84130d2a0e2.headline: Ecuador and US discuss revising joint operations after raid probe
auto-e84130d2a0e2.summary:
The United States and Ecuador have held talks on reviewing their joint operations in Ecuador, which Washington had paused while it investigated a September raid carried out by Ecuadoran forces. The operation killed Carlos German Munoz Jara, whom officials describe as a senior gang member, and has raised questions about possible human rights abuses. Ecuador's interior minister, John Reimberg, said last week's meeting between US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and President Daniel Noboa in Quito was productive and produced an agreed action plan.

The joint effort, announced in March as a new phase against drug trafficking and illegal mining, has also drawn attention to a US presence at Taura Air Base. Noboa has said the American personnel there are only on temporary activities and denied that the US runs a base in the country.

actors.why: Joint operations resume under an agreed plan, but abuse allegations draw scrutiny.
Paused operations are under review, with a new action plan agreed with Ecuador.

impact_points: Ecuador faces scrutiny over possible abuses, while its government says the US partnership has delivered results.
The United States must weigh its anti-drug cooperation against concerns about human rights and military accountability.

auto-90b50f60612a.headline: Britain shelters RAF aircraft overnight and plans anti-drone netting, reports say
auto-90b50f60612a.summary:
Britain's Royal Air Force is reportedly moving aircraft into hangars and hardened shelters at night to guard against possible drone attacks. The Times and Sky News, which reported the measures without naming sources, also said anti-drone netting is planned for planes left outside. The Ministry of Defence did not confirm the details but said it is adapting to potential threats and is investing an additional £470 million in site security, including counter-drone capabilities.

The move follows warnings from the Ministry of Defence and MI5 about Russian sabotage aimed at firms supporting Ukraine's military, and recent incidents at British bases that appeared linked to Iran, which Tehran denies. US forces also responded to suspected drone activity at RAF Lakenheath this month.

actors.why: Bases being hardened with £470m investment amid Russian and Iran-linked threats
Accused by UK authorities of sabotage threats against Ukraine-supporting firms
Linked to recent incidents at UK bases, which Tehran denies
US aircraft moved from British bases after Iran-linked threats and drone activity
Supporting firms face sabotage risks from Russia, indirectly affecting Ukraine's supply chain

impact_points: The UK is hardening its air bases against drones, reflecting concern over sabotage by Russia and Iran-linked actors.
US forces stationed at British bases, such as Lakenheath and Fairford, face similar drone and sabotage risks.

auto-52a3bb993a32.headline: Russia braces for possible Ukrainian drone strikes on winter utilities
auto-52a3bb993a32.summary:
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said Moscow's top priority is getting through the winter despite the threat of Ukrainian drone attacks on utility infrastructure, especially in border regions. Ukraine has this year struck Russian refineries, ports and warehouses, some deep inside Russia, and attacks on utilities are widely expected. Authorities are reportedly covering some Moscow power and heating plants with anti-drone nets, while residents are stocking up on generators and batteries.

Khusnullin told lawmakers that budget pressures complicate the response, since residents in many border regions are legally exempt from paying utility bills. Russia itself has resumed large-scale strikes on Ukraine's energy and heating systems, which Moscow says are legitimate military targets.

actors.why: Must defend utilities against drones while budgets and exemptions strain heating and power
Its drone campaign against Russian energy infrastructure is seen as a growing pressure point

impact_points: Russia faces winter risks to power and heating in border regions after Ukrainian drone strikes.
Russian households and budgets face strain from utility disruptions and unpaid bills in exempt border areas.

auto-f9d9aa523a89.headline: Ukraine claims hits on Russian aircraft and refineries as strikes intensify
auto-f9d9aa523a89.summary:
Ukraine says it damaged five Russian military aircraft, including three MiG-31s and two Su-34s, in a strike on the Savasleyka airfield about 300km east of Moscow. Kyiv said the full extent of the damage was still being assessed and did not specify the weapons used. Russia has not commented. Ukraine also said it hit two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region, where one person was reported killed and several towns lost power.

Meanwhile, Russian attacks across Ukraine have left people without electricity in five regions, including Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Odesa and Kharkiv, with at least five people reported killed. Ukrainian officials said the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost external power again, its 17th such loss this year.

actors.why: Lost aircraft and refinery output after Ukrainian strikes, with a fatality in Samara
Widespread power outages and deaths from Russian attacks across several regions

impact_points: Russia faces damage to military aircraft and oil refining capacity, with Moscow's fuel processing reportedly weakened by repeated strikes.
Ukraine suffers ongoing blackouts and deadly attacks, with repair work slowed by repeated strikes and air raid alerts.

auto-3e94e993d125.headline: Iran signals resilience against US blockade while tackling runaway inflation
auto-3e94e993d125.summary:
Iran's first vice president, Mohammad Reza Aref, said Tehran is not worried about the US naval blockade, pointing to a rise in goods moving through non-southern land borders. He gave no figures to back the claim of strong reserves. The government says it aims to hold basic goods prices steady for at least three months. Inflation is severe: consumer prices were 88.7% higher in October than a year earlier, and food and drink prices rose 112.6%, according to the Statistical Centre of Iran.

The blockade, reimposed by Washington in July and extended through the US Task Force Iron Gate to land borders and the Caspian Sea, is part of a wider confrontation. Iran's Foreign Ministry separately vowed to counter what it called American aggression by all available means, while the two sides trade accusations over Gulf attacks.

actors.why: Faces blockade, inflation above 88% and pressure on living standards
Uses naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate to squeeze Iranian revenue
Pressed to close crossings and police cross-border trade with Iran
Asked to close crossings and police cross-border trade under US pressure
Asked to close crossings and police cross-border trade under US pressure

impact_points: Iran faces its worst inflation in decades, with food costs sharply higher and living standards under strain.
Neighbouring states such as Iraq, Turkey and Pakistan are pressed to close crossings and police cross-border trade.

auto-b215b64f90cd.headline: Deported Salvadoran man leaves United States for Spain after legal fight
auto-b215b64f90cd.summary:
Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran man whose 2025 deportation to El Salvador was later admitted by the US government to be a mistake, arrived in Madrid after a commercial flight from the United States. He left voluntarily, saying he was leaving with his freedom, and his lawyers describe the move as temporary, with a hope to return once the current administration ends.

The US Department of Homeland Security called him a criminal and said he would never be allowed back, a claim his lawyers dispute as they say he denies the gang allegations. A judge had earlier dismissed the criminal charges against him, ruling they were politically motivated.

actors.why: Case exposes wrongful deportation and court defiance, drawing criticism of the administration's immigration policy
Deportation to its CECOT prison drew scrutiny over conditions and the threats he faced there
Receives Abrego Garcia as a new base, though details of his stay remain unclear

impact_points: The United States faces renewed scrutiny over its deportation policy and its compliance with court orders in this case.
Spain takes in Abrego Garcia, who plans to travel to other countries to speak about his experience and his dispute.

auto-0c5017a98763.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Russian vessels off eastern Libya, raising regional concerns
auto-0c5017a98763.summary:
Ukraine says its naval drones struck a Russian corvette and a Russian cargo ship over the weekend. The corvette was reportedly sunk while docked at Benghazi, in eastern Libya. Kyiv's security service is reported to be behind the attacks, which were said to target vessels on a Russian supply route through the Mediterranean.

Russia has built a presence in eastern Libya since about 2019, backing the forces of Khalifa Haftar, whose rival government is based in Tobruk. Analysts say the strikes could threaten Moscow's logistics links to Africa and draw the divided North African country into the wider war, with possible effects on European support for Ukraine.

actors.why: Corvette reportedly sunk and cargo ship hit, threatening its Libyan supply route
Strikes extend its reach far beyond the front lines, a notable operational gain
Divided country risks becoming a battleground between Moscow and Kyiv
Escalation could test European backing for Ukraine and regional security

impact_points: Russia loses naval assets and a key logistics route into Africa and the Mediterranean, according to analysts.
Libya risks being drawn into the Russia-Ukraine conflict, while European support for Ukraine could also come under strain.

auto-cb03e53fe444.headline: Yemen's government reports hundreds of strikes on Houthis as Aden threat grows
auto-cb03e53fe444.summary:
Yemen's government forces say they carried out 654 strikes against the Iran-aligned Houthis in a few hours, including air raids, drone and rocket attacks and artillery fire, claiming 109 Houthi fighters and commanders were killed or wounded. The military's spokesman, Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili, said the attacks destroyed or damaged 76 vehicles and other assets.

The strikes come as Houthi forces are reported to have advanced to about 60 kilometres from Aden, the temporary seat of the internationally recognised government. Officials say they will not take the city, though the government redeployed forces from Red Sea areas to defend it. The figures were issued by the government and could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Government reports heavy strikes but Houthi advances threaten Aden and the south
Backs the Yemeni government and faces Houthi strikes on oil targets and cities
Houthis, Iran-aligned, are fighting in a conflict tied to the wider US-Iran war

impact_points: Yemen's internationally recognised government faces mounting Houthi pressure around its temporary capital, Aden.
Saudi Arabia, which backs the government, is drawn further into a conflict with Houthi missile and drone attacks on its territory.

auto-e170c3774f80.headline: Poland plans eastern no-fly zone after Russian incursions near Ukraine border
auto-e170c3774f80.summary:
Poland's government plans to set up a no-fly zone along its eastern border with Ukraine, a deputy defence minister said on November 25, 2026. The zone would extend more than ten kilometres from the border, and officials want the regulation in force by late December or early January. The move follows incidents on November 23 and 24 in which Russian missiles and a drone entered Polish airspace during Russian attacks on Ukraine.

Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said the zone would let Polish pilots identify and, if needed, engage aerial targets using radar, allied intelligence, altitude and speed rather than visual confirmation. Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine at Kyiv's request could count as self-defence, while Warsaw also raised NATO interception of such missiles. Tomczyk said NATO was not supportive of that idea.

actors.why: Must tighten eastern airspace defence after Russian incursions and a planned no-fly zone
Faces a Polish plan to shoot down its missiles and aircraft near the border
Gains a neighbour's push to counter Russian missiles, though NATO interception remains unagreed
Faces a NATO eastern flank security concern from Russian airspace violations

impact_points: Poland faces heightened air security risks and must strengthen its eastern airspace defences along the Ukrainian border.
Russia faces a stronger Polish readiness to shoot down its aircraft and missiles entering NATO airspace.

auto-f0ef162893f6.headline: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Ras Tanura refinery as Saudi airstrikes hit Yemen
auto-f0ef162893f6.summary:
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, on the Gulf coast, causing fires. Satellite images showed thick black smoke over the site, while Saudi authorities said air defences had intercepted four drones in the area without confirming a strike. The Houthis framed the attack as retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen that reportedly killed dozens of civilians. Saudi Arabia responded with airstrikes in several Yemeni governorates and warned of a firm response to attacks on civilian targets.

The fighting, which resumed in July, has also seen Houthi projectiles hit Riyadh's financial district and the Red Sea port of Jazan, and has drawn in British military support for Riyadh.

actors.why: Refinery and Riyadh targeted, flights cancelled, events postponed, oil exports strained
Renewed civil war, airstrikes on Hodeidah and displacement of hundreds of thousands
Expanding military support and sanctions against the Houthis, deepening its Saudi partnership

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces damage to oil infrastructure, disrupted exports, and threats to its economic and investment image.
Yemen's civilians face displacement and disrupted vaccination, while the UK deepens its military backing for Riyadh.

auto-418cea236746.headline: Iran's Guards report tanker explosions in Hormuz amid rising shipping attacks
auto-418cea236746.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said several oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, reporting one vessel off the southern coast and others east of the strait. The Guards said the ships were under US military air escort and that the escort did not prevent the incidents, while warning that ships using unauthorised routes would be treated as violators. The claims could not be independently verified, and US Central Command had not responded. Maritime data cited in the coverage shows reported attacks in the wider area rose to their highest level since the conflict began in February.

actors.why: Guards assert control of strait and warn ships, drawing international scrutiny
Escorted tankers were hit despite US air cover, undermining its protection effort
Gulf shipping and energy exports face heightened risk from attacks in the strait
Gulf oil exporters are exposed to disruption from attacks near the strait

impact_points: Iran faces scrutiny as the Guards publicly claim responsibility for threats to commercial shipping in the strait.
Shipping companies and oil tanker operators face higher risks and must weigh US escorts against Iranian warnings.

auto-d5ef974f9e9a.headline: Saudi Aramco and S-OIL open $7bn Shaheen petrochemicals plant in South Korea
auto-d5ef974f9e9a.summary:
Saudi Aramco and its South Korean subsidiary S-OIL inaugurated the $7 billion Shaheen project at a ceremony in Seoul, attended by senior officials and business leaders from both countries. Aramco calls it its largest investment in South Korea. The complex includes the world's largest single steam cracker and uses Aramco's thermal crude to chemicals technology, developed with Lummus Technology. It is expected to add about 3.2 million tons of annual petrochemical capacity, with commercial operations planned for 2027.

The plant sits alongside S-OIL's existing facilities in Ulsan and is designed to supply feedstock to nearby companies through dedicated pipelines. Aramco's CEO said investment decisions remain firm despite economic headwinds and geopolitical risks.

actors.why: Gains a large petrochemical plant reducing import reliance in Ulsan
Aramco expands its downstream value chain and Asian investment footprint

impact_points: South Korea gains a major petrochemical plant that should reduce reliance on imports for nearby Ulsan companies.
Saudi Arabia's Aramco strengthens its downstream footprint in Asia and expands its partnership with S-OIL, which it majority owns.

auto-927751b5d70d.headline: Houthi strikes and threats hit Saudi Red Sea ports amid escalating Yemen fighting
auto-927751b5d70d.summary:
Yemen's Houthi group struck the Saudi Red Sea port of Jizan on Wednesday, causing minor damage with no civilian casualties, according to the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition also said it intercepted a drone over Jeddah's port and ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, following a Houthi drone strike on a Riyadh skyscraper that injured at least 11 people.

The Houthis warned that Jeddah and all other Saudi Red Sea ports would be targeted if Saudi Arabia attacked Yemen's Hodeidah port, which handles most of Yemen's imports. The coalition then struck targets at Hodeidah and in Saada and Amran, and officials said the strikes are part of a wider escalation across Yemen.

actors.why: Ports and Riyadh targeted by drones and missiles, with rising security costs
Hodeidah port strikes threaten food and aid imports for millions
Iran-aligned Houthis gain leverage in escalating confrontation with Saudi Arabia

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces rising attacks on ports, airports and cities, with at least 11 injured in Riyadh.
Yemen's civilians could lose vital food and aid if Hodeidah port is closed or damaged.

auto-4d9ef213f1e1.headline: Cambodia and China begin joint military drills
auto-4d9ef213f1e1.summary:
China and Cambodia have started a joint military exercise, which reports describe as the largest yet in the long-running Golden Dragon series. Cambodia is hosting Chinese forces for the drills.

The exercise is a bilateral training event between the two militaries. Coverage does not give a full list of participating units, and it does not specify the scope of activities beyond the joint training itself.

actors.why: Hosts the largest Golden Dragon drills, deepening military ties with China
Expands its military partnership and presence in Southeast Asia via Cambodia

impact_points: Cambodia deepens its military cooperation with China through hosting its largest Golden Dragon drills yet.
China strengthens its military footprint and partnership in Southeast Asia through the exercise with Cambodia.

auto-ffa6147695a3.headline: Kim Jong Un urges broader tactical nuclear arsenal as Pyongyang expels Swiss diplomat
auto-ffa6147695a3.summary:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, inspecting nuclear material and weapons research sites, said tactical nuclear weapons should be deployed across several military domains and that output of nuclear material is being steadily increased. He called the country's nuclear status untouchable despite international calls for denuclearisation. The facilities were not named in state media reports.

In a separate development, North Korea ordered the closure of the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang and expelled Swiss diplomat Sylvain Astier, giving him 48 hours to leave. Pyongyang tied the move to Swiss sanctions on a children's camp in Songdowon, which Switzerland linked to transfers of children from Russian-occupied Ukraine. Switzerland said it regretted the decision.

actors.why: Expands nuclear posture and expels Swiss diplomats, gaining defiance but facing isolation
Diplomatic office shut and envoy expelled over its sanctions, a clear setback
Faces a North Korea openly expanding tactical nuclear deployment, a growing security threat
Linked to Swiss sanctions over children from Russian-occupied Ukraine, a reputational concern
Swiss sanctions cite children transferred from Ukrainian territory under Russian occupation

impact_points: Switzerland loses its recently reopened diplomatic presence in Pyongyang and its envoy is being recalled to Beijing.
South Korea and regional neighbours face a North Korea signalling expanded tactical nuclear deployment and rejecting denuclearisation talks.

auto-79141548e3a9.headline: Jolie and Pitt settle court dispute over French vineyard stake sale
auto-79141548e3a9.summary: Actors Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt have settled their lawsuits over a stake in Château Miraval, the French winery they co-owned. Their representatives said in a joint statement that the deal was made out of court for the sake of their family, and no terms were disclosed. Pitt had sued Jolie after she sold her share to a company controlled by Russian oligarch Yuri Shefler, arguing she broke a pledge not to sell without consent. Jolie had countersued over alleged abusive conduct on a 2016 flight; Pitt denied those claims. Pitt's separate litigation with the Russian-linked Stoli Group is reported to be ongoing.

actors.why: Château Miraval winery in France; dispute resolved privately
Oligarch-controlled Stoli Group still in ongoing litigation with Pitt
Dispute between US celebrities settled; no state-level impact

impact_points: France hosts the winery at the centre of the dispute, which now stays out of the courts.
Russia-linked Stoli Group and its oligarch owner remain tied to the case through Pitt's ongoing litigation.

auto-42bca7e20b2d.headline: Islamist attack on Syrian security post in Hasakah kills two personnel
auto-42bca7e20b2d.summary: Two Syrian internal security personnel were killed and five others wounded when Islamic State fighters attacked a checkpoint in the Mushirfa area of Hasakah, in northeastern Syria, on Wednesday, according to local authorities and state media. Four attackers took part; two died in clashes with security forces and two detonated themselves, one using a booby-trapped motorcycle at the post's entrance. Officials said all four assailants were killed. The deputy governor vowed to identify those responsible. A UN report earlier this year said President Ahmed al-Sharaa and senior ministers had been targets of foiled Islamic State assassination plots.

actors.why: Security forces lost two personnel and five were wounded in a deliberate attack

impact_points: Syria's government faces continued Islamic State attacks on its security forces, particularly in the north and east.
Syrian internal security forces suffered fresh losses, while regional stability and public safety in Hasakah are under pressure.

auto-61c2742fede8.headline: Eisenkot's coalition bid faces setbacks as talks stall and partners split
auto-61c2742fede8.summary:
Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leading a bloc aiming to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, faces mounting coalition obstacles. After the inconclusive October 27 election, his Yashar party reached a deal with Avigdor Lieberman's Israel Our Home, but the left-wing Democrats suspended their talks with Yashar over its parallel negotiations with Netanyahu's Likud and ultra-Orthodox parties. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

The bloc won 48 seats against Netanyahu's 53 in the 120-seat Knesset, with Arab-led parties taking 19. Reports say Eisenkot's allies oppose a government backed by Arab parties, while talks with Likud and the haredi party United Torah Judaism continue.

actors.why: Coalition deadlock raises risk of another election and prolonged political uncertainty
Arab-led parties' 19 seats are excluded from potential governing arrangements

impact_points: Israel's political bloc opposing Netanyahu risks fracturing as the Democrats step back from talks.
Israel's Arab-led parties, now holding 19 seats, are sidelined by partners ruling out cooperation with them.

auto-27d8cba8360a.headline: Two men arrested after break-in at Norfolk home used by Prince William
auto-27d8cba8360a.summary: Police in Norfolk, eastern England, arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespass after a reported break-in at Anmer Hall on the Sandringham estate. The property belongs to Prince William and Catherine, who were not there at the time, and police said it was unoccupied. Officers used police dogs, drones and a helicopter after receiving a call about suspicious activity on Monday evening. The men remained in custody. The estate is owned by King Charles, and the couple occasionally stay at the house, particularly during school holidays.

actors.why: Royal property targeted in burglary; security scrutiny at a private royal residence

impact_points: The British royal family faces a security embarrassment at one of its private residences on the Sandringham estate.
Prince William and Catherine's property was targeted, though police reported no occupants were present during the incident.

auto-d128c63c7fc5.headline: US detonates degraded lead azide stockpile at Iowa plant despite public health concerns
auto-d128c63c7fc5.summary:
The US Army detonated about five tonnes of degraded lead azide, a volatile explosive, at its Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Wednesday morning. Officials said the controlled blast was preferable to a spontaneous explosion, and that airborne lead monitors showed no detection afterward, though surface sampling results were still pending. The operation had been delayed several times after public outcry and legal challenges, and a federal appeals court cleared it on Monday.

Residents were warned to stay indoors, and some nearby people faced possible evacuation. Illinois's governor reported little to no impact, while Iowa's incoming governor called for greater transparency about how the situation was handled.

actors.why: Army removed a volatile hazard, but faces criticism over transparency and communication
Reports little to no impact, but remains on standby near the border

impact_points: Residents of Middletown and nearby Iowa communities face continuing uncertainty about lead dust exposure until surface sampling results are released.
Illinois, only about 10 miles from the site, is monitoring for any unanticipated impact from the blast.

auto-664f2dc008f3.headline: China and Netherlands discuss stable supply chains and bilateral ties in Beijing
auto-664f2dc008f3.summary: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang met Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen in Beijing and called for joint work to keep industrial and supply chains stable and unobstructed. Ding described the relationship as open and pragmatic, and said it sets the pace for China-EU cooperation. Both sides pledged to strengthen high-level exchanges ahead of the 55th anniversary of ambassadorial relations next year. Berendsen praised China's hosting of the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen and said the Netherlands wants to resolve differences through dialogue.

actors.why: Secures stable supply chains and deeper high-level exchanges with a key European partner
Commits to deeper cooperation and dialogue-based handling of differences with China
Dutch-China ties are described as leading China-EU cooperation, so bloc relations are affected

impact_points: China gains a stronger channel to Dutch officials on trade and supply chains, which Beijing says it wants kept stable.
The Netherlands, and through it the European Union, gets a dialogue track on managing differences while deepening practical cooperation with China.

auto-2980f112c629.headline: US proposes new tariffs on Brazilian goods; Brasilia calls them unacceptable
auto-2980f112c629.summary: The United States has proposed new tariffs on Brazilian goods, including a 10% duty on finished aircraft that are currently exempt, and a new rate on out-of-quota sugar. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the changes would address practices Washington considers unreasonable and give it more leverage in talks. Brazil's government responded with outrage, calling the move a unilateral threat that undermines ongoing negotiations and vowing not to yield. The measures are part of a wider round of US tariffs covering more than a dozen trading partners, and Brazil was the first country targeted under this new strategy.

actors.why: Faces new US tariffs and pressure to change regulations; government calls it unacceptable.
Gains more leverage in trade talks, though US airlines may face costs for regional routes.

impact_points: Brazil faces pressure over Pix, digital trade and other disputed regulations, and has rejected all allegations.
Embraer could be hit hard by the aircraft duty, and US airlines serving smaller regional routes could face costs.

auto-51b79380da03.headline: Islamic State gunmen and suicide bombers strike Syrian security post in Hasakah
auto-51b79380da03.summary:
Four Islamic State militants attacked an internal security checkpoint in the Mushirfa neighbourhood of Hasakah, in northeastern Syria, on Wednesday. Syrian authorities said two security personnel were killed and five wounded. All four attackers died, two in clashes with security forces and two in suicide blasts, one of them on a booby-trapped motorcycle at the post's entrance.

The deputy governor of Hasakah vowed to identify those behind the attack. Officials said the group has since declared a new phase of operations against the government of President Ahmed al-Sharaa, and a UN report in February cited five foiled assassination plots against him and two senior ministers.

actors.why: Two security personnel killed and five wounded in an Islamic State attack on Hasakah post

auto-0f930007e283.headline: North Korea orders Swiss diplomat out and demands closure of Pyongyang office
auto-0f930007e283.summary: North Korea has declared the head of Switzerland's newly opened Pyongyang diplomatic office persona non grata and given him 48 hours to leave. Pyongyang also demanded the office close, in retaliation for Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp in Wonsan. auto-5bf936186606.headline: US unveils new proposed tariffs on 14 major trading partners
auto-5bf936186606.summary:
The United States has proposed a new round of tariffs on imports from 14 major trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, India and several Southeast Asian economies. The US Trade Representative announced the measures, which target what Washington describes as harmful industrial and trade practices. Rates range from 20 to 40 per cent, with China facing the highest, up to 40 per cent, and Vietnam up to 35 per cent. The duties are not expected to take effect until next year and must first pass a public consultation process.

The proposals follow a Supreme Court ruling that struck down earlier Liberation Day tariffs. Lower rates are available to countries that reach or already hold trade agreements with Washington. Officials in Brazil and the European Commission have pushed back, with the Commission saying it expects the 15 per cent ceiling agreed last year to be respected.
