auto-d142349fbc49.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners after court ruling
auto-d142349fbc49.summary:
The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union, arguing that excess production gives them an unfair trade advantage. The levies follow an eight-month investigation under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, launched after the Supreme Court struck down earlier sweeping global tariffs in February.

China faces the highest proposed rate at 20 percent, though about $30bn of its imports are excluded under a bilateral review mechanism. Beijing rejected the overcapacity claims, and the EU, Switzerland and Norway also pushed back or defended their practices. US stock indexes dipped and gold fell more than 3 percent on the news.

auto-ecd4445ebc7b.headline: Iran weighs force to break US naval blockade amid economic strain
auto-ecd4445ebc7b.summary:
Iranian officials are increasingly signalling that military options could be used to break the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, which was reimposed in July. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has reportedly directed officials to end the state of neither war nor peace with Washington, though talks remain deadlocked over Iran's conditions. Tehran's first vice president, Mohammad Reza Aref, said the government is not worried by the blockade, citing rising trade through non-southern borders, while Iran faces inflation of 88.7 percent in October.

Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei said Iran is determined to break the blockade and respond forcefully to any new aggression. The US has also launched Task Force Iron Gate to restrict movement across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Analysts warn that prolonged pressure could push Tehran toward confrontation.

Blockade and Task Force Iron Gate aim to pressure Iran's economy

auto-4f5e5b7c8501.headline: Iran says two tankers hit mines and burned in Hormuz
auto-4f5e5b7c8501.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy and the Iranian Army both say two oil tankers suffered explosions and fires after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels were said to have entered a restricted route east of the strait with their tracking and navigation systems switched off. Iran's army added that the strait would stay closed until Iran's objectives and demands are met, and that tanker owners must coordinate with the armed forces for safe passage. The claims come from Iranian officials and could not be independently verified.

auto-39a6e4165a8d.headline: Militants strike Syrian security checkpoint in Hasakah, killing two personnel
auto-39a6e4165a8d.summary:
Four gunmen attacked an Internal Security Forces checkpoint in the Mushirfa neighbourhood of Hasakah, northeastern Syria, on Wednesday. Local authorities said two security personnel were killed and five wounded. Two attackers died in clashes with security forces and two in suicide blasts, one on a booby-trapped motorcycle. The Islamic State group is blamed, and Syrian officials vowed to identify those responsible.

The attack fits a pattern cited by Syrian authorities and the UN, which say the group has pursued a campaign against government forces since declaring a new phase in February. Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has reportedly been the target of foiled assassination attempts.

auto-8372c769fece.headline: Beijing praises EU decision to delist a Chinese company from sanctions
auto-8372c769fece.summary:
China has welcomed a decision by the European Union to remove a Chinese company from its sanctions list. Beijing presented the move as a positive step and called for the bloc to continue correcting its approach toward Chinese firms.

The delisting is a small but notable easing of tensions over EU sanctions targeting entities linked to Russia's war effort. Coverage available for this story did not provide the company's name or full details of the reasons for its removal.

auto-738265812f32.headline: Major 2026 events: Venezuela raid, Iran war, Artemis II and more
auto-738265812f32.summary:
A year-end review of 2026 highlights several major developments. In January, US forces captured Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro in Caracas and flew him to New York to face charges, a move critics questioned legally. Later, a US-Israeli attack killed Iran's supreme leader, starting a war that spread across the Middle East; Iran responded by blockading the Strait of Hormuz, lifting oil prices. Other milestones included the Artemis II crewed Moon flyby, a deadly Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and the expanded World Cup in North America.

Separately, reporting on the Iran war says hundreds of US installations in the region have been damaged, with repair costs estimated at $9.4 billion, and European authorities have accused Iran of plotting attacks on their countries, which Tehran denies.

auto-226fb8cd99b3.headline: EU leaders gather in Brussels for divided talks on budget and Ukraine aid
auto-226fb8cd99b3.summary: EU leaders met in Brussels for a two-day summit focused on the bloc's next seven-year budget and a proposed 45 billion euro loan to Ukraine. European Council president António Costa offered a compromise budget that cuts 44 billion euros from an earlier plan, but diplomats expected no deal before the final summit of the year in December. Northern states favour a smaller budget focused on defence and competitiveness, while southern and eastern countries want to protect farming and poorer regions. Four states, Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, have resisted contributing to the Ukraine loan, prompting Germany to link the issues.

auto-e8c8d43f8305.headline: Paris backs Kyiv's strikes on Russian vessels off Libya
auto-e8c8d43f8305.summary: France's foreign minister, Jean-Noel Barrot, said Ukraine was within its right to self-defence when it struck two Russian ships in Libyan waters. A Russian warship sank in the drone attack over the weekend, and Libyan authorities said two of their soldiers died from wounds sustained in it. Ukraine has acknowledged carrying out the operation, which reportedly used sea drones, and Italy has raised concerns with Kyiv. Barrot placed blame on Moscow for widening the conflict, accusing President Vladimir Putin of attacking Ukraine and pressuring European unity.

auto-5636c82c2309.headline: Blast at Bangchak oil depot in eastern Bangkok prompts evacuation order
auto-5636c82c2309.summary: An explosion broke out at an oil depot in eastern Bangkok on Thursday, with flames and thick black smoke visible across the city's skyline. Officials in the Bang Na district urged nearby residents to leave the area immediately. No casualties had been reported in the immediate aftermath, and the cause of the blast had not been announced. The sprawling facility is operated by Thai energy company Bangchak Corporation.

auto-9f7dc1199f78.headline: Solomon Islands and Australia sign security treaty barring foreign bases
auto-9f7dc1199f78.summary:
The Solomon Islands and Australia signed a broad bilateral treaty in Canberra, with Prime Minister Matthew Wale and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese presenting it as a new chapter in relations. The agreement names Australia the islands' primary security partner, states there will be no foreign military or security base on Solomon soil, and keeps sensitive infrastructure free from militarisation and foreign interference. Australia will commit A$740 million over a decade to education, sports and other programs.

The deal is widely seen as a setback to China, which signed a 2022 security pact with the islands. Reports said Honiara had told Beijing it would not renew that pact, which expires in 2027, but Wale said talks with China were ongoing and could not discuss details because of a non-disclosure clause. China's foreign ministry did not confirm the termination and warned that cooperation should not target third parties.

auto-c416e4154dd2.headline: Eisenkot's coalition talks with the Democrats resume after a brief suspension
auto-c416e4154dd2.summary:
Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot said he had settled a dispute with the left-wing Democrats, whose suspension of talks had threatened his effort to form a government and unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He said negotiations with the Democrats had restarted and that marathon talks on a coalition deal would continue. The October 27 election left neither bloc with a majority, and Eisenkot's bloc holds 48 of 120 seats. He faces a December 6 deadline, with a possible 14-day extension.

Eisenkot's bloc still needs partners, and Avigdor Lieberman's party has signalled openness to a government with a Jewish majority that includes the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism. Any such deal would likely require a compromise on drafting ultra-Orthodox seminary students into the military.

auto-b34565162f92.summary: An explosion struck the Bangchak oil depot in eastern Bangkok on Thursday, sending a fireball and thick black smoke over the Thai capital. Authorities said seven people were hurt, four of them in critical condition, and urged nearby residents and students to evacuate. Bangchak Corporation said a fire started around 2:45 pm local time and was extinguished by 3:15, with production units shut down. The cause is under investigation. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the situation appeared under control and that it was too early to assign blame.

auto-f546f01c44f5.headline: Ukrainian strikes push Russian refinery output to multi-decade low
auto-f546f01c44f5.summary:
Russian oil refining has dropped to its lowest level in more than two decades, according to analysts at Rystad Energy, as Ukrainian drone and missile attacks continue. By late November, output was estimated at roughly 2.6 to 2.7 million barrels a day, about half the late-October level. Bloomberg counts at least 18 Russian refineries hit since late October.

The strikes have hit Russia's domestic fuel market, with weekly retail petrol prices rising 0.5 percent, the largest weekly jump since early September. Ukraine's General Staff also confirmed attacks on the Kuibyshev and Syzran refineries in Samara Oblast, saying it acted with a Russian resistance group. Vladimir Putin has warned of retaliation.

auto-a74c431800b9.summary:
A Russian Shahed drone hit a high-rise residential building in Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district early on 26 November, killing two people, according to Mayor Ihor Terekhov. Three others were injured, and people were reported to be possibly trapped under the rubble.

Separately, Samara Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said Ukrainian drones killed one person in the Samara region overnight, with air defences downing more than 145 drones. auto-7173b273aa25.headline: Seoul urges calm with Moscow after Russian bombers near its air zone
auto-7173b273aa25.summary:
South Korea's defense minister, Kang Shin-chul, called for efforts to ease tensions with Russia after Russian military aircraft entered Seoul's air defense identification zone over the East Sea. Two Tu-160 strategic bombers and two other jets reportedly came within about 1 kilometer of the airspace above Ulleung Island, prompting South Korean fighter scrambles. Seoul lodged a strong protest with Moscow's military attache, while Kang said the flight did not appear intentional but asked for advance notice of future military flights.

auto-a55dbbe3cede.headline: Abrego Garcia leaves US for Spain after long deportation dispute
auto-a55dbbe3cede.summary:

Local residents and the Astra channel reported explosions and a hit on a nearby thermal power plant that supplies the plant, but these reports could not be independently confirmed. Russian forces fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv late on Wednesday, striking a shopping centre and two other buildings on the east bank of the Dnipro River, with residents told to stay in shelters, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. auto-78629004d95e.headline: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to meet in Islamabad on their defence pact
auto-78629004d95e.summary:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey are set to hold a meeting in Islamabad on Friday and Saturday to discuss their mutual defence agreement, two Pakistani sources told Reuters. The Islamabad government has also declared a local holiday in the capital on November 27, though no official reason was given. The Rawalpindi-Islamabad metro is partly closing from November 26 to 28 due to expected VIP movement.

auto-48934003af60.headline: Riyadh skyscraper hit by Houthi drone; Gulf and other states condemn attack
auto-48934003af60.summary:
A Houthi drone attack struck the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Tuesday, wounding at least 11 people, including Saudi, Indian, Nepali and Egyptian nationals, according to Saudi authorities. The tower, home to the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund, was hit for the second time in less than a week. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen called it a terrorist attack and vowed a firm response.

The GCC secretary-general condemned the strike as an act of aggression, and Qatar, the UAE, Kuwait, Pakistan and the United States also denounced it. Separately, Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemned a deadly attack on a Syrian security forces site in Al-Hasakah.

Regional Gulf states and Pakistan warn the attacks heighten tensions and threaten efforts to restore peace in the region.

auto-292c6fa2e8cd.headline: Israeli soldiers describe using detained Palestinians as human shields in Gaza
auto-292c6fa2e8cd.summary:
Testimonies broadcast by Israel's public channel Kan describe Israeli soldiers forcing detained Palestinians, including a 16-year-old boy, to search buildings and tunnels ahead of troops in Gaza. Soldiers described the practice as the "Mosquito Protocol", and the United Nations said in June 2025 it had verified cases involving 27 Palestinian boys. Israel's defence minister called for the broadcast to be censored, warning of legal risks abroad.

Separately, the Israeli military is investigating 16 cases of human shield use, 10 in Gaza and six in the occupied West Bank, according to Haaretz, with fresh testimony suggesting the practice also occurred in Lebanon. The military says the practice is prohibited.

actors.why: Military faces investigations, legal risks abroad and accusations over human shield use
Palestinian detainees were forced to act as human shields, including children
Testimony suggests Israeli troops used human shields in Lebanon operations

impact_points: Palestinians detained in Gaza and the West Bank face forced use as human shields, a practice prohibited under international humanitarian law.
Israel's military faces criminal investigations and possible legal exposure abroad, while officials seek to suppress the broadcast.

auto-07127867dc1c.headline: Houthi strikes target Saudi ports and Riyadh after coalition hits Hodeidah
auto-07127867dc1c.summary:
Yemen's Houthi rebels say they struck Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, and Saudi officials report intercepting several drones over the kingdom's east, including at the Ras Tanura refinery. The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government said it had hit operational targets at the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah, and a Houthi drone wounded 11 people at a Riyadh tower housing the sovereign wealth fund. The coalition reported only minor damage and no casualties at Jazan.

The Houthis framed the port attacks as retaliation for the Hodeidah strike, while Qatar, Pakistan and India condemned the Riyadh attack. Fighting between the two sides has escalated since July, and Hodeidah is a key entry point for food and aid.

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces attacks on energy, port and capital infrastructure, testing its air defences.

auto-7fd57e6f8ae0.headline: North Korea orders Swiss diplomatic office closed after sanctions dispute
auto-7fd57e6f8ae0.summary:
North Korea has ordered Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang to close and told its head to leave within 48 hours. The move follows Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp, which Western governments accuse of helping indoctrinate Ukrainian children taken from Russian-occupied areas. Pyongyang called the sanctions a hostile act that violated its sovereignty.

Bern said it regretted the decision and would bring the office head back to its embassy in Beijing, insisting the closure does not end diplomatic relations. The office had been reopened only weeks earlier by Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis during a rare visit.

actors.why: Expelled diplomat and lost Pyongyang office, though relations formally continue
Pushed back against sanctions it sees as sovereignty violations, expelling Swiss envoy
North Korea's closeness to Moscow is highlighted amid Ukraine-related sanctions
Swiss diplomatic head to return to Beijing embassy, which covers North Korea

impact_points: Switzerland loses its newly reopened diplomatic foothold in Pyongyang, one of few Western channels to North Korea.
North Korea faces Western sanctions pressure over its ties to Russia's war in Ukraine and child transfers.

auto-28008798c5cf.headline: Poland to set up no-fly zone along Ukrainian border after Russian incursions
auto-28008798c5cf.summary:
Poland plans to create a no-fly zone in its east, along the border with Ukraine, after Russian missiles and a drone entered its airspace during attacks on Ukraine on November 23 and 24. Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said the zone would extend more than ten kilometres from the border and that the decree should take effect in late December or early January.

The measure would back a new procedure letting Polish pilots identify and engage aerial targets using radar, allied intelligence, altitude and speed rather than visual confirmation. Polish officials also raised the idea of NATO intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine, though reports say NATO has not supported it and no decision has been made.

actors.why: Faces repeated Russian airspace violations and must expand air defence measures
Russian strikes continue; Polish interception support could help protect Ukrainian cities
Its missiles and drones are entering NATO airspace, drawing a tougher Polish response
NATO eastern flank security concerns affect the wider European alliance

impact_points: Poland faces growing risk from Russian aerial incursions and must tighten its airspace defences.
Ukraine could gain if NATO allies agree to intercept Russian missiles over its territory.

auto-e0b14cf0ff38.headline: Kushner praises Putin in interview as US-Russia peace talks stall
auto-e0b14cf0ff38.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner, a key negotiator on Ukraine, described Russian President Vladimir Putin as a skilled political strategist and a historic figure in a podcast interview with Axel Springer chief Mathias Döpfner. Kushner said Putin wants peace and a new relationship with America, and credited him with agreeing not to use nuclear weapons. He also said Putin is not interested in an immediate ceasefire and that talks on ending the war have reached an impasse over territory. Critics note Kushner's remarks echo Kremlin narratives, and reporting from Kyiv highlights continued Russian missile strikes on Ukrainian cities the same day.

actors.why: Peace talks stalled over territory while Russian strikes continue killing civilians
US envoy publicly praises Putin and accepts Kremlin framing, easing diplomatic pressure
Envoy's praise of Putin contrasts with Russia's support for Iran and rejection of ceasefire

impact_points: Ukraine faces stalled peace talks and continued Russian strikes despite Washington's mediation efforts.
Washington's negotiating posture toward Moscow draws scrutiny, and Russia gains a sympathetic US voice in talks.

auto-2a71a4ca65c8.headline: Iraqi court sentences 11 over oil smuggling in national crackdown
auto-2a71a4ca65c8.summary: An Iraqi Central Criminal Court has sentenced 11 people to 15 years in prison each under the country's anti-terrorism law for smuggling oil. The convictions form part of a wider nationwide campaign against illegal oil trade, ordered by Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi, who has called for tougher measures. Reports also note other recent smuggling operations uncovered by security services. Iraq relies heavily on oil revenue, and smuggling routes linked to Iran have been highlighted as a target of the crackdown.

actors.why: Crackdown strengthens state control over oil revenue and enforcement against smugglers
Targeted smuggling routes reportedly linked to Iran could reduce cross-border trade

impact_points: Iraq's government is tightening enforcement against oil smuggling, which costs the state revenue and fuels illicit trade.
Iran may feel pressure as Iraqi action targets smuggling routes that reportedly connect to its territory.

auto-cb641dfdd724.headline: Two Italian workers die in Kuwait as Iranian drone debris falls
auto-cb641dfdd724.summary:
Two Italian workers were killed in Kuwait when fragments from intercepted Iranian drones fell on the ground, according to Kuwait's Defence Ministry. The drones had been aimed at a vital site that the ministry did not name. Two other people, a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, were also hurt. Italian news agency Ansa reported that the dead were employees of the German arms maker Rheinmetall.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed deep sorrow for the deaths and offered condolences to the families of the victims. The reports cited here do not confirm the Italians' identities beyond the agency account.

Iranian drone attack on a vital site caused deaths and damage

impact_points: Italy is facing the deaths of two of its citizens working in Kuwait, prompting condolences from its prime minister.
Kuwait and Germany's Rheinmetall are affected, as the attack hit a site in Kuwait and killed employees of a German firm.

auto-27b62652db42.headline: Bangladesh police disperse garment workers blocking highway over minimum wage
auto-27b62652db42.summary: Police in Bangladesh used tear gas and stun grenades to break up garment workers who tried to block a major highway, demanding higher pay. The protest came a day after a government-appointed wage board approved a 36% rise in the garment minimum wage, the smallest increase in four decades, despite calls for it to be doubled. Protesters also set fire to a police motorcycle in Gazipur, a key garment hub, and police said calm had since returned, though they remain on alert. Weeks of protests have closed factories and disrupted production in a sector employing over four million people.

actors.why: Factories shut and production disrupted; wage deal fails to calm unrest, fuelling instability
Sheikh Hasina's exile in India is tied to wider political tensions in Bangladesh

impact_points: Bangladesh's garment sector, a major exporter, faces renewed instability and disrupted production from prolonged worker unrest.
Garment workers, who labour advocates say will not earn a living wage under the new rate, remain dissatisfied and mobilised.

auto-4f8ee8b38430.headline: Trump urges Putin to halt military action across Europe
auto-4f8ee8b38430.summary: US President Donald Trump said he pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin during their recent meeting in China to end military aggression across European territories. He framed this as a way to help reach a quick deal between Russia and Ukraine, which he described as possible. The remarks follow Russian missiles and drones entering Polish airspace during strikes on Ukraine on November 23 and 24. Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte also called on Russia to avoid actions that could widen the war. The Kremlin, through spokesman Dmitry Peskov, placed blame on Ukraine for any escalation.

auto-63a9b3e0b747.headline: Iranian drone debris kills two Italians at Kuwaiti site
auto-63a9b3e0b747.summary:
Two Italian nationals died after Iranian drones were intercepted over Kuwait, Kuwait's Defence Ministry said. The drones were aimed at a facility it called vital, and falling debris caused the deaths and damage. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were also injured and taken to hospital. The Gulf Cooperation Council condemned the attack, backed Kuwait's right to defend itself, and held Tehran responsible.

The incident comes amid wider Gulf attacks, including Houthi missile and drone strikes on Saudi targets. Riyadh's coalition said a refinery at Jazan was hit and vowed a firm response.

Italy loses two citizens, while Gulf states face rising regional tension and possible wider conflict escalation.

auto-492ce0251128.headline: Iowa blast destroys US lead azide stockpile; early air tests show no lead
auto-492ce0251128.summary:
The US Army carried out a controlled detonation of its entire stockpile of lead azide, about 4.5 tonnes, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Wednesday. Earthen barriers and foam and water were used to contain the blast. Officials said the explosion appeared not to spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms, and Environmental Protection Agency air monitors detected no airborne lead. The army said the explosive was degrading and could detonate unpredictably as temperatures fell, so it moved quickly.

Some experts cautioned that it is too early to judge the risk, and government agencies and independent researchers plan extensive testing for lead in water, soil, farms, homes and playgrounds in the coming weeks. Residents and environmental groups had raised concerns over health risks and a lack of information before the blast, and a lawsuit had sought to halt it.

actors.why: Army removed a hazardous stockpile, but testing and transparency concerns remain unresolved

impact_points: Residents of Middletown and nearby Iowa communities face possible lead contamination, pending the results of environmental testing.
Children and pregnant women near the site are most vulnerable if lead dust has spread, according to health guidance on lead exposure.

auto-c3d671fa4611.headline: Baghdad's push for Kurdish oilfields and borders draws rival party condemnation
auto-c3d671fa4611.summary: Iraq's two main Kurdish parties, the KDP and PUK, set aside their rivalry to denounce Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's directives to bring Kurdistan Region oilfields and border crossings under federal control. They called the moves a breach of constitutional rights, and KRG Prime Minister Masrour Barzani described them as unacceptable. Thousands of Kurds protested in Erbil and Duhok, while Iraq's top court ruled that Baghdad may deploy federal forces along all international borders, including in the Kurdistan Region. Zaidi's government also accuses an Iran-aligned militia of smuggling, adding a separate standoff.

actors.why: Federal government gains oil and border control, though implementation may prove difficult

impact_points: Iraqi Kurdistan Region faces loss of control over oilfields and border crossings to Baghdad.
Baghdad gains leverage over oil revenue and security, but faces entrenched resistance and implementation hurdles.

auto-058b80fcea92.headline: Kushner blames stalled Ukraine peace talks on alleged strike on Putin residence
auto-058b80fcea92.summary:
US envoy Jared Kushner told a podcast interview that Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations lost momentum after an alleged Ukrainian attack on Vladimir Putin's residence in Valdai in late December 2025. Kushner said the talks had since reached a deadlock over territory. Ukraine has called the claim a lie, and US intelligence reportedly concluded that no attack on the residence occurred, though Ukrainian drones may have targeted a military site nearby.

Separately, the Kremlin accused Kyiv of spreading the war into the Mediterranean and Baltic seas after Ukrainian strikes on Russian vessels. Libya, Italy and Norway urged caution, and Trump and NATO's Mark Rutte called on Russia to avoid widening the conflict.

auto-500f76833db9.headline: Reported Russian nuclear satellite raises fears of a space detonation
auto-500f76833db9.summary:
German broadcasters and a newspaper, citing western intelligence assessments, report that Russia may launch a nuclear-enabled satellite called Sputnik-S within about 60 days. The satellite is said to have been assembled years ago and kept near Moscow. A German government spokesperson said the reports were being taken very seriously.

Experts explain that a nuclear blast in space releases energy as radiation rather than a mushroom cloud. In low Earth orbit, where most satellites operate, X-rays could disable spacecraft across thousands of miles, and trapped particles could last for years. Analysts recall the 1962 US Starfish Prime test, which damaged satellites and disrupted Hawaii.

actors.why: Germany is taking intelligence on the satellite very seriously, facing security concerns.
Reported satellite plans could raise pressure and isolation for Russia over space threats.
Starlink, which supports Ukraine's defence, could be disrupted by a space detonation.
The US faces risks to its satellites and military systems, citing its 1962 test precedent.

impact_points: Western countries and their satellite operators face risks to weather, military and communications networks in low Earth orbit.
Ukraine could lose access to Starlink broadband, which supports its defence against Russia's invasion.

auto-f2226b4e7c41.headline: Drone strike in West Kordofan kills 11 civilians, Sudan's war escalates
auto-f2226b4e7c41.summary: A drone struck a truck carrying passengers and goods in Ghubeish, West Kordofan, killing at least 11 people and wounding nine, a local medical source said. The town is held by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, which blamed the Sudanese army; the army's response was not reported. Separately, drone strikes on Damazin and Roseires in Blue Nile state reportedly killed around 19 civilians, according to Emergency Lawyers, a rights group, and disrupted power facilities. UN estimates say drone attacks killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of the year.

actors.why: Civilians killed by drones in two states; power infrastructure damaged amid civil war

impact_points: Sudan's civilians face mounting deaths as both army and RSF rely heavily on drone strikes.
Power supplies and the national grid in Blue Nile state are at risk after strikes on the Roseires dam and facilities.

auto-bf501395815c.headline: Turkey says Ukrainian strikes on Russian ships off Libya breach international law
auto-bf501395815c.summary:
Ukraine carried out drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libyan waters off Benghazi over the weekend, sinking a Russian warship. Libya says two of its soldiers died from wounds sustained in the attack. Turkey's Defence Ministry said the strikes are illegal under international law because hostile acts in a neutral state's waters are prohibited, and called on warring parties to spare civilian ships. Libya has taken the matter to the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

France's foreign minister, Jean-Noel Barrot, defended Ukraine's action as self-defence against Russia's ongoing strikes, while Italy has voiced concern to Kyiv. Ukraine's foreign minister has called the attack legitimate.

auto-4302fe1d9007.headline: Russian drone strike on Donetsk post office kills one, injures three
auto-4302fe1d9007.summary:
A Russian drone struck a post office in Bylbasivka, in Donetsk Oblast, on the evening of 25 November, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service. A woman was killed and three other people were injured, and a fire spread over about 350 square metres before firefighters contained it. Firefighting was halted because of the risk of further attacks and heavy drone activity in the area.

The same night, Russia launched ballistic missiles and drones at Ukraine, with Kyiv hit by a missile attack on a shopping centre and other buildings, injuring seven people, according to local authorities. Ukraine's Air Force said it downed or suppressed most of the drones it tracked.

auto-8c33472c6a18.headline: US Army destroys aging lead azide stockpile in Iowa, testing begins
auto-8c33472c6a18.summary:
The US Army carried out a controlled open-air detonation of nearly 4,500 kg of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Wednesday morning. Officials said the explosive had become unstable after roughly 20 years in storage and risked detonating on its own as temperatures fell. The blast was preceded by mitigation steps such as misting and foam, but residents worried about lead dust spreading over homes, farms and livestock across southeastern Iowa and northern Missouri.

The Environmental Protection Agency reported zero airborne lead at monitors after the blast, and more than 1,000 samples are being analysed, with results expected within 24 to 48 hours. Officials have said early readings are promising, though some local leaders have called for fuller transparency.

actors.why: Army disposed of unstable stockpile, though sparked public health controversy and legal challenges

Northern Missouri sits within projected dust plume and was advised to shelter

impact_points: Iowa and Missouri farmers face soil and livestock testing while awaiting lead sample results.
Residents of Des Moines County, many on lower incomes, face disrupted routines and lingering health concerns.

auto-c27684c70d3e.headline: Mexico requests airspace talks with US over SpaceX launch debris
auto-c27684c70d3e.summary:
Mexico's government wants meetings with US aviation authorities about rocket launches from SpaceX's Starbase site in Texas, near the Gulf of Mexico. President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico is seeking a discussion on permission to use Mexican airspace, how frequently launches might occur, and whether the launch site should be moved. Mexican officials earlier recovered debris that washed ashore in Tamaulipas after a failed Starship flight, and environmental authorities plan to ask SpaceX to take it back. SpaceX disputes that the material came from its launch and says it has found little debris on the beach.

The dispute comes as SpaceX seeks US approval to sharply expand launches at Starbase, from 25 to 456 a year.

Must review SpaceX expansion and coordinate airspace talks with Mexico

impact_points: Mexico faces environmental and airspace risks from SpaceX debris and possible expanded launch activity near its border.

auto-1b8f6e34f71b.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia is finishing preparations for a new mass attack on Ukraine, citing intelligence that targets include energy and logistics infrastructure and other life support facilities. The warning followed a meeting on power supply, which described severe outages in Dnipro, Pavlohrad and surrounding areas, with repairs ongoing. Separately, overnight Russian strikes hit energy and industrial sites in Zhytomyr and Poltava oblasts, injuring one person in Zhytomyr. Zelensky also said Patriot air defence deliveries from the United States remain delayed.

auto-3bcab66a4ef5.headline: Settlers damage Palestinian family's homes in Jaloud despite court order
auto-3bcab66a4ef5.summary:
Israeli settlers used a bulldozer to break the concrete foundations of two Palestinian family homes in Jaloud, near Nablus in the occupied West Bank, in the early hours of Thursday. Security cameras recorded the attack, which came after settlers had blocked the Tubasi family from returning, despite a court order requiring the military to remove them. The family says it was forced out months earlier after repeated attacks, arson and cut utilities.

The Israeli military condemned the incident as a serious criminal act and said it was investigating, though settlers were still in the area during the day. Lawyers and rights groups say such cases rarely lead to charges, and UN figures show an average of 53 settler attacks a week in 2026.

auto-2ba6be5483ea.headline: Houthi drones target Saudi sites after coalition strikes Hodeidah port
auto-2ba6be5483ea.summary: Saudi Arabia says its air defences intercepted several Houthi drones over its Eastern Province, including near the Ras Tanura oil terminal, with no casualties in the initial assessment. The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government had struck the rebel-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah, a key entry point for food and aid, and hit targets in Saada and Amran. The Houthis, who had earlier struck a tower in Riyadh and injured at least 11 people, threatened Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah and Yanbu. The coalition promised a firm response to attacks on civilian infrastructure.

auto-512d6f9f17ee.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence agency says North Korea has temporarily paused part of its military cooperation with Russia, including deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery shells. auto-e2be1453f165.headline: Russian strikes hit Ukrainian cities and energy sites as Kyiv targets Russian refineries
auto-e2be1453f165.summary:
Russian forces launched missiles and scores of drones at Ukraine overnight, damaging energy sites and civilian areas. Kyiv's mayor said a missile wounded seven people in an industrial zone, while a drone strike on a Kharkiv apartment block killed two. Officials reported deaths and injuries across several regions, plus power cuts in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia.

auto-28352a3779a2.headline: Andalusian politics hints at how Spain's national vote could favour the right
auto-28352a3779a2.summary:
Ahead of a snap national vote, the southern region of Andalusia is being watched as a possible preview of Spain's political future. Since a May regional election, it has been run by a coalition of the conservative People's Party and the far-right Vox, which has gained ground by focusing on migration. Opinion polls put the PP first, the Socialists second and Vox third, with the two right-wing parties together likely to have enough seats to govern. PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo has reportedly preferred a minority government backed by Vox, though he has not ruled out a coalition.

Observers note that the PP opened the door to Vox in Andalusia in 2018, which they say helped normalise the party's stance on migration. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has framed the vote as a contest between progress and regression, while Vox and the PP are expected to draw votes from one another.

actors.why: Snap election could hand the right-wing bloc power, ending Sanchez's Socialist-led government

impact_points: Spain's Socialists under Pedro Sanchez face losing power to a right-wing bloc backed by Vox.
Spain's migrant population and its immigration policy could shift sharply if Vox gains influence in national government.

auto-599eede677a3.headline: US export curbs push Nvidia to halt server shipments to Southeast Asia
auto-599eede677a3.summary: Nvidia has reportedly told manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to people familiar with the matter. The move follows new US export rules aimed at blocking Chinese firms from reaching advanced chips by renting cloud capacity in the region. It is unclear whether the halt is temporary, and cloud providers face a 90-day window to obtain licences. Malaysia's booming data centre sector, which has drawn heavy investment from US and Chinese firms, is among the areas exposed to the disruption.

auto-44d93eae4c2a.headline: Russia and Ukraine swap fallen soldiers' bodies via Belarus
auto-44d93eae4c2a.summary:
Russia and Ukraine have exchanged the bodies of fallen soldiers in Belarus, according to reports carried under the headline on this exchange. The article texts provided do not include details on the number of bodies, the exact date, or the handover arrangements, so these could not be confirmed from the reporting.

The same reporting cluster also covers Ukraine's General Staff claims of Russian losses over the course of the full-scale invasion, and Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko's denial that he knew in advance of a 2022 Russian push toward Kyiv through Belarusian territory.

Belarus gains a visible mediating role between Moscow and Kyiv, while its own 2022 role is contested by Lukashenko's denials.

auto-62ebe3db5e6d.headline: Russian drone strike on Donetsk Oblast post office kills one, injures three
auto-62ebe3db5e6d.summary:
A Russian drone struck a post office in Bylbasivka, in Donetsk Oblast, on the evening of 25 November, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service. One woman was killed and three other people were injured, and a fire spread over about 350 square metres. Firefighters brought the blaze under control, but they had to stop work because of the risk of further attacks and heavy drone activity.

The attack came as Russia hit Ukrainian cities with ballistic missiles and drones overnight, including Kyiv, where seven people were hurt. In Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia, a Moscow-installed governor said a Ukrainian drone attack killed five people.

impact_points: Ukraine faces further civilian casualties and damage from Russian drone and missile attacks across its frontline and major cities.
Russia-occupied Zaporizhzhia reports deaths from Ukrainian drone strikes, with Moscow-installed officials blaming Kyiv for the casualties.

auto-4ede51124cbc.headline: Australia imposes financing sanctions on two men tied to Iran-directed arson
auto-4ede51124cbc.summary:
Australia has placed counterterrorism financing sanctions on Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad, whom Foreign Minister Penny Wong says orchestrated 2024 arson attacks on a kosher restaurant in Sydney and the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne on Iran's behalf. The measures restrict the pair's access to funds and aim to curb their ability to recruit, plan and carry out attacks. Authorities say the attacks used a chain of proxies. Tehran has denied the allegations, and the men's contact details could not be determined.

The sanctions follow Canberra's August 2025 decision to expel Iran's ambassador, the first such expulsion since World War Two, suspend operations at its Tehran embassy and list the Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organisation.

auto-c0d983aec20d.headline: Power cut at Zaporizhzhia plant prompts UN push for local repair ceasefire
auto-c0d983aec20d.summary:
Russian strikes have cut power across several Ukrainian regions, including Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa and Kharkiv, according to Ukraine's energy ministry. Repairs are under way but repeated attacks and air-raid alerts are slowing the work, and rolling outage schedules apply across most of the country.

The Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost both external power lines and switched to diesel generators, the 28th such loss since the conflict began, per the UN nuclear watchdog. The IAEA said the outage was reportedly caused by military activity, while Russian plant operators blamed protective devices. The IAEA is working with both sides to arrange a local ceasefire for repairs.

Placeholder not used

auto-7b9b78fe501a.headline: China trials civilian-ship floating bridge for Taiwan-facing landing drill
auto-7b9b78fe501a.summary: China is running a weeks-long amphibious landing exercise in Dacheng Bay, Fujian province, across from Taiwan, according to satellite images and a report by geospatial firm ingeniSPACE. Eight civilian vessels were linked into a floating bridge about 800 metres long, which was assembled and dismantled between November 1 and 16. A senior Chinese security official said the drill aimed to practise seizing small islands and was aimed at contingencies along the first island chain. China's defence ministry did not respond to a request for comment, calling its training legitimate. Taiwan's defence ministry said it was assessing the implications for regional security.

auto-17dd72e80b2c.headline: North Korea orders Swiss diplomatic envoy out and seeks office closure
auto-17dd72e80b2c.summary:
North Korea's foreign ministry declared the head of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang persona non grata and gave him 48 hours to leave, state media KCNA reported. The move came a day after Kim Yo-jong threatened the closure. Pyongyang reacted to Swiss sanctions imposed on Songdowon International Children's Camp over alleged involvement in the transfer of Ukrainian children from occupied territories. Switzerland reopened its Pyongyang office as a diplomatic mission in October, after operating a humanitarian office from 1997.

The ministry summoned the Swiss office head and handed him a memorandum calling for the office's closure, calling the sanctions an open hostile act. Pyongyang said violations of its sovereignty would never be welcomed.

Russia and North Korea face Western pressure over alleged deportation of Ukrainian children, which Pyongyang rejects.

auto-ab6a96600a82.headline: US war funding fight over Iran conflict deepens ahead of Congress changeover
auto-ab6a96600a82.summary:
Democrats, who will control both houses of Congress from January, are pressing to halt funding for the nine-month conflict with Iran, which has pushed up food and fuel prices. Lawmakers face a December 11 deadline to pass a funding bill and avoid a government shutdown, and critics say a bill could curb offensive operations, though a veto and a Senate 60-vote threshold complicate passage.

President Donald Trump says his administration has enough money to keep fighting until late January and claims Iran's military has been largely destroyed. NBC News reported officials are weighing further strikes, including targeting senior Iranian leaders. The US embassy in Jerusalem has warned Americans in the region of possible Houthi and Iranian attacks.

actors.why: Faces funding fight, shutdown risk and divided politics over the war

Iranian attacks on US sites in Bahrain raise security threats
Iranian attacks on US sites in Kuwait raise security threats

Iran and Gulf states risk renewed strikes and retaliatory attacks if Washington escalates the war.

auto-a521fbc8d342.headline: Eisenkot's Yashar signs preliminary coalition pact with Democrats
auto-a521fbc8d342.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party agreed a preliminary coalition deal with Yair Golan's left-leaning Democrats in Israel on Thursday, strengthening his effort to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Democrats would receive four ministries, including a expanded national security post now held by Itamar Ben-Gvir, plus labour, communications, and culture and sport. Eisenkot has until December 6, extendable by 14 days, to form a government after the October election gave neither bloc a majority.

The combined bloc still falls well short of the 61 seats needed. Talks with Lieberman's Israel Beiteinu and Bennett's Beyachad remain unfinished, and the Democrats had earlier pressed for an alliance with Arab-majority lists.

actors.why: Opposition nears a government, but the bloc still lacks a parliamentary majority

impact_points: Israel's opposition moves closer to ousting Netanyahu, though its coalition remains short of a majority.
The Democrats gain four ministries, shifting Israel's security and social policy away from the far-right.

auto-5728ca1a0790.headline: Iran urges South Korea to avoid widening Gulf military role
auto-5728ca1a0790.summary:
Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araqchi, told his South Korean counterpart, Cho Hyun, in a phone call that foreign military deployments in the Gulf region would raise tensions and widen conflict. Cho reportedly reaffirmed that Seoul does not intend to join any war or send troops to the Gulf, according to the Iranian embassy in Seoul, which posted the account on X.

South Korea's parliament is reviewing a government plan to extend the operating area of its Cheonghae naval unit, now based in the Gulf of Aden since 2009, to the outer Gulf of Oman to protect commercial shipping. Seoul says the mission is to safeguard its citizens and economic interests, and about 70 percent of its 2025 oil came from the Middle East, mostly through the Strait of Hormuz.

actors.why: Seeks to protect oil imports and citizens by expanding naval patrols
Opposes foreign naval presence it sees as escalating regional tensions

impact_points: South Korea faces tension with Iran over a naval expansion meant to protect its oil and commercial shipping.
Iran would see the deployment as escalation, while energy-dependent South Korea relies heavily on Hormuz transit routes.

auto-e5a9373d1977.headline: Russian drones strike two Kharkiv districts, injuring three people
auto-e5a9373d1977.summary:
Russian drones struck the Shevchenkivskyi and Kyivskyi districts of Kharkiv on the morning of 27 November, according to Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv Oblast military administration, and Mayor Ihor Terekhov. Officials said one drone hit a petrol station, and that as of 08:10 three people had sought medical attention. Terekhov also reported a further strike in the Kyivskyi district around 07:50. The reports describe early figures that may change.

The attacks come amid wider Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities as winter approaches, including a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv overnight that injured seven people and hit energy and commercial sites.

Drone strikes on Ukrainian cities continue as winter pressure grows

impact_points: Ukraine faces civilian injuries and damage to fuel infrastructure in Kharkiv as Russian drone attacks continue.

auto-d75a5fe36cf4.headline: Ukraine reports 110 drones downed in overnight Russian attack
auto-d75a5fe36cf4.summary:
Ukraine's Air Force says Russian forces launched 155 attack drones, including decoys, at the country from the evening of 26 November. By 08:00 the next morning, air defences had destroyed or jammed 110 drones, among them 51 jet-powered Shahed models. Hits were recorded at 27 locations and debris fell at four others, and the attack was still ongoing at that time.

Separately, presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said on 25 November that a Ukrainian laser weapon, Blysk, had intercepted a Russian jet-powered Geran drone in combat for the first time while guarding critical infrastructure. He cautioned that serial production was not yet near.

Ukraine's private air defence groups and new laser systems are being tested as cheaper ways to counter Russian drones.

auto-aedafa9ae085.headline: Turkey finalises ratification of Saudi-Pakistan-Turkish mutual defence pact
auto-aedafa9ae085.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has formally approved a mutual defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, completing Turkey's ratification after parliament approved it on November 5. Under the pact, an attack on any one member counts as an attack on all three. The pact was signed in August amid concern over the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, and Turkey's approval paves the way for military support to Riyadh against Houthi attacks from Yemen. Pakistan is hosting a two-day meeting of the alliance's decision-making committee in Islamabad, where officials say Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Houthis will be on the agenda.

auto-8fb80889e131.headline: Ukrainian drone barrage hits Russian cities, airfield and refineries
auto-8fb80889e131.summary:
Ukraine launched a wave of long-range drone strikes against Russian territory, according to Russian officials and Ukrainian military statements. Russian governors reported drone debris and explosions in St. Petersburg, Novorossiysk and the Tula region, where three people were injured in Novorossiysk and flights were halted at Pulkovo Airport. Russia also reported that one person was killed in Samara, where Ukraine says it hit two oil refineries.

Kyiv's General Staff said it damaged five Russian military aircraft at the Savasleyka airfield in Nizhny Novgorod region, a claim Moscow has not commented on. Ukraine also said it struck a radar system and fuel depots in occupied Ukrainian territory. Russian attacks on Ukraine meanwhile caused power outages across five regions.

auto-2b200010bf03.headline: US proposes 25% tariffs on India, cut to 17% if a deal is signed
auto-2b200010bf03.summary: The US Trade Representative has proposed a net tariff of 25% on Indian goods, which would fall to 17% if Washington and New Delhi sign a bilateral trade agreement. The measures are not final: public comments are open until January 5, 2027, with hearings from January 25. Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the deal is close to completion and differences are narrowing, while exporters and trade experts urged New Delhi to accept only a balanced, reciprocal agreement. The proposed rates largely return tariffs to levels seen at the start of negotiations.

auto-bd75b711b163.headline: Ukraine's strike on Russian ships in Benghazi draws Italian rebuke
auto-bd75b711b163.summary:
Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette and a cargo ship in Benghazi port in eastern Libya using maritime drones, and says the action targeted Russia's military rather than Libya. Libyan authorities condemned the attack, and two Libyan army personnel reportedly died, with the Libyan National Army promising a response.

Italy's foreign minister said Rome had no prior knowledge of the operation and that Ukraine was wrong to violate Libyan sovereignty. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned that the war must not spread to the Mediterranean, while the Kremlin called the move very dangerous.

auto-4ee16ef492c3.headline: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to meet in Islamabad on mutual defence pact
auto-4ee16ef492c3.summary: Pakistan is hosting defence and diplomatic officials from Saudi Arabia and Turkey in Islamabad on November 27 and 28 to review their trilateral defence agreement, signed in Mecca in August. auto-7d736dfd9584.headline: US reportedly urged Venezuela and Iraq to weigh exiting OPEC
auto-7d736dfd9584.summary: According to ten people familiar with the matter, the Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC earlier this year and blocked Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues. auto-cd2738338ebe.headline: Unidentified drone briefly enters Latvian airspace, triggering alerts and jet response
auto-cd2738338ebe.summary:
An unidentified drone briefly entered Latvian airspace in the early hours of Friday, according to the Latvian National Armed Forces. Air-raid style alerts were issued for Ludza Municipality, with an orange alert at 02:30, and a lower-level yellow alert for neighbouring Balvi Municipality. NATO Baltic Air Policing jets were scrambled, and Latvian forces launched an interceptor drone, which returned to base after the flight. Both alerts were lifted within about an hour.

The military warned that similar incursions could recur while Russia's war against Ukraine continues. The incident came as Ukrainian drones attacked Russia's Leningrad region, where the governor said more than 40 drones were downed. Poland had earlier accused Moscow of a similar border violation.

auto-5011ac708627.headline: Trump defends calling Putin a friend as Kushner praises Kremlin leader
auto-5011ac708627.summary: US President Donald Trump said he describes Russian leader Vladimir Putin as a friend because he wants to secure a deal to end the war in Ukraine, arguing that open hostility would make progress harder. auto-ea0310454e80.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and EU
auto-ea0310454e80.summary:
The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners, among them China, the European Union, India and Japan. The measures, aimed at what Washington calls excess manufacturing capacity, could reach up to 20 percent, with China facing the joint-highest proposed rate. Officials said the tariffs could take effect in January at the earliest and are still at the proposal stage, with a public comment period to follow.

The EU rejected the premise that it contributes to structural overcapacity and said it expects Washington to honour a 2025 deal capping duties on the bloc at 15 percent. The proposals follow a Supreme Court ruling in February that struck down earlier across-the-board tariffs, and come as consumer prices rise ahead of the G20 summit in Miami in December.

auto-187c42e858db.headline: Britain contacts about 100,000 veterans as NATO threat concerns grow
auto-187c42e858db.summary:
Britain's armed forces have written to roughly 100,000 former personnel who form the strategic reserve, asking them to update their contact details and listing any new skills. The step, described as the first of its kind since the Cold War, is aimed at improving preparedness and deterrence. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the country is operating in a heightened threat environment and called the readiness measure a sensible precaution. Officials stressed the letters do not mean reservists are about to be mobilised, and some veterans may be asked to return only in exceptional circumstances.

The move follows concern about Russian aggression in Europe since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Veterans may volunteer for exercises such as NATO's Steadfast Defender next spring. auto-18cf31e73b74.headline: Mossad chief reportedly favours Israeli strike on Iran even without US support
auto-18cf31e73b74.summary:
Roman Gofman, head of Israel's Mossad, has reportedly backed a unilateral Israeli attack on Iran if needed, even without American participation, echoing outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. auto-35cf5a1950f3.headline: Gunmen kill 13 Nigerien soldiers in Sanam, near Mali border
auto-35cf5a1950f3.summary: Attackers struck a National Guard compound in Sanam, western Niger, before dawn on Thursday, killing at least 13 soldiers and wounding 20, according to the Defence Ministry. The ministry called it a terrorist attack by numerous heavily armed assailants, said troops killed several attackers, and said operations to find the perpetrators are ongoing. auto-7f2b85e7cfb9.headline: Iranian navy says it retook two tankers seized by US forces
auto-7f2b85e7cfb9.summary:
Iran's navy commander, Rear Admiral Shahram Irani, said Iranian commandos recovered two tankers and their equipment from US naval personnel during the recent 40-day conflict he called the Ramadan War. Speaking at Friday prayers in Tehran, he also accused Washington of charging shipowners millions of dollars for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz without accepting liability when vessels were attacked. These claims were made by Iranian officials and could not be independently verified.

Irani said Iran would keep the Strait of Hormuz closed on the orders of its leader, and that US efforts to force ships through had failed. The remarks come amid heightened tensions over the waterway, a key route for global energy shipments.

auto-3e5b28d40b4a.headline: Spain's election could reshape its tense relations with Morocco
auto-3e5b28d40b4a.summary:
Spain holds a general election on November 29, called after parliament rejected the government's housing decrees. Foreign policy is also weighing on the campaign, above all relations with Morocco, which involve Ceuta and Melilla, irregular migration and Western Sahara. A poll cited by Al Jazeera found Morocco-related issues were the top international concern for voters. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has taken a cautious line toward Rabat, while the far-right Vox has promised to review ties. Analysts note that campaign pledges often soften once parties hold power.

auto-e62fb3104381.headline: Sabotage against European infrastructure rises as Russia's hybrid campaign continues
auto-e62fb3104381.summary:
A report from the International Institute for Strategic Studies says Russia has stepped up unconventional tactics against European countries, including sabotage, reconnaissance and intimidation. Sabotage attacks on European infrastructure rose 16 percent in the year to September 2026, with arson and explosives use roughly doubling. Incidents include a drone attack on a German airport and attacks on energy sites and defence manufacturers.

auto-15e9ba95b41d.headline: US backs Iraqi premier's push for state control over weapons and oil
auto-15e9ba95b41d.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Washington supports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's drive to extend central government authority across Iraq. Trump's Truth Social post named the goals as ending oil smuggling, fighting corruption and placing all weapons under state control. The statement came as Baghdad treated crude sold outside the state marketer SOMO as smuggling, a government spokesman said. He claimed Iraq lost an estimated $100 billion to such smuggling through the Kurdistan region between 2008 and 2025, though the method behind that figure was unclear.

The moves have put Baghdad at odds with Iran-aligned militias and Kurdish authorities. Iraq closed two border crossings in Kurdistan, one with Syria and one with Iran, and Kurdish protests followed. auto-2e1f12870136.headline: Reported Saudi strike in Yemen's Taiz kills civilians, unverified
auto-2e1f12870136.summary:
Houthi-affiliated media reported that Saudi air strikes killed 11 civilians, most of them children, in al-Turbah, south of Taiz city in Yemen. Rescuers reportedly recovered eight bodies, with three people still missing under rubble. Al Jazeera said it could not independently verify the claims, and the Saudi-led coalition did not immediately comment, though it later said it destroyed a Houthi drone aimed at Riyadh.

The reports come amid renewed fighting between Houthi forces and Saudi-backed government troops since July, which escalated as the US war on Iran intensified. The World Health Organization says over 13,000 people have been killed or injured since August, and aid groups warn of worsening hunger and displacement.

auto-e44f3dfa2288.headline: Kyiv says Pyongyang paused some arms supplies to Moscow after diplomatic rift
auto-e44f3dfa2288.summary:
Ukraine's military intelligence agency said North Korea has temporarily suspended some military cooperation with Russia, including deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery shells. The agency linked the pause to a dispute that began in October, after a Russian deputy foreign minister said the Kremlin would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang. North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui reportedly called such statements inconsistent with the alliance. The claims come from Ukraine and could not be independently verified.

Separately, Ukraine's energy sector has been hit hard by Russian strikes, with more than 1,000 attacks since September. Following a major attack on 20 November, Ukraine halted electricity exports entirely by 22 November, while imports rose sharply, mostly from Hungary.

Possible loss of North Korean missiles and shells amid a diplomatic rift

Main supplier of Ukraine's imported electricity, benefiting from higher demand

North Korea loses a rare source of hard currency, despite heavy international sanctions, if the suspension lasts.

auto-ce04dcc567c7.headline: Israeli minister threatens mass displacement in Gaza if Hamas refuses disarmament
auto-ce04dcc567c7.summary:
Israel's defence minister Israel Katz has threatened a new offensive in Gaza and the forced displacement of about one million Palestinians southward, unless Hamas disarms. He posted the warning on X, saying Israel already controls around 70 percent of the territory and that Hamas's hold on the rest is an illusion. Aid and rights groups have previously described mass displacement of this kind as possible war crimes.

The threat came as overnight Israeli strikes killed eight Palestinians in Gaza City and central Gaza, according to local medical officials, and Israel said it killed Khaled Abu Nada, a senior Hamas figure. The threats come despite a ceasefire in place since October 2025, under which Hamas agreed in principle to hand over its weapons, a step Israel says has not yet been carried out.

Threats risk international criticism over displacement, though Israel frames it as pressure on Hamas
Neighbouring Egypt borders Gaza and could face pressure from a mass influx of displaced people
Threats threaten the Trump-backed ceasefire and Board of Peace disarmament plan it brokered

impact_points: Palestinians in Gaza, around one million civilians, face the risk of forced displacement and renewed fighting.
Hamas is under pressure to disarm or face military action, while the ceasefire framework is put at risk.

auto-7d7fca3cded7.headline: Trump plays down Russian and Chinese backing for Iran, citing ongoing US war
auto-7d7fca3cded7.summary: US President Donald Trump, speaking by phone to troops over Thanksgiving and in remarks at his Florida residence, said Iran could threaten Israel and other regional states with nuclear weapons without peace in the Middle East. He claimed Iran has missiles able to reach Europe and minimised reports that Russia and China shared intelligence that helped Tehran target US bases, saying Beijing's involvement would mean military action. Iran has stepped up attacks on US targets across the region, and Kuwait said an Iranian drone strike killed two Italian workers, which Tehran denies.

actors.why: Troops face Iranian attacks; administration pursues war and pressure on Tehran
Faces renewed US threats and strikes, though offered a negotiating opening
Accused of intelligence sharing with Iran, but Trump downplays it
Accused of intelligence sharing with Iran, but Trump downplays it
Trump says he spoke with Netanyahu; Israel faces the threat of Iranian nuclear attacks
A drone attack on a vital site killed two Italian workers

Iran faces renewed US threats of strikes while Trump says it still has a chance to negotiate a deal.

auto-dd9c2fa93508.headline: US Army destroys lead azide stockpile in Iowa; early tests show no airborne lead
auto-dd9c2fa93508.summary:
The US Army detonated its entire stockpile of lead azide, roughly five tons used in explosives, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Wednesday. Earthen barriers and foam and water were used to contain the blast, and officials said the initial air readings from the Environmental Protection Agency detected no airborne lead. The Army described the operation as a success, and the Federal Emergency Management Agency issued an all-clear around the plant.

The Army said the material was degrading and could explode unpredictably as colder weather arrived, which drove the timing. Researchers cautioned that lab results on samples would take days to weeks, and residents and farmers remain concerned about possible lead exposure.

actors.why: Army removed a degrading explosives stockpile, but health concerns and testing continue.
No direct involvement reported.

impact_points: Iowa and neighbouring Missouri residents, farms and livestock face lingering lead-testing uncertainty while samples are analysed.
Illinois and Mississippi River communities are monitoring water supplies, with officials saying no impact has been seen so far.

auto-254957af0977.headline: Norwegian long-haul carrier Norse Atlantic's unit enters bankruptcy amid fuel crisis
auto-254957af0977.summary:
Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit has filed for bankruptcy, the long-haul budget airline said, after warning that its finances were critical and suspending all flights. The company, founded in 2021, cited soaring fuel costs linked to the conflict involving Iran. Its parent listed company and other group units are not part of the filing and are still trying to continue operating. Reports also said lessors had moved to terminate leases on its 12 aircraft, a claim the company disputed.

The collapse is part of a wider strain on the aviation sector, which faces its toughest period since the Covid-19 pandemic. Pakistan International Airlines, a wet-lease partner, said it would move its UK flights to its own fleet after Norse's sudden suspension.

actors.why: Norwegian unit bankrupt; parent listing and group firms still trying to operate
Partner airline PIA must move UK flights to its own fleet
AerCap, an Ireland-based lessor, faces recovering leased Dreamliners
Singapore-based BOC Aviation faces losses on leased Dreamliners
Flights from London and Manchester cancelled after Norse suspended operations
Conflict with the US drove up fuel costs that hurt the airline sector

impact_points: Pakistan International Airlines faces disruption to UK routes and must shift operations to its own fleet.
Norse's lessors, including AerCap and BOC Aviation, must recover aircraft and handle the terminated leases.

auto-8f6af8d9e84d.headline: Fire at Bangkok refinery injures seven and halts production
auto-8f6af8d9e84d.summary: A fire broke out on Thursday afternoon at the Phra Khanong oil refinery in Bangkok, owned by Thai energy firm Bangchak Corp. The blaze, which started around 2:45 p.m. local time, was brought under control about half an hour later, according to the company. Emergency services reported at least seven people hurt, four of them seriously. Bangchak has shut all production units at the site, which has a capacity of 120,000 barrels per day, and says the cause is under investigation. Witnesses nearby described a blast and a column of black smoke over the city.

actors.why: Industrial fire disrupts a major domestic refinery and injures several people.

impact_points: Thailand's domestic fuel supply could tighten, since Bangchak runs two refineries with about 300,000 barrels daily.
Bangchak faces losses from halted output and injured workers, while investigators examine what caused the blaze.

auto-d2d61fb0126b.headline: UK revokes Bahraini broadcaster's licence over Houthi leader's October 7 speech
auto-d2d61fb0126b.summary:
Britain's media regulator Ofcom has removed the UK broadcasting licence of Lualua TV, a Bahrain-based channel. The decision followed a broadcast of a speech by Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi that praised the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. Ofcom also said the channel had produced antisemitic content.

The move marks a regulatory action against a foreign broadcaster for content aired to UK audiences, and it comes amid wider regional tensions linked to the Gaza war and Houthi operations.

actors.why: Regulator Ofcom acts to enforce broadcasting standards against extremist content
Bahrain-based Lualua TV loses its UK licence and reach
Houthi leader's speech is removed from UK broadcast channels
Coverage of the October 7 attacks in Gaza's context is condemned as praise

impact_points: The UK loses a Houthi-linked broadcaster from its licensed airwaves, following Ofcom's action against Lualua TV.
Bahrain's broadcaster faces the loss of UK reach, while Gaza-linked propaganda and antisemitic content face tighter scrutiny.

auto-63c782239b30.headline: Moscow prolongs jet fuel export restrictions through March 2027
auto-63c782239b30.summary: Russia's government has extended its ban on jet fuel exports, now running from 1 December until 31 March 2027. The earlier embargo, imposed in June, was due to lapse at the end of November. Officials cite the need to keep domestic supply reliable after Ukrainian drone strikes on oil refineries, which have pushed refining output to its lowest level in more than two decades. Exemptions cover intergovernmental agreements, humanitarian shipments, military supplies and some official uses. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has described the domestic fuel market as tense and said Russia is importing fuel to cover a deficit.

actors.why: Ukrainian strikes strain fuel supply, forcing export bans and imports
Drone attacks on Russian refineries continue to disrupt Russian energy output

impact_points: Russia's domestic fuel market faces continued shortages while major refineries remain under repair after drone attacks.
Airlines and fuel buyers outside Russia may see reduced access to Russian jet fuel through the coming months.

auto-a3d71fc3b0d9.headline: Uganda plans to pull troops from Lubero as Kinshasa row deepens
auto-a3d71fc3b0d9.summary: Uganda's army has said it will withdraw its forces from Lubero, a town in North Kivu province in eastern DR Congo, within about two weeks, handing security to Congolese troops. The move follows Kinshasa's summoning of Uganda's top diplomat over social media posts by Ugandan army chief Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, which included remarks about taking the mineral-rich town of Walikale. Uganda gave no reason for the withdrawal and did not say whether it was linked to the dispute. The army also accused militias, some apparently allied with Kinshasa, of attacking civilians.

actors.why: Withdrawing troops from Lubero amid strained ties and a diplomatic row with Kinshasa
Must assume security in Lubero while rebel fighting and civilian attacks continue

impact_points: Uganda's troops end nearly two years of operations in Lubero, though the wider joint campaign continues elsewhere.
The Congolese government faces renewed fighting with rebels in Lubero and must now take over security there.

auto-7ab8e6d7c076.headline: Ukrainian units destroy hidden Russian fuel depot in occupied Luhansk region
auto-7ab8e6d7c076.summary:
Ukraine's 1st National Guard Corps, known as Azov, says its forces destroyed a concealed underground fuel depot in occupied Luhansk Oblast, along with its supporting infrastructure. The corps said Russian troops stored fuel in hidden tanks in a forest, delivered by train and then trucked to front-line units, and protected the site with electronic warfare and mobile fire groups. Azov released a video of the operation but did not give a date or its duration, so the timing could not be independently confirmed.

The corps also said Ukrainian forces had earlier hit Russian oil depots and logistics sites in occupied Donetsk Oblast. Separately, a large Russian ballistic missile and drone attack overnight struck Kyiv, injuring seven people, according to local authorities.

actors.why: Strike on Russian fuel logistics, while Kyiv was also hit by missiles
Lost a hidden fuel depot supplying front-line troops in Luhansk

impact_points: Russian forces in occupied Luhansk Oblast lose a fuel supply point used to sustain their units.
Ukraine gains a logistics strike against Russian supply lines, though Azov's account has not been independently verified.

auto-330e6f68340b.headline: Kyiv says Russia is building a second military satellite network
auto-330e6f68340b.summary:
Ukraine's military intelligence says Russia is developing Innoset, a new military satellite communications network built by Geoscan of St Petersburg, alongside the Rassvet low-Earth orbit system. Officials cited by Ukrainian outlets say Russia plans 240 Innoset satellites by 2036 and 924 Rassvet satellites by 2035. Ukraine warns the networks could let Moscow guide weapons far beyond the Black Sea, which it calls a global threat.

Separately, Ukrainian intelligence says North Korea has temporarily suspended military aid to Russia after a diplomatic dispute over Moscow's approach to Seoul. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed these claims, which Kyiv says were prompted by a Russian remark about easing tensions with South Korea.

actors.why: Building new military satellite networks and relying heavily on North Korean arms supplies
Reportedly halting arms and troop support to Russia over a diplomatic dispute
Faces threat from expanded Russian military satellite communications for strikes
Seoul is the subject of the Russia-North Korea dispute and sees ongoing military cooperation as a concern

impact_points: Ukraine and Europe face a possible new global threat if Russia's satellite networks reach full deployment.
North Korea faces a diplomatic rift with Russia, which may reduce its supply role and bargaining position.

auto-b34e9ea0bb0d.headline: Italy says it was kept in the dark over Ukrainian strike in Libya
auto-b34e9ea0bb0d.summary:
Italy's foreign minister Antonio Tajani told parliament that Rome had no advance knowledge of a Ukrainian sea-drone attack on a Russian warship and a cargo vessel at the Libyan port of Benghazi. He said Italy opposed the decision and considers violating Libyan sovereignty a mistake, while still backing Kyiv. Libya's rival authorities condemned the strike, and Ukraine says its targets were Russian military assets and that it has no intention of extending the war to Libya.

Kyiv said the warship and cargo ship carried military equipment and were legitimate targets. Libya's eastern forces reported two naval personnel killed, and the Kremlin accused Ukraine of spreading the conflict into the Mediterranean.

Libya risks being drawn into the Russia-Ukraine war, which could further destabilise its already divided government.

auto-2197e95b5719.headline: China rehearses floating-bridge landing method near Taiwan in Fujian drill
auto-2197e95b5719.summary:
China is running a weeks-long amphibious landing exercise in Dacheng Bay, Fujian Province, directly across from Taiwan. Satellite imagery and a report by the geospatial firm ingeniSPACE show the People's Liberation Army linking civilian vessels into a floating bridge roughly 800 metres long, which it assembled and dismantled between November 1 and 16.

A senior security official confirmed the drill is ongoing and said it aims to practise seizing small islands along the first island chain, which stretches from Japan through Taiwan to the Philippines. Beijing called its training legitimate, while Taiwan's defence ministry said it was weighing the security implications. Officials cautioned against overstating the battlefield value of improvised barges.

actors.why: Faces a rehearsed landing method aimed at nearby coastline, raising threat pressure

Japan and the Philippines are implicated, since the drills target contingencies along the first island chain.

auto-95a08e1e300c.headline: US strikes disables Palau-flagged cargo ship trying to leave Iran's Bandar Abbas
auto-95a08e1e300c.summary:
US Central Command said a Palau-flagged commercial ship, the M/V Pacific Archer, was disabled in the Gulf of Oman on November 26 after its crew tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran. The ship had left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas, and US military aircraft fired precision munitions that hit its stern, disabling its propulsion. The civilian crew was not hurt, the military said.

The incident adds to US efforts to enforce the blockade of Iran, which the military says the vessel's crew was warned about before the strike.

Flag state of the disabled ship, whose vessel was struck by US forces

Palau-flagged shipping and its crews face risks when attempting to transit blockaded Iranian waters.

auto-4849e7119a8a.headline: Spain rushes to contain possible oil leak after tanker sinks near Ibiza
auto-4849e7119a8a.summary: Spanish authorities moved quickly to limit possible environmental damage after a Maltese-flagged tanker carrying diesel and refined products sank off Ibiza in the early hours of Thursday, 26 November. Reports say the vessel held up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel, and one crew member died in hospital after 17 others were rescued. The cause of the sinking was unclear, and officials said activating a marine pollution mechanism did not mean pollution had yet been detected. The area is seen as ecologically sensitive, with protected zones and endangered seabirds, so tourism and marine life could be at risk.
