auto-535e081108b0.headline: Ukraine reports strikes on Russian fuel and missile-linked sites as peace talks stall
auto-535e081108b0.summary:
Ukraine's General Staff said its forces, working with a resistance group inside Russia, struck the Efremov Synthetic Rubber Plant in Tula Oblast, a supplier of components for Iskander missile fuel, and the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov Oblast. Separately, US envoy Jared Kushner said peace talks stalled after an alleged Ukrainian attack on Vladimir Putin's residence in late December, which US intelligence and President Trump have questioned. Kushner said the territorial issue is now the main deadlock.

Kyiv also said nine more Ukrainian children were returned from Russian-held areas through the mediation of Melania Trump, and reported that US speed limits on Starshield satellite communications are hampering its strike drones over occupied territory.

Strikes on Russian sites and children's return, but drone losses and US friction

Ukraine faces strained ties with Washington over Starshield restrictions and a stalled negotiation track led by US envoys.

auto-eb103fe39f76.headline: Spain heads to snap election with right-wing alliance prospects
auto-eb103fe39f76.summary:
Spain is holding a snap general election on Sunday after eight years of Socialist-led government under Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Opinion polls put the conservative People's Party (PP) first, followed by Sánchez's Socialists, with the far-right Vox third. The PP is not expected to win an outright majority, but the two right-wing parties together could have enough seats to govern.

PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has reportedly said he would prefer a minority government backed by Vox, while leaving open a coalition. Coverage points to Andalusia, where a PP-Vox coalition has governed since May, as a possible preview. Vox has campaigned against migration, a theme that resonates with some voters.

actors.why: Snap election could end Socialist rule and bring far-right influence into government

impact_points: Spain's Socialists under Pedro Sánchez face losing power after eight years in government.
The conservative PP could depend on Vox, a far-right party, to form a national government.

auto-05b1e0bb1a5f.headline: Kyiv's foreign minister urges Europe to act quickly on Ukraine funding
auto-05b1e0bb1a5f.summary:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke at a joint press conference in Kyiv with Alain Berset, Secretary General of the Council of Europe. He argued that Ukraine's front line also defends European security, so backing Kyiv is a question of Europe's own protection. He warned that postponing decisions could later cost European states far more to defend their own territory.

Sybiha said Russia is trying to split Europe from the United States and to divide European Union members from one another, and called for united, collective responses. He also asked partners to weigh the case for Ukraine's macro-financial support, noting that Russia has raised its war budget and that Ukraine must match it proportionately.

auto-0c384f1a8a9d.headline: Kyiv endures nightly strikes and blackouts as Ukrainians vow to fight on
auto-0c384f1a8a9d.summary: Russia has been launching missiles and drones at Kyiv in large numbers, following a mid-November exchange in which Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea and Russia hit two of the Dnipro River's bridges in Kyiv. Attacks on the power grid leave much of the city dark at night, and water supply is unreliable. A KIIS poll found 62% of Ukrainians willing to endure the war as long as needed, with 79% expecting Ukraine to prevail in the long run. Residents face another difficult winter of strikes, power cuts and rising food prices.

auto-b615ddd38f2e.headline: Indonesia and EU trade deal advances as US tariff proposals loom
auto-b615ddd38f2e.summary:
The European Union and Indonesia signed a trade deal in Brussels after roughly a decade of talks. Indonesia's economy minister, Airlangga Hartarto, said the agreement could lift bilateral trade by 50% within three years and that US tariff negotiations had played a part in closing it. Separately, Washington proposed new tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners, including the EU and Indonesia, which the EU said it strongly rejects.

The minister also expects Indonesia's New Asia Forum in Bali to produce investment deals worth up to $30 billion, and says Indonesia is aiming to join the OECD by 2028. Two EU measures take effect around the turn of the year: the deforestation regulation from 30 December and Indonesia's exit from the EU's GSP scheme on 1 January.

auto-ef58b1db22b8.headline: Russian convoy heading to Libya turns back after Benghazi warship sinking
auto-ef58b1db22b8.summary:
A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles to Libya has reportedly turned around in the Mediterranean, according to three people from military and security services who spoke to Reuters. The move followed an attack on November 22 at the Benghazi naval base, where a Russian corvette, the Merkury, was sunk. Libya's eastern-based government blamed a suspected drone attack, and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said the target was Russian; the convoy's diversion was not officially confirmed by Moscow, whose defence ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

The vessels were reportedly bound for Libya, with the cargo possibly intended for Russia's Africa Corps in West Africa or for forces loyal to Khalifa Haftar. The convoy was last tracked near Algeria, and its next destination remains unclear.

Libya's eastern authorities and Haftar's forces may lose a planned Russian equipment delivery, while the Africa Corps' supply line is disrupted.

auto-df98c68d5530.headline: Trump endorses Iraqi premier's push to curb oil smuggling and central control
auto-df98c68d5530.summary: US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's campaign against oil smuggling and his effort to bring armed groups under state control. Baghdad has moved to place Kurdistan's border crossings and several oil fields under federal authority, closing two crossings, one with Syria and one with Iran, and a court ruling allowed federal forces along all international borders. Kurdish officials rejected the federal moves as a violation of constitutional rights, though they say they do not want clashes. Iraq's oil minister says it will not tolerate exports outside legal channels. Analysts say the moves align with US pressure on Iran, which Iraqi and Kurdish sides both see as a major source of tension.

actors.why: Gains federal control of borders and oil, but risks Kurdish conflict

Gains an ally backing its Iran policy and oil investment goals

Iran faces loss of smuggling routes and pressure from the US economic blockade, which weakens its access to Iraqi crude.

auto-950386e601e7.headline: Canadian petition urging removal of US ambassador Hoekstra tabled in parliament
auto-950386e601e7.summary:
A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians asking Ottawa to declare US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra persona non grata was formally presented to the House of Commons. Green Party MP Elizabeth May, who opened the petition in July, accused him of repeated abusive and insulting remarks about Canadians and of interfering in domestic affairs. The US State Department had not responded to a request for comment.

The petition is non-binding, and May expects the government to decline the request. She said she hopes the signatures will signal support for Canada's government in its dealings with the Trump administration.

impact_points: Canada faces pressure over its relations with Washington as the petition highlights strained ties with the US ambassador.
The US embassy and Ambassador Hoekstra face political backlash in Canada over comments on tariffs, the midterms and annexation.

auto-25bd74a83c1d.headline: Eisenkot says Likud stalling Israeli coalition talks ahead of deadline
auto-25bd74a83c1d.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, has accused Likud, the party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, of stalling coalition talks in an effort to force new elections. He was tasked by Israel's president with forming a government after the October 27 vote, which produced no majority for either bloc. He has until December 6, with a possible 14-day extension.

Yashar has agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats and Israel Beiteinu, but the combined 36 seats remain short of the 61 needed. Likud says it remains open to a unity government, while Eisenkot says he is still willing to talk if Likud changes course.

actors.why: Political deadlock delays a new government and risks another costly election

impact_points: Israel faces a prolonged political deadlock, with Netanyahu's government remaining in caretaker status if no coalition forms.
Netanyahu's Likud faces pressure from its rivals, who accuse it of delaying talks and risking another election.

auto-e3d516ece6ad.headline: Gunmen kill 13 Niger National Guard members in western village attack
auto-e3d516ece6ad.summary: Thirteen members of Niger's National Guard were killed and about 20 wounded in an early-morning attack on their post in Sanam, in the western Tillaberi region near the Mali border. The defence ministry, which called it a terrorist attack by a large, heavily armed group, said several attackers were killed and their logistics destroyed. Islamic State later claimed responsibility on its Telegram channel, though the ministry had not named any group. The killings follow an 11-soldier attack in the southeast's Diffa region earlier that week, and come as the military junta, in power since a 2023 coup, faces jihadist violence and internal strain after a failed mutiny in August.

Neighbouring Nigeria faces jihadist threats and cross-border armed group activity

Mali and Burkina Faso share the tri-border zone where jihadist violence in Tillaberi continues to spread.

auto-32490af753ac.headline: Israeli drone strike kills one man and wounds several in northern Gaza
auto-32490af753ac.summary:
An Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the Bir al-Naaja area, west of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, on Friday evening, killing a Palestinian man identified as Khaled Assaf, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, citing witnesses. Several others were wounded, some seriously. Separately, a child was wounded by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis in the south.

The Palestinian health ministry said Israeli attacks killed at least 19 people and wounded 48 over the previous 48 hours. Officials say 1,705 Palestinians have been killed since the October ceasefire began, though the strikes have continued.

Strikes continue under the ceasefire, drawing international scrutiny over operations

Israel faces renewed scrutiny over strikes that continue during the truce, while the Gaza health system and displaced residents bear the costs.

auto-d2a5d3dd9f4f.headline: Canada's top court backs Quebec ban on religious symbols for public workers
auto-d2a5d3dd9f4f.summary:
Canada's Supreme Court has upheld Quebec's 2019 Bill 21, which bars public sector employees such as teachers and police officers from wearing religious symbols on the job. The court found the law rooted in the province's commitment to state secularism, though it ruled that one provision infringing the rights of National Assembly members who wear face coverings for religious reasons was invalid. Rights groups condemned the decision, arguing it disproportionately affects Muslim women and weakens constitutional protections, while Quebec's governing party called it a victory.

The ruling relies on the notwithstanding clause, which lets provinces shield legislation from certain Charter rights. Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government respects the court's independence, is reviewing the decision, and will not use the clause to override fundamental rights.

actors.why: Top court upholds provincial law, raising minority rights and unity concerns nationally
Canada's internal unity debate unfolds amid trade war and US annexation threats

impact_points: Quebec's Muslim women, who wear the hijab, face continued barriers to public sector jobs and services.
Canada's federal government faces pressure over minority rights while managing national unity amid tensions with the United States.

auto-80728c0d9520.headline: Israeli raids and settler attacks injure and detain Palestinians across the West Bank
auto-80728c0d9520.summary:
Israeli forces and settlers carried out raids and attacks across the occupied West Bank, leaving at least three Palestinians injured and several detained, according to local officials and the Wafa news agency. In one case, soldiers raided a home north of Jerusalem and beat occupants, and a man was detained. Elsewhere, troops fired tear gas in Beit Ummar, and seven people were detained in Jayyus.

Separately, Israeli settlers demolished the foundations of two homes belonging to the Tubasi family in Jaloud, near Nablus, after attacks had stopped the family returning despite a court order. The Israeli military called it a serious criminal act and said it was investigating. UN figures show an average of 53 settler attacks a week this year.

actors.why: Residents injured, detained and losing homes in raids and settler attacks
Military and settlers face criticism over raids and weak enforcement

impact_points: Palestinian families in the West Bank face beatings, detentions and loss of homes during raids and settler attacks.
Israel faces criticism over weak enforcement, as most settler violence investigations close without charges.

auto-9be7fd327727.headline: US Army destroys lead azide stockpile in Iowa; early checks show no toxic spread
auto-9be7fd327727.summary: The US Army detonated its entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used in explosives, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday. Earthen barriers and foam and water on two bunkers appear to have absorbed much of the blast, and EPA air monitors detected no airborne lead, prompting an all-clear alert. The army said the chemical was degrading and could explode unpredictably in colder weather. Researchers caution that lab tests on samples over days to weeks are needed before communities can be fully cleared.

actors.why: Stockpile destroyed safely per early checks, but public concern and testing continue

impact_points: Residents of Middletown, Burlington and nearby communities face lingering uncertainty until lab testing of water, farms and homes is complete.
Livestock farmers and families near the Mississippi River depend on the results of planned lead testing for their water and animals.

auto-33d54897f6ea.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies including China, Beijing protests
auto-33d54897f6ea.summary: The United States has proposed additional tariffs on 14 trading partners, China among them, after a Section 301 investigation into alleged "overcapacity" in industries such as steel, electric cars and solar panels. China faces the highest rate, a 20 percent levy, with Washington threatening 40 percent if trade talks fail. Beijing's Commerce Ministry says it firmly opposes the measures, calls them unilateral and against WTO rules, and reserves the right to retaliate. It also urged Washington to implement a $30 billion reciprocal tariff reduction agreed in September.

actors.why: Highest proposed tariff rate and threatened escalation, though Beijing vows retaliation
Seeks renewed leverage over trade after the Supreme Court struck down earlier tariffs
Named among 14 economies facing proposed tariffs over alleged overcapacity
Named among 14 economies facing proposed tariffs over alleged overcapacity

impact_points: China faces the highest proposed rate and possible retaliation, raising pressure on its exporters and trade relations.
The European Union and India are among the other targeted economies facing new tariffs under the same investigation.

auto-cfd36bdff2fa.headline: EU budget summit ends in walkout with no deal reached
auto-cfd36bdff2fa.summary:
An EU summit in Brussels called to break the deadlock over the bloc's seven-year budget ended after midnight without agreement. European Council President António Costa's proposal to cut €204 billion from the Commission's roughly €2 trillion plan angered many leaders. Several frugal states, including Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria, walked out of his small-group talks, saying the format was designed to divide them. Leaders will try again on 17 December, though some have distanced themselves from a year-end deadline.

France's Emmanuel Macron warned that delay into 2027 would be too close to the French election, where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is favoured. A €45 billion loan for Ukraine was also postponed, with Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic still refusing to take part.

actors.why: Budget deadlock and delayed Ukraine loan leave the bloc without a deal
Macron's ultimatum and election-timing pressure weaken his negotiating position
Germany backs deeper cuts and defence spending, a position partly reflected in later talks
€45 billion loan postponed, delaying financial support for Ukraine
Meloni insists on a larger budget and refuses to sign anything unfair to Italy
Spain wants protected farming and regional spending, and its government faces a vote

impact_points: The EU faces a tight timetable, since the new budget must be operational by January 2028 and still needs Parliament's approval.
Ukraine's €45 billion loan has been delayed to December, leaving Kyiv waiting while Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic withhold support.

auto-5dbb9eb7d189.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly spark fire at Russian oil sites in Rostov and Bashkortostan
auto-5dbb9eb7d189.summary:
Telegram monitoring channels reported that Ukrainian drones struck near the Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refinery in Russia's Rostov Oblast overnight on November 28, with a fire likely at fuel storage tanks, according to an OSINT analysis by the ASTRA channel. Kyiv could not immediately verify the reports, and Ukraine's military had not commented. The attack follows a strike on the same refinery on November 23 that reportedly destroyed or damaged dozens of storage tanks.

Separately, a drone crash sparked a fire at the Subkhankulovo oil pipeline control station, a major hub of Transneft's trunk pipeline system, in Bashkortostan. Local officials said no one was hurt and the extent of damage was unknown. Analysts estimate Russian refining volumes have fallen to their lowest level in over twenty years.

actors.why: Refineries and pipeline hubs hit by drones, cutting oil processing and storage
Drone strikes on Russian energy sites pressure Moscow's war funding

impact_points: Russia faces reduced fuel processing and storage, with refining output reportedly near multi-decade lows after repeated strikes.
Ukraine is pressing its campaign against Russian energy sites, aiming to cut Moscow's ability to fund its war.

auto-d6cc0b3403cf.headline: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly breached by hackers
auto-d6cc0b3403cf.summary:
Hackers have reportedly breached Cloud One, the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters, NBC News and Federal News Network. The intrusion was reportedly found during an upgrade of the system, and it has disrupted work across the platform, including paused migrations and blocked software updates. Investigators have brought in the military's Cyber Command, and it is unclear what data, if any, was taken.

The Pentagon did not directly confirm or deny the breach, saying its systems are safe and that it does not comment on network status. The reports come amid a run of other recent cyber incidents affecting US government agencies, and the European Commission has also said it faced a cyberattack.

actors.why: Flagship Air Force cloud breached, possibly exposing sensitive military data and disrupting operations

impact_points: The US Air Force and Pentagon face possible exposure of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
Air Force personnel may be unable to apply urgent software fixes while the platform remains disrupted.

auto-43fcdcef4c88.headline: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu's Likud of stalling Israeli coalition talks
auto-43fcdcef4c88.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, is trying to form Israel's next government after the October election left neither bloc with a majority. He accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party of stalling talks over a possible unity government, saying Likud refused to table a concrete proposal over two weeks. Likud said it remained open to a unity government while accusing Eisenkot of seeking a left-wing coalition. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

Yashar has agreed coalition deals with the Democrats and Israel Beiteinu, which together with Yashar hold 36 seats, short of the 61 needed. Eisenkot's camp remains divided over ties with ultra-Orthodox parties, Arab-majority lists, and Likud.

actors.why: Political deadlock over forming a government, with stalled talks and a looming deadline

impact_points: Netanyahu and Likud face being pushed out of power if Eisenkot's coalition succeeds.
Israel's political system risks another election if talks collapse under the current caretaker government.

auto-65e7ccb02fef.headline: Iran's Guards say tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
auto-65e7ccb02fef.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps said several oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, near Oman's Khasab port. The Guards said the vessels were using unauthorised routes and had switched off tracking systems. One reported tanker was a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of crude and was left burning. The claims could not be independently verified.

The incidents come amid a US naval blockade of Iran. US Central Command separately said American aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored warnings to halt, and President Trump said no Iranian ship had passed the blockade.

actors.why: Guards assert control of strait, but US blockade pressures Iran's shipping
Mines near Khasab port threaten Omani waters and shipping
Blockade enforcement continues, though strikes on vessels draw scrutiny

impact_points: Iran faces ongoing pressure as the Guards assert control over the strait's shipping lanes.
Oman and the global oil trade face risk from mines and disrupted tanker traffic through Hormuz.

auto-da1f9e60210b.headline: Iranian strikes keep Gulf security under strain as Bahrain base stays thin
auto-da1f9e60210b.summary:
A US naval base in Bahrain is still running with a small fraction of its pre-war staff after Iranian drone and missile strikes, according to a Washington Post report. The base was among the hardest hit US facilities, and nearby neighbourhoods, schools and businesses have largely emptied; damage is estimated at over $400 million. Separately, two Italian technicians working for Germany's Rheinmetall died in Kuwait after a drone strike that Italy and Kuwait blame on Iran. Tehran denies responsibility and calls the incident suspicious.

Italy's prime minister and the European Commission president condemned the Kuwait attack, with the EU calling for more pressure on Iran. Iran's attacks on Gulf states have continued despite US-Iran negotiations.

actors.why: Two Italian nationals killed in Kuwait strike blamed on Iran
Accused of the Kuwait drone attack and faces growing international pressure
Repeated Iranian strikes damaged base, energy sites and residential areas
Drone attacks on a vital site and an airbase hosting US forces
Naval base in Bahrain heavily damaged and still operating at low staffing
Calls for more pressure on Iran and stresses Gulf security as shared concern

impact_points: Italy faces the loss of two nationals and a diplomatic dispute with Tehran over the Kuwait strike.
Bahrain and the US face a long-term reduction in military capacity and disrupted civilian life around the base.

auto-312a8b6308fc.headline: Drone swarm over RAF Lakenheath prompts US counter-drone response, Iran suspected
auto-312a8b6308fc.summary: The US military reportedly used counter-drone technology to repel around six drones that swarmed RAF Lakenheath, a British base used by the US Air Force, earlier in November. The Financial Times reported the drones were not recovered by British or American personnel and that Iran was suspected of links to the incident. The UK Ministry of Defence said police and US security forces responded on 13 November, the situation was quickly resolved, and normal security was restored. The White House and Pentagon did not immediately comment, and Tehran has denied involvement in similar incidents in Britain.

actors.why: Base hosting US forces was targeted; security response quickly restored normal operations
US forces repelled drones at a base, though no personnel or aircraft were harmed
Suspected of links to the drone swarm, which Tehran has rejected, drawing scrutiny

impact_points: The UK and the US face a suspected Iran-linked security threat on a shared air base.
Iran is under suspicion of hostile activity in Britain, though it rejects involvement in the incidents.

auto-7c086c69dd8d.headline: Russian strikes kill 10 and injure 55 across Ukraine in one day
auto-7c086c69dd8d.summary:
Russian attacks killed 10 people and wounded 55 across Ukraine over a single day, local authorities said. The deadliest incident was a strike on businesses in Nizhyn, Chernihiv Oblast, which killed seven and injured seven others on November 27. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 162 drones overnight on November 28, with most intercepted. Separately, Ukraine's president warned of a new mass strike being prepared, while Russia said it had struck drone-related sites in Kyiv.

The violence came amid wider escalation. Ukraine says its drones hit a Russian refinery and military airfield, and naval drones struck Russian vessels off Libya and in the Baltic. Power outages affected several Ukrainian regions after Russian attacks. US President Donald Trump said he had pressed Putin to scale back military action.

actors.why: Civilians killed and injured, businesses and power grid damaged by Russian strikes
Refinery, airfield and vessels hit by Ukrainian drones and naval attacks
Trump pressing Putin on de-escalation and a possible Russia-Ukraine deal
Pausing some military cooperation with Russia amid diplomatic tensions
Ukrainian naval drones struck a Russian corvette at Benghazi port
Suspected Ukrainian drone struck a Russia-bound cargo ship near Finland

impact_points: Ukraine faces ongoing civilian casualties and damage to businesses, homes, schools and power infrastructure from Russian strikes.
Russia faces Ukrainian drone and naval attacks on refineries, airfields and vessels, which Moscow's Kremlin called a very dangerous trend.

auto-c64c8ada693e.headline: Russian strikes hit Ukrainian energy and rail sites as Kyiv warns of bigger attack
auto-c64c8ada693e.summary:
Russian forces struck energy and rail facilities in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr and Kirovohrad oblasts overnight on 26-27 November, according to regional officials, with two people reported injured. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said intelligence showed Russia was preparing a new mass strike on energy and logistics infrastructure in the coming days. Ukraine has also reported ongoing repairs after earlier outages, and says it faces a shortage of air defence interceptors ahead of winter.

Kyiv said it would retaliate, while Ukrainian forces reported drone strikes on Russian oil and military sites. Russian officials did not respond in these reports, and the Ukrainian and Russian claims could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Energy and rail facilities hit, injuries reported, and a new mass strike is feared
Ukrainian drone strikes reported on refinery and airfield, though unverified
European air defence and aid are increasingly critical to Ukraine's winter defence

impact_points: Ukraine faces winter power and rail disruption, with energy repairs ongoing and interceptor shortages reported.
Russia faces Ukrainian retaliatory drone strikes on oil and military sites, which Reuters could not verify.

auto-c8fd1a29f613.headline: Russian drone strikes kill couple in Kharkiv as wider attacks hit Ukraine
auto-c8fd1a29f613.summary:
A married couple, both 38 and working in IT, were killed on 26 November when a Russian Shahed drone hit their 14th-floor flat in Kharkiv, with their cat also killed. Their neighbour said the couple had recently finished renovating and had been living there in recent years. The same day, Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv, injuring seven people, and Kyiv Oblast, Kherson and other regions reported further deaths. Ukraine's Air Force reported Russia launched drones and missiles overnight, and Russia said its forces hit military-industrial sites in Kyiv.

Separately, Moscow-installed officials said a Ukrainian drone attack in occupied Zaporizhia killed five people, and Ukraine said it struck a major Russian military base east of Moscow. Trump and NATO chief Rutte urged Russia not to expand the war, but fighting has continued.

actors.why: Civilians killed and injured by missile and drone strikes; energy grid hit
Ukrainian drones hit a military base and occupied Zaporizhia; losses reported
Trump and Rutte urged restraint, but Russia's war continues unresolved

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued deadly Russian strikes on cities, homes and energy infrastructure, with energy capacity reported below 40 percent of pre-war levels.
Russia faces Ukrainian drone strikes on its territory and occupied Zaporizhia, while Moscow's military claims strike on Ukrainian industry continue.

auto-0dadbf870187.headline: Kyiv Oblast faces emergency power cuts after Russian strikes and grid overload
auto-0dadbf870187.summary: Authorities in Kyiv Oblast have introduced emergency electricity cuts after damage from Russian attacks and overloaded equipment, according to Ukraine's state grid operator Ukrenergo. Repair crews have started work, and the region will return to scheduled outages once the system allows. Separately, reporting indicates Ukraine halted electricity exports on November 22 after a Russian strike on its transmission network, while imports surged to their highest daily level since mid-June. Analysts at the Center for Economic Strategy say Russia has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on Ukraine's energy sector since September.

actors.why: Grid damage forces outages, lost export income and rising import reliance
Attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure continue to pressure the grid

impact_points: Ukraine's households and businesses in Kyiv Oblast face renewed power outages while repairs continue.
Ukrainian electricity producers lose export revenue and the country relies more heavily on imports to meet demand.

auto-b94f2289ab99.headline: Pakistan's first orbiting astronaut joins Chinese space station, speaks with leaders
auto-b94f2289ab99.summary:
Pakistani astronaut Zeeshan Ali, a 40-year-old pilot, became the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station. On Saturday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir spoke with him by call from Suparco's headquarters in Islamabad, with China's ambassador present. Ali, a payload specialist, will stay aboard for about 5 to 10 days and is carrying Pakistani experiments, including microalgae cultivation and quinoa seed studies.

Leaders praised the mission as a milestone for Pakistan's space ambitions and its strategic partnership with China. The mission was launched from China's Jiuquan centre and is part of a 2025 cooperation agreement between Suparco and China's space agency.

actors.why: Gains prestige and space programme momentum from first orbiting astronaut
Expands space diplomacy by hosting foreign astronaut on Tiangong

impact_points: Pakistan gains prestige and momentum for its space programme through its first orbiting astronaut and onboard experiments.
China strengthens its space diplomacy by hosting a foreign astronaut and expanding ties with Pakistan.

auto-81ead2aa8a7f.headline: Kurds protest as Baghdad moves to take over oilfields and borders
auto-81ead2aa8a7f.summary:
Thousands of Kurds protested in Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region on Thursday against Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's push to seize oilfields held by Kurdish security forces and station federal troops on the region's international borders. Iraq's highest court ruled Wednesday that Baghdad may deploy federal forces along all international borders, including in Kurdistan. The Kurdistan Regional Government rejected what it called military language and threats, though it said it would work with federal authorities against corruption and oil smuggling.

The moves follow a separate standoff in which Zaidi ordered the army to prepare to enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, where Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah is accused of smuggling; the group agreed to let soldiers in. Analysts warn that enforcing these measures against entrenched interests may prove difficult.

actors.why: Baghdad asserts central control but risks confrontation with Kurds and militias
Iran-aligned militia pressured over smuggling and its influence in Iraq weakens
Washington has praised Zaidi's moves against oil smuggling

impact_points: Iraq's Kurdistan region faces losing control of oilfields and borders to federal authority.
Iran-aligned militias such as Kataib Hezbollah face pressure from Baghdad's anti-smuggling campaign.

auto-73926897323b.headline: Israel's coalition talks stall as Eisenkot seeks majority
auto-73926897323b.summary:
Israel's government formation remains uncertain after October elections produced no majority bloc. Centrist Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot has been holding talks with Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud on a possible unity government, but the latest round ended without a deal and a follow-up meeting was announced. Eisenkot has until December 6, extendable by 14 days, to assemble 61 seats. He has signed coalition pacts with Yisrael Beiteinu and the left-leaning Democrats, giving him 36 seats, still well short of a majority.

Eisenkot accused Likud of stalling and refusing concrete proposals, while Likud has floated a rotation deal for the premiership. Divisions persist over whether to partner with ultra-Orthodox parties or the Arab-led parties, which won a record 19 seats.

actors.why: Government formation deadlock and possible new elections destabilise the country's politics

impact_points: Israel faces prolonged political uncertainty, with a possible return to elections if no coalition is formed.
Palestinian citizens of Israel, represented by Arab-led parties, are sidelined despite their record 19 seats.

auto-3417b4fc837e.headline: Tribunal rejects Argentina's bid to halt Falklands oil project
auto-3417b4fc837e.summary:
An international tribunal in Hamburg has declined Argentina's request to halt the Sea Lion oil project near the Falkland Islands. Judges voted 18 to 3 against Argentina's challenge, ruling that they lacked jurisdiction because they cannot decide questions of sovereignty over the islands. Argentina had sought a temporary order stopping drilling while its wider sovereignty claim went to arbitration.

The Sea Lion field, about 1.7 billion barrels, is being developed by Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum, with production planned for around 2028. The UK government said an order would have had serious consequences for islanders' right to develop their resources. Argentina's president Javier Milei has called the project illegal and imposed sanctions on firms involved.

actors.why: Legal bid to halt drilling rejected; sanctions pursued against firms involved
Tribunal rejected Argentina's request, backing UK-linked Sea Lion development
Israeli partner Navitas Petroleum can proceed with the joint venture

impact_points: Argentina is set back in its bid to contest the Sea Lion project, though it may still pursue arbitration.
The Falkland Islands and the UK gain a clear legal path to develop oil that could transform the territory's economy.

auto-9a10acc5943a.headline: Israeli strike in Gaza City fails to kill Hamas leader's son
auto-9a10acc5943a.summary:
An Israeli air strike on a Gaza City residence hit the family of Izzeldeen al-Hayya, the last surviving son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya, but he and his family survived, Hamas said. Several relatives were reportedly wounded, including his daughter-in-law, though no deaths were reported. Hamas called the attack an attempt to assassinate him, linking it to threats from Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz, and said it undermined the October 2025 ceasefire.

The same day, other Israeli attacks in Gaza killed several Palestinians, according to local officials. Israel's military separately alleged that Hamas used part of Al-Ahli Baptist Hospital as an interrogation centre; Hamas rejected the claim and the hospital's diocese said it knew of no such site.

actors.why: Gaza families struck and killed in ongoing attacks despite the ceasefire
Accused by Hamas of violating the ceasefire; alleges hospital militant activity, facing criticism

impact_points: Hamas is affected as its leadership family is targeted, and it accuses Israel of undermining the ceasefire.
Palestinians in Gaza face continued strikes, with Gaza's Health Ministry reporting over 1,700 killed since the ceasefire took effect.

auto-965e1e54e68a.headline: EU summit ends without budget deal as states clash over spending and Ukraine aid
auto-965e1e54e68a.summary:
EU leaders held a special summit in Brussels aimed at breaking a deadlock over the bloc's 2028 to 2034 budget, which is about 1.78 trillion euros in the compromise put forward by European Council President António Costa. Talks ended after midnight with no agreement, and a planned follow-up was set for 17 December. Frugal states including Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden want deeper cuts and more money for defence, while cohesion states want to protect spending on poorer regions and farming.

The summit also failed to settle a proposed loan of about 45 billion euros for Ukraine, which Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic oppose. Unanimity is required, and the deadline is pressured by national elections in several member states next year.

actors.why: Support package and loan remain stalled, leaving Kyiv's finances under strain
Chancellor Merz pushes for fiscal restraint and conditions on Ukraine aid
Opposes Ukraine military funding, keeping leverage in the talks
Macron's ultimatum on talks after year-end pressures rivals, though no deal reached
Meloni says a deal is far off and rejects paying more to receive less
Stalled EU aid to Ukraine serves Moscow's interests while Kyiv's finances weaken

impact_points: Ukraine faces delayed funding, with a loan and seven-year budget support still unresolved and pushed toward December.
Member states including France face a tight timetable, as elections next year could make the budget negotiations harder.

auto-43b41be76341.headline: Israel debates unilateral strike on Iran while raising military readiness with US
auto-43b41be76341.summary:
Israeli military readiness has risen amid concern that Iran could mount a surprise attack on Israel or US forces in the region. The IDF is coordinating closely with US Central Command, holding frequent calls and reinforcing command centres around the clock, with the Air Force under particular strain.

Inside Israel, reports say Mossad chief Roman Gofman favours a unilateral strike on Iran even without US participation, citing a suspected Iranian chemical weapons programme. Military chief Eyal Zamir backs eventual action but prefers waiting for US President Donald Trump and acting alongside Washington. The reporting says the US has not decided whether to strike, and that a window of about six weeks until the new Congress convenes was discussed; these accounts could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Military on high alert; internal split over whether to strike Iran alone
Faces possible preemptive Israeli or US strike over alleged chemical weapons programme
Pressed by Israel for strikes; US forces in region at risk of retaliation

impact_points: Israel faces a choice between acting alone against Iran or waiting to strike jointly with the United States.
Iran and US forces in the region face heightened risk of escalation if a surprise or preemptive strike occurs.

auto-549509069225.headline: Israel says two slain aid workers in Gaza were Hamas members
auto-549509069225.summary: The Israeli military says two Doctors Without Borders (MSF) workers killed in an air strike on a clinic in Gaza City were members of Hamas. It named one as an artillery unit commander in Hamas's armed wing but provided no evidence for the claim, which could not be independently verified. The military also denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure, saying precautions were taken to limit civilian harm. Separately, reports say several Israeli strikes and a shooting across Gaza killed around 10 Palestinians, and Hamas is weighing a response.

actors.why: Gaza civilians and medical staff killed in strikes, ceasefire under strain
Military defends the strike and faces claims about medical targeting
MSF, a Belgium-linked aid group, loses two staff and faces contested claims

impact_points: Doctors Without Borders faces scrutiny after two of its staff were killed at a Gaza clinic.
Hamas is weighing a response after Israeli strikes killed senior officials and other Palestinians.
